17:1: Abu Ja`far Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: God Almighty means by His saying, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night, to sanctify the One who took His servant by night and to exonerate Him from what the polytheists say about Him, that He has a partner among His creation, and that He has a wife and a son, and that He is superior and glorified over what they have attributed to Him and attributed to Him out of their ignorance and the error of their statements. I have previously explained that His saying Glory be to Him is a noun that was used in place of a verbal noun, so it was put in the accusative case because it is not described, and the Arabs have places in glorification in which they use it. Among them is prayer, many of the people of interpretation interpreted the saying of God Had he not been among those who glorify God as Had he not been among those who pray. Among them is exception, some of them interpreted the saying of God the Most High: Did I not tell you why you glorify God? as Why did you not make an exception? He claimed that this was the language of some of the people of Yemen, and he supported the correctness of his interpretation with His saying: When they swore that they would harvest it in the morning, and they made no exception. He said: The most prominent of them said, ‘Did I not tell you why you glorify God?’ So he mentioned their leaving out the exception. Among them is light, some of them interpreted in the report that was narrated “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Had it not been for that, the glory of His face would have burned up everything I perceived,” that he meant by His saying the glory of His face: the light of His face. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night, the people of interpretation said that it was mentioned by whoever said that. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Muhab, on the authority of Musa bin Talha, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he was asked about glorifying God, that a person should say: Glory be to God. He said: God has kept him free from evil.” Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abda bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Glory be to God. He said: It is a turning away from God. We have mentioned from the narrations on that which is sufficient in what has passed in this book of ours before. The Isra and the Night Journey are the night journeys. So whoever says: Night Journey, says Night Journey, and whoever says Night Journey, says: Night Journey, as the poet said: And one dark night I walked, and he did not turn me away from its secret. I wish It is narrated: A dewy day. He means by his saying at night from the night. And Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman used to recite it in the same way. Abu Kuraib told us: I heard Abu Bakr bin Ayyash and a man narrating to him a hadith about when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey. He said to him: Do not bring someone like Asim or Zar. He said: Hudhayfah recited: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque. And Abdullah recited the same. As for his saying, from the Sacred Mosque, there is a difference of opinion about it and its meaning. Some of them said: He means from the Sanctuary. He said: The entire Sanctuary is a mosque. We have explained that in more than one place in this book of ours. He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sleeping in the house of Umm Hani’, the daughter of Abu Talib, on the night he was taken on the Night Journey to the Al-Aqsa Mosque. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us: Muhammad ibn al-Sa’ib told us on the authority of Abu Salih ibn Bazan on the authority of Umm Hani’ bint Abi Talib, on the Prophet’s Night Journey, may God bless him and grant him peace, that she used to say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was not taken on the Night Journey except that he was in my house sleeping with me that night. He prayed the last evening prayer, then slept and we slept. When it was just before dawn, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, woke us up. When he prayed the morning prayer and we prayed with him, he said: O Umm Hani’, you have prayed. I have the last evening prayer with you, as you saw in this valley. Then I came to Jerusalem and prayed there. Then I prayed the morning prayer with you now, as you see. Others said: Rather, he was taken on a night journey from the mosque, and he was there when he was taken on a night journey. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated: Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn `Adi narrated to us, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of Malik ibn Sa`sa, a man from his people, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While we were at the House, between sleeping and awake, I heard a voice saying one of the three. So I was brought a golden basin containing Zamzam water, and my chest was opened to such and such. Qatada said: I said: What does he mean by that? Qaan: To the bottom of his stomach. He said: So my heart was taken out and washed with Zamzam water, then it was returned to its place, then it was stuffed with faith and wisdom. Then I was brought a white beast, and in another narration: a white beast called Al-Buraq, bigger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, taking a step as far as its eyes could reach. So I was carried on it, then we set off until we came to the Holy House, and I prayed there as an imam with the prophets and messengers, then I was taken up to the lowest heaven... and he mentioned the hadith. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Khalid Ibn Al-Harith told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas Ibn Malik, on the authority of Malik, meaning Ibn Sa’sa’ah, a man from his people, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’a, a man from his people, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated: Amr ibn Abd al-Rahman narrated: al-Hasan ibn Abi al-Hasan narrated: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: While we were sleeping in the Hijr, Gabriel came to me and nudged me with his foot. I sat up but did not see anything, so I returned to my bed. Then he came to me a second time and nudged me with his foot. I sat up but did not see anything, so I returned to my bed. Then he came to me a third time and nudged me with his foot, so I sat down. He took hold of my arm and I stood up with him, then he went out with me to the door of the mosque, and there was a white animal between a donkey and a mule. It had two wings on its thighs with which it nudged its feet, and it put its hand where it reached its farthest point. It carried me on it and then went out with me, neither missing me nor me missing it. Al-Rabi’ bin Sulayman narrated: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, on the authority of Sulayman bin Bilal, on the authority of Sharik bin Abi Namir, who said: I heard Anas narrating to us about the night journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the mosque of the Kaaba, that three men came to him before revelation came to him while he was sleeping in the Sacred Mosque. The first of them said: Which one is he? He said: The middle one is the best of them. One of them said: Take the best of them. That was the night, and he did not see them until they came another night, as his heart sees, and the eyes of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, sleep, but his heart does not. And so it is with the prophets: their eyes sleep, but their hearts do not sleep. They did not speak to him until they carried him and placed him near the well of Zamzam. Gabriel, peace be upon him, took charge of him and cut open the space between his throat and his loin, until he finished with his chest and his stomach. He washed him with the water of Zamzam until his stomach was cleansed. Then he was brought a golden basin in which was a bowl filled with faith and wisdom. He filled his stomach, chest, and jawbone with it, then closed it and mounted Al-Buraq. He traveled until he came to the Holy House and led the prophets and messengers in prayer there. Then he ascended with him to the lowest heaven and knocked on one of its doors. The people of heaven called out to him: Who is this? He said: This is Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Or has he been sent to? He said: Yes, they said: Welcome to him and hello! The people of heaven were delighted with him, for the people of heaven do not know what God intends for the people of the earth until He informs them. So he found Adam in the lowest heaven, and Gabriel said to him: This is your father, so greet him, and he greeted him back and said: Welcome to you and hello to my son, what an excellent son you are! Then he went with him to the second heaven, and Gabriel opened one of its doors. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has a message been sent to him? He said: Yes, a message was sent to him. It was said: Welcome to him! So the gate was opened for them, and when he ascended it, he saw two flowing rivers. He said: What are these? The two rivers, O Gabriel? He said: This is the Nile and the Euphrates, their origin. Then he ascended with him to the third heaven, and Gabriel asked to be opened. A door was opened for him, and he saw a river with domes and palaces of pearls, emeralds, rubies, and other things that only God knows about. He went to smell its dust, and it was the most fragrant musk. He said: O Gabriel, what is this? The river? He said: This is Al-Kawthar which your Lord has hidden for you in the Hereafter. Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, and they said to him the same. Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and they said to him the same. Then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and they said to him the same. Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and they said to him the same. And in each heaven there are prophets whom Anas had named, and I remembered among them Idris in the second, and Aaron in the fourth, and another in the fifth whose name I did not remember, and Abraham in the sixth, and Moses in the seventh with the preference of his speech by God, so Moses said: My Lord, I did not think that anyone would be raised above me, then he ascended with him above that with what none knows except God, until he came to the Lote Tree of the Limit, and approached the door of the Almighty, the Lord of Majesty, so he came down and was two bow lengths or nearer, and revealed to His servant what He willed, and God revealed among what He revealed fifty prayers to His nation every day and night, then he descended until he reached Moses and detained him and said: O Muhammad, what did your Lord enjoin upon you? He said: He entrusted me with fifty prayers for my nation every day and night. He said: Your nation cannot do that, so go back and let it be made easier for you and for them! So he turned to Gabriel as if he was consulting him about that, and he indicated to him yes, so Gabriel took him back until he came to the Almighty, the Majestic, who was where he was, and said: O Lord, make it easier for us, for my nation cannot do that, so He reduced ten prayers from him, then he went back to Moses, peace be upon him, and held him back. Moses kept returning him to his Lord until it became five prayers, then He held him back at the five, and said: O Muhammad, by God, I tempted the Children of Israel to less than these five, but they weakened and abandoned it, so your nation is weaker in body, heart, sight and hearing, so go back and your Lord will make it easier for you! All of this while turning to Gabriel to advise him, and Gabriel did not dislike that, so He raised him to the five, and he said: O Lord, my nation is weak in body, heart, hearing and sight, so make it easier for us! The Almighty said: O Muhammad! He said: At your service and at your pleasure! He said: The word with Me will not be changed as I have written for you in the Mother of the Book. And for every good deed you will have ten like it, and they are fifty in the Mother of the Book, and they are five for you. So he returned to Moses and said: How did you do? He said: Lighten it for me, He gave us for every good deed ten like it. He said: By God, I tried to seduce the Children of Israel for something less than this, but they abandoned it, so go back and let it be lightened for you as well. He said: O Moses, by God, I feel shy before my Lord about what I have gone to. He said: Then go down in the name of God. So he woke up and found himself in the Sacred Mosque. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God the Almighty informed that He took His servant on a night journey from the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred Mosque is the one that people recognize among themselves when they mention it, and His saying to the Farthest Mosque means: the Mosque of Jerusalem, and it was called Al-Aqsa because it is the farthest of the mosques that are visited, and the virtue of visiting it is sought after the Sacred Mosque. So the interpretation of the statement is to glorify God and to acquit Him of what the polytheists attributed to Him of polytheism, rivals, and companions, and what is too great for Him, the Almighty, who took His servant by night from His Sacred House to His Farthest House. Then the scholars differed regarding the description of the Night Journey of God Almighty with His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the Sacred Mosque to the Mosque. Al-Aqsa, some of them said: God took his body on a night journey, and he traveled with it at night on Al-Buraq from his Sacred House to his Al-Aqsa House until he reached it and showed him whatever he wanted to show him of the wonders of his command, his lessons, and the greatness of his power. So the prophets were gathered for him, and he prayed with them there, and he ascended with him to the heavens until he ascended with him above the seven heavens, and he revealed to him there whatever he wanted to reveal, then he returned to the Sacred Mosque that night, and he prayed with him the dawn prayer. He mentioned who said that, and mentioned some of the narrations that were narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with his authentication: Yunus bin Abdul A’la told us: Ibn Wahb told us: Yunus bin Yazid told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: Ibn al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah bin Abdul Rahman told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey. Al-Buraq, which is the mount of Abraham on which he used to visit the Sacred House, its hoof falling where its tip was. He said: A camel from the camels of the Quraysh passed by one of those valleys, and the camel was frightened. Among them was a camel with two jugs on it: black and blue, until the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to Ilya. Two cups were brought to him: a cup of wine and a cup of milk. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the cup of milk, and Gabriel said to him: You have been guided to the natural disposition. If you had taken the cup of wine, your nation would have gone astray. Ibn Shihab said: Ibn al-Musayyab informed me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, met Abraham, Moses, and Jesus there. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described them, and said: As for Moses, he was a man with a striking head as if he were from the men of Shanu’ah. As for Jesus, he was a red man as if he had come out of Dimas. The most similar to those I have seen is Urwah ibn Mas’ud al-Thaqafi. As for Abraham, I am the most similar of his sons to him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned, he told the Quraysh that he had been taken on the Night Journey. Abdullah said: Many people turned away. After they converted to Islam, Abu Salamah said: Abu Bakr Al-Siddiq came and was asked: What do you think of your companion? He claims that he was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem and then returned in one night! Abu Bakr said: Did he say that? They said: Yes, he said: Then bear witness that if he said that, he has spoken the truth. They said: Do you bear witness that he came to Ash-Sham in one night? He said: I believe him beyond that, I believe him with report from heaven. Abu Salamah said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdullah say: I heard the Messenger of God say: When the Quraysh denied me, I stood up and God made Jerusalem appear to me, and I began to tell them about His signs while I was looking at it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yaqub ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Zuhri told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Hashim ibn Utbah ibn Abi Waqqas, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, he said: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, brought al-Buraq to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it was as if she had been struck with her tail, so Gabriel said to her: Be still, O Buraq, for by God, someone like him has ridden you! So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, continued on, and there he saw an old woman far from the road: that is, on the side of the road. Abu Jaafar said: It should be said: distant, but the feminine gender was dropped from it. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: Muhammad has gone on. So he walked as long as God willed him to walk, and then something called him from the road saying: Come, O Muhammad. Gabriel said: Go, O Muhammad. So he walked as long as God willed him to walk. He said: Then a group of people met him, and one of them said: Peace be upon you, O First, and peace be upon you, O Last, and peace be upon you, O Gatherer. Gabriel said to him: Return the greeting, O Muhammad. He said: So he returned the greeting. Then the second met him and said to him the same as the first ones, until he reached the Holy House. He offered him water, milk, and wine. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took the milk, and he said to him: Gabriel: You have hit the mark, O Muhammad. If you had drunk water, you and your nation would have drowned. If you had drunk wine, you and your nation would have gone astray. Then Adam and the prophets after him were sent to him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, led them that night. Then Gabriel said to him: As for the old woman whom you saw on the side of the road, there is nothing left of this world except as much as that old woman’s life remains. As for the one who wanted you to lean towards him, that is the enemy of God, Satan. He wanted you to lean towards him. As for those who greeted you, they were Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. Ali bin Sahl told me: Hajjaj told us: Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah al-Riyahi, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or someone else. Abu Ja`far doubted the words of God, the Almighty and Majestic: “Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.” He said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with Michael, and Gabriel said to Michael: Bring me a basin of Zamzam water so that I may purify his heart and expand his chest. He said: So he split open his stomach and washed it three times, and Michael came to him with three basins of Zamzam water, and expanded his chest, and removed whatever rancor was in it, and filled it with patience, knowledge, faith, certainty, and Islam, and sealed between his shoulders with the seal of prophethood. Then he brought him a horse and carried it with every step of it as far as his gaze and the furthest reaches of his sight. He said: So he walked and walked. Gabriel, peace be upon him, was with him. He came upon a people who sow in one day and harvest in the next. Every time they harvest, it returns to how it was. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, O Gabriel, what is this? He said, “These are the ones who strive in the cause of God. Their good deeds will be multiplied seven hundredfold. Whatever they spend, He will replace it, and He is the Best of providers.” Then he came upon a people whose heads were being smashed against rocks. Every time they were smashed, they returned to how they were. Nothing of that would stop for them. He said, Who are these, O Gabriel? He said, These are the ones whose heads are too heavy to perform the obligatory prayers. Then he came upon a people with patches on their fronts and patches on their backs. They graze as camels and sheep graze, and they eat the thorny thorn, the zaqqum, and the stones and stones of Hell. He said, Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These people do not pay the zakat of their wealth, and God has not wronged them in the least, and God is not unjust to His servants. Then he came upon a people who had before them cooked meat in pots, and other raw, dirty, filthy meat. They began to eat some of the raw meat and leave the good cooked meat. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: This man from your nation, who has a lawful, good wife, so he goes to an evil woman and spends the night with her until morning, and the woman leaves her husband who is lawful and good, and goes to an evil man and spends the night with him until morning. He said: Then he came upon a piece of wood in the road that he would not pass by. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is like people from your nation who sit on the road and cut it off. Then he recited: {And do not sit on every road, threatening and turning away}. Then he came upon a man who had gathered a huge bundle of firewood that he could not carry, and he kept adding more. He said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This man from your nation has people’s trusts that he is not able to fulfill, and he keeps adding more, and he wants to carry them but he is unable to do so. Then he came upon people whose tongues and lips were being cut off with iron scissors, and every time they were cut off, It returned as it was, never stopping them! That is something. He said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the preachers of your nation, the preachers of sedition, they say what they do not do. Then he came to a small hole from which a huge bull came out, and the bull wanted to go back from Where he went out and could not, he said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: This man speaks a great word, then regrets it, and is unable to take it back. Then he came to a valley, and found a pleasant, cool wind, and in it was the scent of musk, and he heard a voice, so he said: O Gabriel, what is this pleasant, cool wind and this scent that is like the scent of musk, and what is this voice? He said: This is the voice of Paradise saying: O Lord, give me what you promised me, for my rooms have increased, and my brocade, and my silk, and my satin, and my incantations, and my pearls and my coral, and my silver and my gold, and my cups, and my plates, and my pitchers, and my fruits, and my palm trees and my pomegranates, and my milk and my wine, so give me what you promised me. He said: For you is every Muslim man and woman, and every believer man and woman, and whoever believes in Me and My messengers, and does righteousness and does not associate anything with Me, and does not take rivals besides Me, and whoever fears Me is safe, and whoever asks Me, I will give him, and whoever lends to Me, I will reward him, and whoever relies on Me will suffice him, for I am God, there is no god but Him. Except that I do not break my promise, and the believers have succeeded, and blessed be God, the best of creators. She said: I am satisfied. Then he came to a valley and heard an unpleasant sound, and he found a foul odor, so he said: What is this odor, O Gabriel, and what is this sound? He said: This is the sound of Hell, saying: O Lord, give me what You promised me, for my chains and shackles have increased, and my blazing and my hellfire, and my affliction and my torment and my punishment have increased, and my bottom has become far and my heat has become intense, so give me what You promised me. He said: For you is every polytheist, male and female, and every disbeliever, male and female, and every wicked man and female, and every tyrant who does not believe in the Day of Judgment. She said: I am satisfied. He said: He walked until he came to the Holy House, then he dismounted and tied his horse to a rock, then he entered and prayed with the angels. When he finished the prayer, they said: O Gabriel, who is this with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, brother and Khalifa, what a good brother and what a good successor, and what a good coming he came, he said: Then the souls of the prophets were taken and they praised their Lord, so Abraham said: Praise be to God who took me as a friend and gave me a great kingdom, and made me a nation obedient to God who follow me, and saved me from the fire, and brought upon me coolness and peace, then Moses praised his Lord and said: Praise be to God who spoke to me directly, and caused the destruction of the people of Pharaoh and the salvation of the Children of Israel at my hands, and made from my nation a people who guide with the truth and do justice with it, then David, peace be upon him, praised his Lord, and said: Praise be to God who made for me a great kingdom and taught me the Psalms, and softened iron for me, and subjected the mountains to glorify God and the birds, and gave me wisdom and the ability to make clear speech, then Solomon praised his Lord, and said: Praise be to God who subjected the winds to me, and subjected the devils to me, they make for me whatever I wish of shrines and statues and basins like basins, and fixed pots, and taught me the language of birds, and gave me from all things in abundance, and subjected to me The soldiers of the devils, mankind and birds, and He preferred me over many of His believing servants, and He gave me a great kingdom such as no one after me will have, and He made my kingdom a good kingdom in which I will not be held accountable. Then Jesus, peace be upon him, praised his Lord, and said: Praise be to God who made me His word and made my likeness like that of Adam, whom He created from dust, then He said to him: Be, and it was. He taught me the Book and wisdom and the Torah and the Gospel, and made me create from clay like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it, and it becomes a bird by God’s permission. He made me heal the blind and the leper, and bring the dead back to life by God’s permission. He raised me and purified me and protected me and my mother from the accursed Satan, so Satan had no way over us. He said: Then Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, praised his Lord, and said: All of you have praised your Lord, and I praise my Lord. He said: Praise be to God who sent me as a mercy to the worlds, and as a bringer of good tidings and a warner to all people, and sent down to me the Criterion in which is clarification of everything, and made my people the best nation brought forth for mankind, and made my nation And He made my nation the first and the last, and expanded my chest for me, and removed my burden from me, and raised my reputation for me, and made in me a conqueror and a seal. Abraham said: This is your excellence, Muhammad - Abu Najr, who is Al-Razi, said: The seal of prophethood, and the conqueror of intercession on the Day of Resurrection - then three buildings were brought to him with their mouths covered, and a vessel from them was brought in which was water, and it was said: Drink, so he drank a little from it, then another vessel was given to him in which was milk, and it was said to him: Drink, so he drank from it until he was satisfied, then another vessel was given to him in which was wine, and it was said to him: Drink, so he said: I do not want it, I have been satisfied, so Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: As for it, it will be forbidden to your nation, and if you drank from it, only a few of your nation would follow you, then he ascended with him to the lowest heaven, and Gabriel opened one of its doors. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life from A brother and a successor, what a good brother and a good successor, and what a good arrival he has come, so he entered and behold a man of perfect creation, nothing was missing from his creation, as is missing from the creation of people, on his right was a door from which a good smell came out, and on his left was a door from which a bad smell came out, if he looked at the door on his right he would laugh and be happy, and if he looked at the door on his left he would cry and be sad, so I said: O Gabriel, who is this old man of perfect creation who nothing was missing from his creation, and what are these two doors? He said: This is your father Adam, and this door on his right is the door of Paradise, if he looked at who of his descendants would enter it he would laugh and be happy, and the door on his left is the door of Hell, if he looked at who of his descendants would enter it he would cry and be sad, then Gabriel, may God bless him and grant him peace, ascended with him to the second heaven and asked to be opened, so it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life from A brother and a successor! What a brother and a successor! What a coming! He came. He said: Then he saw two young men. He said: O Gabriel, who are these two young men? He said: This is Jesus, son of Mary, and John, son of Zakariya, the sons of the maternal aunt. He said: So he ascended with him to the third heaven, and asked for permission. They said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, a brother and a successor! What a brother and a successor! What a coming! He said: So he entered, and saw a man who was superior to all people in beauty, just as the moon on the night of the full moon is superior to all the stars. He said: Who is this, O Gabriel, who was superior to all people in beauty? He said: This is your brother Joseph. Then he ascended with him to the fourth heaven, and asked for permission. It was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, a brother and a successor! What a brother and a successor! The Caliph, what a wonderful coming he has come, he said: So he entered and saw a man, he said: Who is this, O Gabriel? He said: This is Idris, may God raise him to a high place. Then he ascended with him to the fifth heaven, and Gabriel asked to be let in, and they said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, a brother and a Caliph, what a wonderful brother and a Caliph, and what a wonderful coming he has come, then he entered and saw a man sitting and around him were people telling stories to them, he said: Who is this, O Gabriel, and who are these people around him? He said: This is Aaron, beloved by his people, and these are the Children of Israel, then he ascended with him to the sixth heaven, and Gabriel asked to be let in, and it was said to him: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, a brother and a Caliph, what a wonderful brother and a Caliph, and what a wonderful coming he has come, and there he is A man was sitting, so he passed him, and the man cried, so he said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: Moses. He said: Why is he crying? He said: The Children of Israel claim that I am the most honored of the children of Adam in the sight of God, and this man from the children of Adam has succeeded me in this world, and I am in the next. If he were himself, I would not care, but with every prophet is his nation. Then he ascended with him to the seventh heaven, and Gabriel asked for permission, and it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. They said: And who is with you? He said: Muhammad. They said: Has he been sent to? He said: Yes. They said: May God give him life, what a brother and a successor! What a good brother and a good successor, and what a good coming he has come. He said: So he entered and there was a man with disheveled hair sitting at the gate of Paradise on a chair, and with him were sitting people with white faces, like papers, and people with different colors. Those who had different colors got up, entered a river and washed in it, and came out with something of their colors gone, then they entered another river and washed in it, and came out And some of their colors were purified, then they entered another river and washed themselves in it, and they came out and some of their colors were purified, so they became like the colors of their companions, so they came and sat with their companions, and he said: O Gabriel, who is this disheveled one, and who are these whose faces are white, and who are those whose colors are slightly different, and what are these rivers that they entered, and they came and their colors were clear? He said: This is your father Abraham, the first to be disheveled on earth, and as for these whose faces are white: they are people who did not mix their faith with injustice, and as for these whose colors are slightly different, they are people who mixed good deeds with bad ones, so they repented, and God repented to them, and as for the rivers: the first is the mercy of God, the second is the blessing of God, and the third is that their Lord gave them to drink a pure drink. He said: Then he reached the lote tree, and it was said to him: This is the lote tree that everyone will reach except for your nation according to your tradition, and behold, it is a tree from whose root flows rivers of water that do not stagnate, and rivers of milk whose taste does not change, and rivers of delicious wine. For those who drink, and rivers of purified honey. It is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for seventy years without cutting it, and its leaves cover the entire nation. He said: Then the light of the Creator, the Almighty and Majestic, covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they land on the tree. He said: Then He spoke to him and said to him: Ask. He said: I took Abraham as a friend, and gave him a great kingdom, and I spoke to Moses directly, and I gave David a great kingdom, and I softened iron for him, and I subjected the mountains to him, and I gave Solomon a great kingdom, and I subjected the jinn, mankind and devils to him, and I subjected the winds to him and gave him a kingdom such as no one after him will have, and I taught Jesus the Torah and the Gospel, and I made him heal the blind and the leper and bring the dead back to life by God’s permission, and I protected him and his mother from Satan the accursed, so Satan had no way over them. Then his Lord said to him: I have taken you as a beloved and a friend, and it is written in the Torah: Beloved of God, and I have sent you to all people as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And I have expanded your chest for you, and removed your burden, and raised your remembrance, so that I am not mentioned except that I am mentioned with you, and I have made your nation a middle nation, and I have made your nation the first and the last, and I have made it not permissible for your nation to speak until they testify that you are My servant and Messenger, and I have made from your nation people whose hearts are their Gospels, and I have made you the first of the prophets to be created, and the last of them to be sent, and the first of them to be judged, and I have given you seven of the oft-repeated verses, which were not given to any prophet before you, and I have given you al-Kawthar, and I have given you eight shares: Islam, migration, jihad, charity, prayer, fasting Ramadan, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong, and I have made you the opener and the seal, so the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: My Lord has favored me with six things: He has given me the openings of words and their endings, and the comprehensive hadith, and He has sent me to all people as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and He has cast fear into the hearts of My enemies from a distance of a month’s journey, and the spoils of war have been made lawful for me, as they were not made lawful for anyone before me. And He has made the whole earth pure and a place of prostration for me. He said: And He has enjoined upon me fifty prayers. When he returned to Moses, he said: What have you been commanded, O Muhammad? He said: Fifty prayers. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, returned to his Lord and asked Him to lighten it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he returned to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded? He said: Forty. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to lighten it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: So he returned to his Lord and asked Him to lighten it, so He reduced it by ten. Then he returned to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded? He said: I was commanded with thirty, so Moses said to him: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: So he went back to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. He went back to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded with? He said: Twenty. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: So he went back to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by ten. He went back to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded with? He said: Ten. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: So he went back shyly to his Lord and asked Him to reduce it, so He reduced it by five. He went back to Moses and said: How much have you been commanded with? He said: Five. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce it, for your nation is the weakest of nations, and you have encountered hardship from the Children of Israel. He said: I have gone back to my Lord, and I am ashamed, for I will not go back to Him. It was said to him: As you have been patient with yourself for five prayers, they will suffice for you as fifty prayers, for every good deed is rewarded tenfold. He said: So Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was completely pleased, and Moses was the most severe of them towards him when he passed by him, and the best of them towards him when he returned to him. Muhammad ibn Ubayd God told me, he said: Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, he said: Abu Ja`far al-Razi told us, on the authority of al-Rabi` ibn Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah or someone else. Abu Ja`far was not sure, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, regarding his statement, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night. to His statement, Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing. He said: Gabriel came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to the hadith of Ali ibn Sahl, on the authority of Hajjaj, except that he said: Gabriel came with Michael, and he said in it: And there are people grazing as livestock graze, eating the thorny thorn and the zaqqum. And he said in every place, `Ali said, Who are these? Who are these, O Gabriel? And he said in one place, Their tongues will be cut off, their tongues will be cut off. And he also said in one place, `Ali said in it: And what an excellent caliph. He said in mentioning wine, so he said: I do not want it, I have already satisfied my thirst. Gabriel said: You have hit upon the fitrah, O Muhammad, it will be forbidden to your nation. He also said about the Lote Tree of the Limit: This is the Lote Tree of the Limit, to it everyone from your nation will end except for you. He also said about the leaf from it that shades all of creation, and the angels cover it like crows when they land on the tree, out of love for God Almighty. The rest of the hadith is like the hadith of Ali. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Harun al-Abdi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri - and al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Abu Harun al-Abdi told us, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri, and the wording is from the hadith of al-Hasan ibn Yahya, in his saying: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque. He said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, narrated to us about the night he was taken on the Night Journey. The Prophet of God said: I was brought a beast that was most similar to a mule, with two twitching ears, and it was Buraq, which was the one that the prophets before me used to ride. I rode it, and it took me off, placing its hand as far as its sight could reach. Then I heard a call to my right: O Muhammad, take it easy, I ask You. So I went on and did not stop at it. Then I heard a call to my left: O Muhammad, take it easy, I ask You. So I went on and did not stop at it. Then I met a woman on the road, and I saw her wearing every adornment of this world, raising her hand, saying: O Muhammad, take it easy, I ask You. So I went on and did not stop at it. Then I came to the Holy House - or he said the Farthest Mosque - and I got off the beast and tied it to the ring that the prophets used to tie it to. Then I entered the mosque and prayed in it. Gabriel said to me: What did you see on your face? I said: I heard a call to my right, ‘O Muhammad, take it easy, I ask You. ’ So I went and did not go up to him. He said: ‘That is the caller of the Jews. If you had stopped at him, your nation would have become Jewish. ’ He said: Then I heard a call to my left, ‘O Muhammad, take it easy, I ask You. ’ So I went and did not go up to him. He said: ‘That is the caller of the Christians. If you had stopped at him, your nation would have become Christians. ’ I said: Then a woman met me, wearing every adornment of the world, raising her hand and saying, ‘Take it easy, I ask You. ’ So I went and did not go up to her. He said: ‘That is the world adorned for you. If you had stopped at him, your nation would have become Christian. ’ The best thing I have seen is, have you not seen how the dead person narrows his gaze towards him? Then he ascended with us in it until we reached the door of the lowest heaven. Gabriel asked to be opened, and it was said: Who is this? He said: Gabriel. It was said: Who is with you? He said: Muhammad. It was said: Has he been sent for? He said: Yes. So they opened and greeted me, and behold, an angel was assigned to guard the heaven, and he was called Ismail, and with him were seventy thousand angels, with each angel of them a hundred thousand. Then he recited: And none knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. And behold, I saw a man as he was on the day God created him, nothing of him had changed. Then behold, the souls of his descendants were presented to him. If it was the soul of a believer, he would say: A good soul and a good fragrance, place his book in the highest place. But if it was the soul of an unbeliever, he would say: A bad soul and a bad fragrance, place his book in Sijjil. So I said: O Gabriel, who is this? He said: Your father is Adam, so he greeted me and welcomed me and prayed for my well-being and said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son. Then I looked and saw people with lips like the lips of camels, and someone was assigned to them to take hold of their lips, then he put in their mouths rocks of fire coming out of their bottoms. I said: O Gabriel, who are these? He said: These are those who eat the property of orphans unjustly. Then I looked and saw people whose skins are being put into their mouths, then it is said: Eat as you have eaten, and I hate what God created for them. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the slanderers and backbiters who eat the flesh of people and slander them for no reason. Then I looked and saw people at a table on which was grilled meat, the best meat I have ever seen, and around them were carcasses, so they began to lean over the carcasses and eat from them and leave that meat. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These adulterers have deliberately committed what God has forbidden them and abandoned what God has permitted them. Then I looked and saw people with bellies like houses, and they were on the path of the people of Pharaoh. When the people of Pharaoh passed by them, they would rise up, and one of them would lean his stomach and fall, and the people of Pharaoh would trample them with their feet, and they would be exposed to the Fire morning and evening. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: These are the ones who consume usury, usury in their bellies, so their example is like that of one who is overcome by Satan due to possession. Then I looked and saw women hanging by their breasts and women with their legs upside down. I said: Who are these, O Gabriel? He said: They are the ones who commit adultery and kill their children. He said: Then we ascended to the second heaven, and saw Joseph surrounded by followers of his nation, and his face was like the moon on a full moon night. He greeted me and welcomed me. Then we proceeded to the third heaven, and saw my maternal cousins, John and Jesus. One of them resembled the other, their clothes and hair, so they greeted me and welcomed me, then we went to the fourth heaven, and there I was with Idris, so he greeted me and welcomed me, and God said, And We raised him to a high station. Then we went to the fifth heaven, and there I was with Aaron, beloved by his people, and around him were many followers of his nation, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him: Long beard, his beard almost touching his navel, so he greeted me and welcomed me, then we went to the sixth heaven, and there I was with Moses, son of Imran, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, described him and said: Much hair, if he had two shirts on, his hair would come out of them, Moses said: People claim that I am the most honored of creation to God, so this one is more honored to God than me, and if he were alone I would not care, but every prophet and those who followed him from his nation, then we went to the seventh heaven, and there I was with Abraham sitting with his back leaning against the Frequented House, so he greeted me and said: Welcome to the righteous prophet and righteous son, so it was said: This is your place and the place of your nation, then he recited: The people who are most worthy of Abraham are those who are most worthy of him. For those who followed him, and this Prophet and those who believed, and God is the protector of the believers. Then I entered the Frequented House and prayed in it, and behold, seventy thousand angels enter it every day who do not return until the Day of Resurrection. Then I looked and behold, I saw a tree, if a leaf of it were to cover this nation, and behold, at its root was a flowing spring that had branched into two branches. I said: What is this, O Gabriel? He said: I stood there and your nation chose this world over the Hereafter. Then I was brought two vessels, one of which contained milk and the other contained wine. It was said to me: Drink whichever one you want. So I took the milk and drank it. He said: You have chosen the fitrah - or he said: You have taken the fitrah. Muammar said: Al-Zuhri informed me, on the authority of Ibn Al-Musayyab, that it was said to him: If you had taken wine, your nation would have gone astray. Abu Harun said in the hadith of Abu Saeed: Then the Mi’raj was brought, in which the souls of the children of Adam ascend, and behold, it is this: it is the River of Mercy, and this: it is Al-Kawthar which God has given you, so I washed myself in the River of Mercy, and He forgave me for what I had done. I have forgiven my sins and what I have delayed. Then I took Al-Kawthar until I entered Paradise, and there was in it what no eye has seen and no ear has ever heard. I heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of man, and if in it are pomegranates like the skins of camels, and if in it are birds like the camels, Abu Bakr said: That bird is soft. He said: I ate it softer than that, O Abu Bakr, and I hope that you will eat from it. I saw a girl among them, so I asked her: Who do you belong to? She said: Zaid bin Haritha. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Zaid the good report of her. He said: Then God commanded me with His command, and imposed upon me fifty prayers. I passed by Moses, and he said: What did your Lord command you? I said: He has imposed fifty prayers upon me. He said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce them, for your nation will not do this. So I went back to my Lord and asked Him, and He reduced ten for me. Then I went back to Moses, and I kept going back to my Lord whenever I passed by Moses until He imposed five prayers upon me. Moses said: Go back to your Lord and ask Him to reduce them. I said: I have gone back to my Lord until I felt ashamed - or he said: I said: I will not go back - and it was said to me: For these five prayers you have fifty prayers, a good deed is worth ten like it. Whoever intends to do a good deed but does not do it, a good deed is written for him, and whoever does it, ten are written for him. Whoever intends to do a bad deed but does not do it, nothing is written for him, but if he does it, one is written for him. Narrated Ibn Humayd: He said: Narrated to us Salamah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq: He said: Narrated to us Ruh ibn al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Harun ‘Amara ibn Juwayn al-‘Abdi, on the authority of Abu Sa’id al-Khudri - and narrated to us Ibn Humayd: Narrated to us Salamah, on the authority of Mali - and narrated to us Abu Ja’far, on the authority of Abu Harun, on the authority of Abu Sa’id: I heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: When I finished what was in the Holy House, I was brought the Mi’raj, and I have never seen anything more beautiful than it. It is the one to which your dead extend their eyes when they are present. My companion made me ascend in it until he reached a door of the doors called the Gate of the Guardians, over which was a king called Ismail, under whose hands were twelve thousand angels, under the hands of each of them were twelve thousand angels. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said when he narrated this hadith: None knows the soldiers of your Lord except Him. Then he mentioned something similar to the hadith of Mu’ammar, on the authority of Abu Harun, except that he said in his hadith: Then he entered Paradise with me and I saw a girl in it, so I asked her, To whom do you belong? I was amazed when I saw her. She said: For Zaid bin Haritha. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave Zaid bin Haritha the good report. Then the hadith of Ibn Hamid on the authority of Salamah ended here. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Muammar narrated: Az-Zuhri narrated: Ibn al-Musayyab narrated: Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, described to his companions the night he was taken on the Night Journey Isra, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus. He said: As for Abraham, I have not seen a man more similar to your companion than he. As for Moses, he is a tall, dark-skinned man with curly hair and a hooked nose, as if he were one of the men of Shanu’ah. As for Jesus, he is a red man between short and long, with smooth hair and many bald patches on his face, as if he had just come out of the desert. His head was dripping with water, although there was no water on it. I have never seen anyone more similar to him than Urwah bin Mas’ud. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. He did not say on the authority of Abu Hurairah. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on al-Buraq on the night of the Night Journey, saddled and bridled, so that he could ride it, but he found it difficult, so Gabriel said to him: What makes you do this? By God, no one more honorable to God than him has ever ridden you! He said: Then sweat profusely. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, the Prophet of God was taken on a night journey from Mecca to Jerusalem, and the Prophet of God prayed there, and God showed him some of His signs and commanded him with whatever He willed on the night he was taken on the night journey, then he arrived in Mecca in the morning. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I was carried on a beast called al-Buraq, larger than a donkey and smaller than a mule, placing its hoof where its gaze reached. The Prophet of God told the people of Mecca about that, but the polytheists denied it and rejected it, and said: O Muhammad, you tell us that you came to Jerusalem and returned that night, then you arrived with us in Mecca in the morning? You did not bring it to us, and you did not bring it before today, despite this. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq believed him for that reason. Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us: Abd Al-Wahid Ibn Ziyad told us: Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, on the authority of Abdullah Ibn Shaddad, who said: When the night of the Isra’ of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he was brought a beast called Al-Buraq, smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey, placing its hoof at the end of its nails. When he reached the Holy House, he was brought two vessels: a vessel of milk and a vessel of wine. He drank the milk. Gabriel said to him: You have been guided and your nation has been guided. Others who said that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on a night journey to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, in person and body, said: He was taken on a night journey, peace be upon him, but he did not enter the Holy City, nor did he pray in it, nor did he get off the Buraq until he returned to Mecca. Mention who said that. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan told us: Sufyan told us: Asim bin Bahdalah told us on the authority of Zurbin Habish on the authority of Hudhayfah bin Al-Yaman that he said regarding this verse, Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from Al-Masjid Al-Haram to Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not pray in it, and if he had prayed in it, prayer would have been prescribed for you in it, just as prayer at the Kaaba was prescribed for you. Abu Kuraib narrated: I heard Abu Bakr bin Ayyash, and a man was narrating a hadith in his presence about the Night Journey with the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so he said to him: No one will come like Asim or Zur. Hudhayfah said to Zur bin Hubaish, and Zur was a noble man from the nobles of the Arabs. Hudhayfah recited: “Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Seeing.” And Abdullah recited it in the same way. He said: This is as they say: He entered al-Masjid al-Aqsa and prayed in it, then he entered and tied up his mount. He said: I said: By God, he has entered it. He said: Who are you? I know your face, but I do not know your name. He said: I said: Zur bin Hubaish. He said: What is your work? He said: I said: By the Qur’an. He said: Whoever takes the Qur’an will succeed. He said: So I said: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed. He said: So he looked at me and said: O bald man, do you see its entrance? He said: I said: No, by God. Hudhayfah said: Yes, by God, there is no god but He, he did not enter it. If he had entered it, prayer in it would have been obligatory for you. No, by God, he did not get off al-Buraq until he saw Paradise and Hell, and all that God has prepared in the Hereafter. He said: Do you know what al-Buraq is? He said: An animal smaller than a mule and larger than a donkey, its stride is as far as the eye can see. Others said: Rather, he was taken on a journey in spirit, not in body. Mention who said that. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Yaqub ibn Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhns told me that when Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan was asked about the Night Journey of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would say: It was a true vision from God. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad, who said: Some of the people of Abu Bakr told me that Aisha used to say: The body of the Messenger of God was not lost, but God took his soul on a night journey. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, Ibn Ishaq said: So it was not denied that she said al-Hasan that this verse was revealed: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and because of God’s statement in the report about Ibrahim, when he said to his son, O my son, I see in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think. Then he continued on with that, and I knew that revelation comes to the prophets from God while they are awake and while they are asleep. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, My eyes sleep and my heart is awake. So God knows which of that had come to him and in which he saw of God’s command what he saw in whatever state he was in, whether he was asleep or awake. All of that is true and correct. The correct thing to say about this, according to us, is that God took His servant Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) on a night journey from the Sacred Mosque to the Al-Aqsa Mosque, as God informed His servants, and as the reports from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) have shown us, that God carried him on the Buraq when He brought him to him, and he prayed there with those who prayed from the prophets and messengers, and he showed him the signs that he showed them. There is no meaning to the statement of those who said that he was taken on a night journey with his soul and not his body, because if that were the case, there would be nothing in that that would necessitate that it be evidence of his prophethood, nor would it be an argument for his message, nor would those who denied the truth of that from the polytheists, and they were repelling his truthfulness in it, because it was not objectionable to them, nor to any of the people of sound nature from the sons of Adam, that a dreamer among them would see in a dream something that is a year’s journey away, so how about something that is a month’s journey away or less? And further, God only informed us in His Book that He took His servant on a night journey, and He did not inform us that He took the soul of His servant on a night journey, and it is not permissible for anyone to go beyond what God said to anything else. If someone thinks that this is permissible, since the Arabs used to do this in their speech, as their speaker said: I thought my camel's embrace was a hug, but it is no one but you in the embrace Meaning: I thought the sound of my camel’s tread was an embrace, so he omitted the sound and was satisfied with the embrace, as the Arabs do. This is in what was understood by the speaker’s intent from the speech. As for what has no indication except by its appearance, and does not lead to knowing the intent of the concealer except by its clarification, then it does not delete that, nor does it indicate that what God meant by His saying, He took His servant on a night journey is the soul of His servant on a night journey. Rather, the clear evidence and the successive reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is that God took him on a night journey on a beast called Al-Buraq. If the night journey was with his soul, then the soul would not have been carried on Al-Buraq, since beasts only carry bodies. Unless someone says: The meaning of our saying, He took his soul on a night journey is that he saw in a dream that he was taken on a night journey with his body on Al-Buraq. Then he is lying about the meaning of the reports that were narrated from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that Gabriel carried him on Al-Buraq. Because if this was a dream according to the one who said this, and the soul was not among those who ride beasts, and it was not carried On Buraq was the body of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not say that he was carried on Buraq, neither his body nor anything of it. The matter became, in his view, like some of the dreams of sleepers. This is a rejection of the apparent meaning of the revelation and the successive reports from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was reported by the Imams, the Companions and the Followers. And His statement, whose surroundings We have blessed, the Most High says: the surroundings We have made blessed for its inhabitants in their livelihoods, their sustenance, their crops, and their crops. And His statement, that We may show him some of Our signs, the Most High says: so that We may show Our servant Muhammad some of Our signs, meaning: our lessons, evidence, and arguments. And that is what I mentioned in the reports that I narrated earlier, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown on his way to the Holy House, and after his return to it, some of the wonders of lessons and sermons. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, his statement, To show him some of Our signs is what God showed him of the signs and lessons on the road to Jerusalem. And His saying, Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, God Almighty says: Indeed, He who took His servant by night is the All-Hearing of what these people say. The polytheists of Mecca during the Night Journey of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca to the Holy House in Jerusalem, and for other things they said and others said. He is All-Seeing of what they do of deeds. Nothing of it is hidden from Him, and nothing of it escapes His knowledge. Rather, He encompasses all of it with knowledge, and He counts it by number. He is watching them, to reward all of them for what they are worthy of. Some of the Basrans used to say: I broke the word in from His statement, Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing, because the meaning of the statement is, “Say, O Muhammad: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night,” and say: Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
17:2: God Almighty says: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night and gave Moses the Scripture. The speech returns to and We gave. He began with the phrase took him by night because of what we mentioned before in what came before of the Arabs’ actions in similar cases of beginning the report with report about the absent, then returning to the address and similar things. And what he meant by the book that was given to Moses: the Torah, And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, he says: And We made the book, which is the Torah, an explanation of the truth, and a guide for them on the path of correctness in what He imposed upon them, and commanded them to do, and forbade them from. And His saying, That you do not take besides Me a guardian, the reciters differed in the recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it that you do not take besides Me a guardian, meaning: And We gave Moses the book that you do not take besides Me a guardian. And some of the reciters of Basra recited it that you do not take besides Me a guardian, with the ya’ as a report on the Children of Israel, meaning: And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, that the Children of Israel do not take besides Me a guardian. And they are two readings that are correct in meaning, in agreement and not different, so whichever one the reciter recites, he is correct, but I prefer the recitation with the ta’, because it is more famous in recitation and more widespread among them than the recitation with the ya’. The meaning of the statement: And We gave Moses the Book and made it a guide for the Children of Israel, that you should not take as a guardian other than Me. We have previously explained the meaning of the agent, and Mujahid used to say: Its meaning in this context is: partner. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, That you do not take besides Me a protector, he said, a partner. It is as if Mujahid made the establishment of someone who establishes something other than God in His place a partner from Him to him, and a protector for the one who established him in the place of God. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of this verse, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guide for the Children of Israel, God made it a guide for them, bringing them out of darkness into the light, and made it a mercy for them.
17:3: God Almighty says: Glory be to Him who took His servant by night from the Sacred Mosque to the Farthest Mosque. And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, descendants of those We carried with Noah. And by descendants He meant: all those whom He, the Most High, used this Qur’an as evidence from among the races of nations, Arabs and non-Arabs from the Children of Israel and others, and that is from everyone on the earth from the children of Adam, so they are from the descendants of those whom God carried with Noah in the ship. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, The descendants of those whom We carried with Noah, and all people are descendants of those whom God saved in that ship. And he mentioned to us that no one was saved in it that day except Noah, his three sons, his wife, and three women, and they are: Shem, Jam, and Japheth. As for Shem, he is the father of the Arabs, and as for Ham, he is the father of the Abyssinians, and as for Japheth, he is the father of the Romans. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, The descendants of those whom We carried with Noah, he said: His three sons and their wives, and Noah and his wife. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Mujahid said: His sons, their women, and Noah, but his wife was not. We have explained this in other places in the past, so there is no need to repeat it. His saying, He was a grateful servant, means by the Almighty’s saying: Noah, and the ha is from the mention of Noah, was a grateful servant of God for His blessings. The people of interpretation differed about the reason why God called him Shukur. Some of them said: God called him that because he used to thank God for his food when he ate it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Taymi, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, who said: Whenever Noah put on a garment or ate food, he would praise God, so he was called a grateful servant. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Sinan, on the authority of Saeed ibn Masoud, similarly. Abu Kuraib told us: Abu Bakr told us, on the authority of Abu Hasin, on the authority of Abdullah bin Sinan, on the authority of Saeed bin Masoud, who said: Noah never wore new clothes, nor did he eat food without praising God, and for that reason God said, A grateful servant. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us: Sufyan Al-Thawri told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, on the authority of Salman, who said: Noah was called a grateful servant because when he put on a garment he praised God, and when he ate food he praised God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, The descendants of those We carried with Noah, from the Children of Israel and others. He said: He was a grateful servant. He said: He never renewed a garment without praising God, and he never wore out a garment without praising God. And when he drank a drink, he praised God and said: Praise be to God who gave me this to drink with desire, pleasure and health. And there is no interpretation of it: And when he drank a drink, he said this, but this has reached me. Al-Qasim told me: Al-Husayn told us: Abu Fadala told us, on the authority of Al-Nadr bin Shafi, on the authority of Imran bin Salim, who said: Noah was called a grateful servant because when he ate food he would say: Praise be to God who has made me thirsty, and if He had willed He would have made me hungry. And when he drank he would say: Praise be to God who has given me drink, and if He had willed He would have made me thirsty. And when he put on a garment he would say: Praise be to God who has clothed me, and if He had willed He would have left me alone. And when he put on a sandal he would say: Praise be to God who has given me shoes, and if He had willed He would have covered me. And when he fulfilled a need he would say: Praise be to God who has removed its harm from me, and if He had willed He would have withheld it. Others said about this: Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Abd al-Jabbar ibn Umar told me that Ibn Abi Maryam told him: God called Noah a grateful servant because whenever he defecated, he would say: Praise be to God who made you pure, removed your harm from me, and preserved your benefit. Others said about this: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, God said to Noah, Indeed, he was a grateful servant. He told us that he never bought a new garment without praising God, and he used to command that if a man bought a new garment, he should say: Praise be to God who clothed me with what I can adorn myself with and cover my nakedness with. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He was a grateful servant. He said: Whenever he put on a garment, he would say: Praise be to God, and whenever he wore it out, he would say: Praise be to God.
17:4: We have previously explained that the meaning of qada’ is: to finish something, and then it is used for everything that is finished. The interpretation of the speech in this place: And your Lord directed to the Children of Israel in what He revealed of His Book to Moses, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, by informing them and telling them, You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice. He says: You will disobey God, O group of Children of Israel, and you will disobey His command in his lands twice with Him. And you will be very haughty. He says: And you will be very arrogant towards God by your insolence towards Him, with great arrogance. In a similar manner to what we said about that, he said in A: Is interpretation permissible? Who said that? Hali Thani Yunus said: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding God’s statement, We decreed for the Children of Israel, he said: We informed them. Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We decreed to the Children of Israel, he said: We informed them. Others said: The meaning of this is: We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Mother of the Book, and His knowledge preceded it. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We decreed for the Children of Israel, he said: It is a decree that was decreed for them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We decreed for the Children of Israel, is a decree that He decreed for the people, as you hear. Others said: The meaning of this is: He informed us. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture, he said: The Children of Israel informed us. All these sayings have meanings that go back to what I said about the meaning of his saying, And We decreed, even if what we chose from the interpretation is… It is more likely to be correct, because the readers unanimously read his statement you will surely corrupt with a ta’ and not a ya’, even if the meaning of the statement was: And We decreed for them in the Book. The reading with the letter Ya would have been more appropriate than the letter Ta, but its meaning is that We informed them and informed them. We told them: The letter taa was more appropriate and more appropriate for addressing.
17:5: The corruption of the Children of Israel on earth was the first time: Harun narrated to me, he said: Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi in a report he mentioned on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Malik, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and on the authority of Marra, on the authority of Abdullah: That God promised the Children of Israel in the Torah, You will surely cause corruption on earth twice. The first of the two corruptions was the killing of Zachariah. Then God sent against them the king of the Nabataeans, who was called Sahabin. He sent soldiers, and his bracelets were from the people of Persia, so they were very strong. The Children of Israel fortified themselves, and Bukhtanasr went out among them, an orphan and a poor man. He only went out to seek a livelihood, and he was gentle until he entered the city and came to their gatherings. He heard them say, If our enemy knew what terror he has cast into our hearts because of our sins, they would not have wanted to fight us. So Bukhtanasr went out when he heard that from them, and the uprising against the army intensified, so they returned. This is the saying of God, “But when the first of the two promises came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great strength, and they ravaged the interior of the dwellings. And it was a promise fulfilled.” Then the Children of Israel prepared themselves, and they attacked the Nabataeans, and they killed some of them. And they rescued what was in their hands, so that is what God said: Then We gave you back the upper hand over them and reinforced you with wealth and children and made you more numerous. He says: in number. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Their corruption that they spread on earth was twice: the killing of Zachariah and John the son of Zachariah. God gave power over them to Shapur Dhul-Aktaf, a king from the kings of Persia, who killed Zachariah, and gave power over them to Bukhtanasr, who killed John. Isam bin Rawad bin Al Jarrah narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, he said: Sufyan bin Saeed Al Thawri narrated to us, he said: Mansour bin Al Mu'tamir narrated to us, on the authority of Rabie bin Harash, he said: I heard Hudhayfah bin Al Yaman say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the Children of Israel transgressed and became arrogant, and killed the prophets, God sent against them the king of Persia, Bukhtanasr, and God ruled over him for seven hundred years. He marched against them until he entered Jerusalem, besieged it and conquered it, and killed seventy thousand over the blood of Zachariah. Then he took its people and the children of the prophets as captives, and plundered the jewelry of Jerusalem, and extracted from it seventy thousand and one hundred thousand carts of jewelry until he brought them to Babylon. Hudhayfah said: I said: O Messenger of God, was Jerusalem great in the sight of God? He said: Yes, he built it for Solomon, son of David, from gold, pearls, rubies, and emeralds.
