Its floor was a floor of gold and a floor of silver, and its pillars were gold. God gave him that, and He subjected to him the devils to bring him these things in the blink of an eye. So Nebuchadnezzar went with these things until he reached Babylon. The Children of Israel remained in his hands for a hundred years, tormented by the Magi and the sons of the Magi, among them the prophets and the sons of the prophets. Then God had mercy on them, and He inspired a king of the Persians called Kurus, who was a believer, to go to the remnants of the Children of Israel until they were exhausted. So Kurus went with the Children of Israel and decorated the Temple of Jerusalem until he returned it to him. The Children of Israel remained obedient to God for a hundred years. Then they returned to sinning, so God empowered Abtanychus over them, so he raided with the sons of those who raided with Nebuchadnezzar. He raided the Children of Israel until he reached the Temple of Jerusalem, so he took its people captive, and burned the Temple of Jerusalem, and he said to them: O Children of Israel, if you return to sinning, we will return to you. By captivity, so they returned to sins, so God sent upon them the third captivity, the King of Rome, whose name was Qaqis bin Isbaios, so he invaded them by land and sea, and he took them captive and took captive the ornaments of the House of Jerusalem, and he burned the House of Jerusalem with fire, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: This is from the workmanship of the ornaments of the House of Jerusalem, and the Mahdi will return it to the House of Jerusalem, and it is a thousand and seven hundred ships, and he will dock it in Jaffa until it is transported to the House of Jerusalem, and with it God will gather the first and the last. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us: Among what God revealed to Moses in his account of the Children of Israel, in their account of what they would do after him, was: “And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture: ‘You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach [a state of] great haughtiness.’”... until His saying: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. So the Children of Israel were among the youth and sinners, and God was in that regard forgiving them, compassionate toward them, and kind to them. So among what was revealed to them regarding their sins was what had been presented to them in the account on the tongue of Moses regarding what was revealed to them regarding their sins. The first of those incidents that befell them was that a king among them was called Siddiqah, and whenever God made a king over them, He sent a prophet to guide and support him, and to be between him and God, and to speak to him about their affair. He did not send down books to them, but they were commanded to follow the Torah and the rulings in it, and they forbade them from disobedience, and called them to what they had abandoned of obedience. So when that king became king, God sent with him Isaiah, son of Amaziah, and that was before the mission of Zachariah, John, and Jesus, and Isaiah who was with Jesus and Muhammad. So that king ruled the Children of Israel and the Holy House for a time, and when his reign ended, the events that befell them became great, and Isaiah was with him, God sent upon them Sennacherib, King of Babylon, and with him six hundred thousand banners. So he proceeded until he descended towards the Holy House, and the king was sick with an ulcer in his leg, so the prophet Isaiah came and said to him: O King of the Children of Israel, Sennacherib, King of Babylon, has descended upon you, he and his soldiers with six hundred thousand banners, and The people feared them and were afraid of them, so this was a great burden to the king, so he said: O Prophet of God, has there been a revelation from God regarding what happened, so that you can tell us what God will do to us and to Sennacherib and his soldiers? The Prophet, peace be upon him, said to him: No revelation has come to me concerning you. While they were like that, God inspired the Prophet Isaiah: Go to the king of the Children of Israel and order him to make his will and appoint whomever he wishes from his family to succeed him in his kingdom. So the Prophet Isaiah went to the king of the Children of Israel, Siddiqah, and said to him: Your Lord has inspired me to order you to make your will and appoint whomever you wish from your family to succeed him in your kingdom, for you are going to die. When Isaiah said that to Siddiqah, he turned toward the qiblah, prayed, glorified God, supplicated, and wept. He said while weeping and supplicating to God with a sincere heart, trust, patience, truthfulness, and honest opinion: O God, Lord of lords, God of gods, Holy of the holy, O Most Gracious, Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful, Whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes, remind me of my work and my actions and my good judgments on the Children of Israel. All of that was from You, for You know it better than I do. My secret and my public are Yours, and the Most Gracious has responded to him and he was a righteous servant. So God inspired Isaiah to tell the king Siddiqah that his Lord has responded to him and accepted from him. And he had mercy on him, and he saw his crying, and he delayed his death for fifteen years, and saved him from his enemy Sennacherib, the king of Babylon, and his soldiers. So the prophet Isaiah came to that king and told him about that, and when he said that to him, the pain went away from him, and the evil and sorrow ceased from him, and he fell down in prostration and said: O my God and the God of my fathers, to you I prostrate and glorify and honor and magnify, you are the one who gives the kingdom to whomever you wish, and takes it away from whomever you wish, and honors whomever you wish, and humiliates whomever you wish, you know the unseen and the witnessed, you are the first and the last, the apparent and the hidden, and you have mercy and answer the call of the needy, you are the one who answered my call and had mercy on my supplication. So when he raised his head, God inspired Isaiah to tell the king his friend to order one of his servants to the fig tree, and to bring him fig water and put it on his wound and he will be healed, and in the morning he will be healed, so he did that and he was healed, and the king said to the prophet Isaiah: Ask your Lord to give us knowledge of what he will do to this enemy of ours, he said: So God said To the prophet Isaiah: Say to him: I have saved you from your enemy, and I have delivered you from him, and they will all be dead in the morning except Sennacherib and five of his scribes. So when they woke up, a crier came to them informing them, and he cried out at the gate of the city: O king of the children of Israel, God has saved you from your enemy, so go out, for Sennacherib and those with him have perished. So when the king went out, he looked for Sennacherib, but he was not found among the dead. So the king sent for him, and the pursuers caught up with him in a cave, along with five of his scribes, one of whom was Nebuchadnezzar. They put them in the mosques, then brought them to the king of the Children of Israel. When he saw them, he fell down in prostration from the time the sun rose until the afternoon. Then he said to Sennacherib: What do you think our Lord did to you? Did He not kill you by His power and strength, while we and you were unaware? Then Sennacherib said to him: The report of your Lord has come to me, and His victory for you, and His mercy with which He showed you before I left my country, but I did not obey a guide, and nothing has thrown me into misery except my lack of intelligence. If I had listened or understood, I would not have attacked you, but misery has overcome me and those with me. Then the king of the Children of Israel said: Praise be to God, Lord of Glory, who has spared us from you as He willed. Our Lord did not spare you and those with you because of His honor towards you, but He only spared you and those with you for what is bad for you, so that you may increase in misery in this world and torment in the Hereafter, and so that you may inform those behind you of what you have encountered from the actions of our Lord, and so that you may warn those after you. Had it not been for that, He would not have spared you. Your blood and the blood of those with you is easier for God than the blood of a tick if you killed it. Then the king of the children of Israel ordered the commander of his guards to throw the mosques around their necks, and he paraded them for seventy days around the holy house of Elijah, and he provided them with two loaves of barley every day for each man of them. Sennacherib said to the king of the children of Israel, Killing us is better than what is being done to us, so do as you are commanded. So the king transferred them to the prison of killing. Then God revealed to the prophet Isaiah, Tell the king of the children of Israel to send Sennacherib and those with him to warn those behind them, and to honor them and carry them until they reach their country. The prophet Isaiah informed the king of that, and he did so. Sennacherib and those with him went out until they reached Babylon. When they arrived, he gathered the people and told them what God had done to his soldiers. His priests and magicians said to him, “O king of Babylon, we have been narrating to you the report of their Lord and the report of their prophet, and the revelation of God to their prophet, but you did not obey us. They are a nation that no one can defeat with their Lord.” So the matter of Sennacherib was among what they feared, but God sufficed them as a reminder and a lesson. Then Sennacherib remained after that for seven years, then he died. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: When Sennacherib died, he appointed Nebuchadnezzar, his grandson, as his successor, to do what his grandfather had done and to judge according to his judgment. He remained seventeen years, then God took the kingship of the Children of Israel, Siddiqah. The affair of the Children of Israel was confused and they competed for the kingdom until some of them killed each other over it, and their prophet Isaiah was with them, not submitting to him or accepting from him. When they did that, God said, as we have heard, to Isaiah: Stand up among your people and inspire with your tongue. So when the prophet stood up, God made his tongue speak with the revelation and he said: O sky, listen, and O earth, be silent. For God wants to tell the story of the Children of Israel, whom He raised with His grace, and chose for Himself, and singled them out with His honor, and favored them over His servants, and favored them with honor. They are like lost sheep that have no shepherd, so He sheltered their strays, and gathered their lost ones, mended their broken ones, treated their sick ones, fattened their emaciated ones, and preserved… Fatten it, and when he did that, it became arrogant, and its rams butted heads and killed each other, until there was no healthy bone left to mend another broken one. Woe to this sinful nation, and woe to these sinful people who do not know where the moment has come to them. The camel may remember its homeland and be afflicted, and the donkey may remember the meadow on which it has had its fill and return to it, and the bull may remember the meadow in which it has fattened and be afflicted. These people do not know where the moment has come to them, and they are people of understanding and intellects, they are neither cows nor donkeys. I will give them an example, so let them hear it: Tell them: How do you see a land that was empty for a time, ruined and dead, with no civilization in it, and it had a wise and powerful Lord, who turned to it with cultivation, and hated that his land should be ruined, although he was strong, or it may be said that he was lost, although he was wise, so he surrounded it with a wall, and built a palace in it, and caused a river to flow in it, and described in it plantings of olives, pomegranates, palm trees, grapes, and all kinds of fruits. And he took charge of it and kept it as a guardian with a sound mind and determination, a strong and trustworthy guardian. Then he went out and waited for it, and when it came out, its appearance came in ruins. They said: “How evil is this land! We think that its walls and palace should be demolished, its river should be buried, its value should be seized, and its vegetation should be burned until it becomes as it was the first time, ruined and dead, with no life in it.” God said to them: “The wall is my protection, and the palace is my law, and the river is my book, and the value is my prophet, and the vegetation is they, and the carob tree that brought out the vegetation is their evil deeds, and I have decreed upon them their decree upon themselves. And this is an example that God has set for them: they draw near to Me by slaughtering cows and sheep, but the meat does not reach Me nor do I eat it. They claim to draw near to Me through piety and refraining from slaughtering the souls that I have forbidden, but their hands are stained with it, and their clothes are covered with its blood. They build houses as mosques for Me, and purify their interiors, but defile their hearts and bodies.” They defile it, and decorate and adorn houses and mosques for me, and they ruin and corrupt their minds and dreams. So what need do I have to build houses when I do not live in them, and what need do I have to decorate mosques when I do not enter them? I was only ordered to raise them so that I may remember and glorify God in them, and so that they may be a landmark for whoever wants to pray in them. They say: If God were able to gather our love, He would gather it, and if God were able to understand our hearts, He would understand them. So take two dry sticks, then bring them and call them in the place where they are together, and say to the two sticks: God commands you to be one stick. So when He said that to them, they mingled and became one. So God said: Say to them: I am able to gather the love of the dry sticks and to bring them together, so how can I not be able to gather their love if I wish? Or how can I not be able to understand their hearts, when I am the One who formed them? They say: We fasted but our fasting was not lifted, we prayed but our prayer was not illuminated, we gave charity but our charity was not purified, we called with the cooing of doves, and we cried with the howling of wolves, but in all of that we were not heard and our prayers were not answered. God said: Ask them what prevents Me from answering them. Am I not the Hearer of the hearers, the Seeer of the seers, the Nearest of the responders, and the Most Merciful of the merciful? Is it because My hand has become hard, how can it be, when My hands are extended with goodness? I spend as I wish, and the keys to the treasuries are with Me, and none opens or closes them but Me? Beware, My mercy encompasses all things, and only those who are merciful show mercy to one another by virtue of its bounty. Or is it because I am stingy, and am I not the Most Generous of the generous, the Opener of good things, the Most Generous of those who give, and the Most Generous of those who are asked? If these people looked at themselves with the wisdom that was illuminated in their hearts, then they discarded it and bought the world with it, then they would see where they came from, and then they would be certain that their selves are their greatest enemies. How can I raise their fasting while they clothe it with false speech and strengthen themselves with forbidden food? How can I illuminate their prayers while their hearts are attentive to those who fight me and oppose me and violate my prohibitions? Or how can their charity be purified with me while they give charity with the money of others, and I only reward its usurped owners for it? Or how can I answer their supplication while it is only a word on their tongues and action is far from that? I only answer the gentle supplicant, and I only listen to the words of the weak and the poor. And one of the signs of My pleasure is the pleasure of the poor. So if they had mercy on the poor and brought the weak near, would they be fair to the oppressed, support the usurped, be just to the absent, and give the widow, the orphan, and the poor, and every person with a right his right? Then if it were necessary for me to speak Then mankind will have their word, and then I will be the light of their sight, and the hearing of their ears, and the understanding of their hearts, and then I will support their pillars, and I will be the strength of their hands and feet, and then I will remain their tongues and minds, they say when they hear my words, and my messages reach them that they are transmitted sayings, and inherited hadiths, and compositions of what magicians and soothsayers compose, and they claim that if they wished to produce a hadith like it they would do so, and that they would look into the unseen with what the devils suggest to them they would appear, and all of them conceal what they say and conceal, and they know that I know the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and I know what they reveal and what they conceal, and I have decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth a decree that I have established upon Myself, and I have set before it a deferred term, which must come to pass, so if they believe in what they claim of knowledge of the unseen, then let them tell You when I will carry it out, or at what time it will be, and if they are able to produce what they wish, then let them produce something like the ability with which they have I have passed, for I will make it manifest over all religions, even if the polytheists hate it. And if they are able to say what they want, then let them compose a wisdom like it, with which I will manage the matter of that decree, if they are truthful. For I decreed on the day I created the heavens and the earth that I would make prophethood among the hired, and that I would transfer the kingdom to the shepherds, and honor to the lowly, and strength to the weak, and wealth to the poor, and fortune to the few, and cities to the deserts, and thickets to the wastelands, and papyrus to the fields, and knowledge to the ignorant, and judgment to the unlettered. So ask them when this will be, and who will establish this, and by whose hand will he be established, and the helpers of this matter and its supporters, if they know, for I will send for that an unlettered prophet, who is not blind among the blind, nor misguided among the misguided, and is not rude nor coarse, nor a clamorer in the markets, nor adorned with obscenities, nor a speaker of obscenities. I will guide him to every beautiful thing, I will bestow upon him every noble characteristic, I will make tranquility his garment, and righteousness his slogan. And piety is his conscience, wisdom is his reason, truthfulness and loyalty are his nature, forgiveness and custom are his character, justice and goodness are his conduct, truth is his law, guidance is his leader, Islam is his religion, and Ahmad is his name. I guide with it after misguidance, I teach with it after ignorance, I raise with it after indolence, I make famous with it after insignificance, I increase with it after fewness, I enrich with it after poverty, I strengthen with it after division, I unite with it different hearts, scattered desires, and divided nations, and I make his nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, it enjoins what is right, and forbids what is wrong, in monotheism for Me, and in faith and sincerity for Me, they pray to Me standing and sitting, bowing and prostrating, they fight in My cause in ranks and in groups, and they leave their homes and their wealth seeking My pleasure. I inspire them to glorify and unify, to praise and thank and extol Me in their mosques and gatherings and their beds and their places of rest and their resting place....to abandon? They cheer, and sanctify themselves at the heads of the markets, and purify their faces and limbs for Me, and tie their garments in half, their sacrifice is their blood, and their Gospels are their chests, monks by night, lions by day, that is My bounty which I bestow upon whom I will, and I am the possessor of great bounty. So when their prophet Isaiah finished speaking to them, they attacked him, as I have heard, to kill him, so he fled from them, and a tree met him, and it split open, so he entered it, and Satan caught up with him and took hold of a fringe of his garment and showed it to them, so they put a saw in the middle of it and sawed it until they cut it, and cut him in the middle. Abu Ja`far said: According to the statement that we mentioned from Ibn `Abbas from the narration of al-Suddi, and the statement of Ibn Zayd, the corruption of the Children of Israel in the land was the first time they killed Zachariah, the Prophet of God, along with what had happened from them before and after that, until God sent upon them someone through whose hand He brought down His vengeance upon them of the disobedience of God, and their transgression against their Lord. As for the statement of Ibn Ishaq, from whom we have narrated, their corruption the first time was what was described by the one who killed them, Isaiah, son of Amaziah, the prophet of God. Ibn Ishaq mentioned that some of the people of knowledge told him that Zachariah died a death and was not killed, and that the one who was killed was Isaiah, and that Nebuchadnezzar was the one who was given power over the Children of Israel the first time after they killed Isaiah. Ibn Hamid told us that, on the authority of Salamah, on his authority. As for their corruption on earth the last time, there is no disagreement among the people of knowledge that it was their killing of John the Baptist, son of Zechariah. They differed as to who gave him power over them to take revenge on them at that time, and I will mention their disagreement on that, God willing. As for his statement, and to declare them to be of great haughtiness, we have mentioned the statement of those who said: What is meant by it is their arrogance towards God by their boldness towards Him and their opposition to His command. Mujahid used to say about that what follows: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And you will proclaim with great loftiness, he said: And you will proclaim with great loftiness to the people. Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. As for his saying, So when the first of the two promises comes, he means: So when the first of the two promises comes, with which they will cause corruption on earth, as: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, So when the first of the two promises comes, he said: When the first of the two promises comes, those are the two times that We decreed for the Children of Israel, You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice. And His statement, And We sent against you servants of Ours of great strength, and they scoured through the dwellings, and it was a promise fulfilled, means, the Most High, by His statement, We sent against you, We directed you, and We sent against you servants of Ours of great strength, meaning: those of great strength in war. And His statement, And they scoured through the dwellings, and it was a promise fulfilled, means: they went back and forth between the houses and dwellings, and they went and came. It is said about it: the people scoured through the houses and scoured with one meaning. And I scoured, scouring, scouring, and scouring. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the report was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas. Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, They went through the houses, he said: They walked. Some of the people of Basra who were knowledgeable in the speech of the Arabs used to say: The meaning of they went through is: They killed, and he used as evidence for his statement the following verse of Hassan: And among us is he who met the enemies with the sword of Muhammad, and with it he trampled the armies. It is possible that its meaning is: So they roamed throughout the homes, and killed them as they went and came, so both interpretations are correct. What is meant by his saying, And it was a promise to be fulfilled, is that the roaming of the people against whom We were sent throughout their homes was a promise from God to them that would inevitably be fulfilled, because He does not break His promise. Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God meant by his saying, Of great strength, in what they did the first time to the Children of Israel when He sent them, and about those against whom He sent them the second time, and what they did to them. Some of them said: The one whom God sent against them the first time was Goliath, and he was from the people of the peninsula. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad Bani Saad told me, he said: My father told us, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And when the first of the two promises came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they penetrated into the interior of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled. He said: God sent Goliath against them, and he penetrated into their homes, and We imposed on them taxes and humiliation, so they asked God to send them a king to fight in the way of God, so God sent Talut, and they fought Goliath, so God gave victory to the Children of Israel, and Goliath was killed by the hand of David, and God restored the kingdom to the Children of Israel. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, So when the first of the two promises came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they penetrated into the interior of the homes, and it was a promise fulfilled. God decreed a decree against the people as you hear, so in the first one He sent against them Goliath of Jazari, who took captive and killed, and they penetrated into the interior of the homes as God said, then the people returned and smoke hung among them. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: As for the first time, God sent Goliath against them, until He sent Talut and David with him, and David killed him. Others said: Rather, He sent Sennacherib against them the first time, and we have mentioned some of those who said that previously, and we will mention what we have witnessed of those we did not mention before. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mu’alla, who said: I heard Sa’id bin Jubayr say, regarding His statement, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, that God Almighty sent against them the first time Sennacherib from the people of Assyria and Nineveh, so I asked Sa’id about it, and he claimed that it was Mosul. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim bin Sa`id bin Jubayr narrated to me that he heard him say: A man from the Children of Israel was reciting until he reached, We sent against you Our servants of mighty war, he cried and his eyes overflowed with tears, and he closed the Mushaf and said that for as long as God willed, then he said: O Lord, show me this man at whose hands the destruction of the Children of Israel took place. So I saw in a dream a poor man in Babylon, whose name was Bukhtanasr. He went with his wealth and worshipped him, and he was a wealthy man. It was said to him, Where do you want to go? He said, I want to trade. Until he reached a house in Babylon, and he hired it, and there was no one there but him. He began to call the poor and treat them kindly until there was no one left. He said, Is there a poor man left besides you? They said, Yes, a poor man in the valley of so-and-so who is sick and whose name is Bukhtanasr. So he said to his servants, Go, until he came to him. He said, What is your name? Qaq: Bukhtanasr, he said to his servant: Carry him, so he carried him to him and treated him until he recovered, then he clothed him and gave him sustenance, then the Israelite gave permission to depart, so Bukhtanasr wept, so the Israelite said: What makes you weep? He said: I weep because you did to me what you did, and I do not find anything with which to repay you, he said: Yes, a little, if I were to rule you would obey me, so the other one followed him and said: Are you mocking me! And nothing prevented him from giving him what he asked for, except that he saw that he was mocking him, so the Israelite wept and said: I know what prevents you from giving me what I asked for, except that God wants to implement what He has decreed and written in His book and time has struck down its blows. So one day, Sahun, the king of Persia in Babylon, said: If we were to send an advance guard to the Levant! They said: What harm would it do you if you did? He said: Who do you think? They said: So-and-so. So he sent a man and gave him a hundred thousand, and Bukhtanasr went out to his kitchen. He did not go out except to eat in his kitchen. When he came to Syria and saw that the leader of the vanguard had the most horses and the most strong men on earth, he broke his arm, but he did not ask. He said: So Bukhtanasr began to sit in the gatherings of the people of Syria and say: What prevents you from invading Babylon? If you invaded it, there would be nothing less than its treasury. They said: We are not good at fighting. He said: So if you invaded, they said: We are not good at fighting and we do not fight! Until he carried out the councils of the people of Ash-Sham, then he returned and the vanguard informed their king of what he had seen, and Bukhtanasr kept saying to the king’s horsemen: If the king had called me, I would have told him something other than what so-and-so had told him. So he brought that up to him, so he called him and told him the story and said: When so-and-so saw that most of the land of God was horse and strong man, that was great in his mind and he did not ask them about anything, because I did not leave a council in Ash-Sham without sitting with its people, so I said to them such-and-such, and they said to me such-and-such, which Saeed bin Jubair mentioned that he said to them. The vanguard said to Bukhtanasr: You have disgraced me, you will have a hundred thousand and you will stop what you said. He said: If you gave me the treasury of Babylon, I would not stop. Time has struck its blows. The king said: If we sent a group of horses to Ash-Sham, if they found a way they would go, otherwise they would turn back as they could not. They said: What harm would it do you if you did? He said: Who do you think? They said: So-and-so. He said: Rather, it is the man who told me what he told me. So he summoned Nebuchadnezzar and sent him, and chose with him four thousand of their horsemen. They set out and scoured throughout the lands, and they took captive as much as God willed, but they did not destroy or kill. Then King Sayhun died. They said: Appoint a man as your successor! They said: Take it easy until you come to your companions, for they are your horsemen. They will not attack you at all. Give him respite. So they gave him respite until Nebuchadnezzar came with the captives and what he had with him, and he distributed them among the people. They said: We have not seen anyone more deserving of the kingdom than this one. So they made him king. Yunus bin Abdul A'la told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Sulayman bin Bilal told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, he said: I heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say: Nebuchadnezzar appeared in the Levant, so he destroyed Jerusalem and killed them, then he came to Damascus, and found there blood boiling on a sack, so he asked them: What is this blood? They said: We knew our fathers doing this, and whenever a sack appeared on it, it appeared. He said: So seventy thousand Muslims and others were killed because of that blood, and it calmed down. Others said: He meant by that some people from Persia. They said: There was no fighting the first time. Those who said that are mentioned: Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And when the first of the two promises came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they searched through the interior of the houses. He said: Those who came to them from Persia to spy on their report and listen to their conversation, with Nebuchadnezzar with them, so he memorized their conversations from among his companions, then Persia returned and there was no fighting, and the Children of Israel were victorious over them, so this was the first promise. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, We sent against you servants of Ours, possessors of great strength. An army came to them from Persia to spy on their report. Something similar was mentioned. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: So when the first of the two promises came, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might. He said: That is, whoever came to them from Persia, then he mentioned something similar.
17:6: God the Almighty says: Then We showed you, O Children of Israel, to these people whom He, the Most High, described as sending them against them. That victory and their turning against them was, as al-Suddi mentioned in his report, that the Children of Israel invaded them, took some of them, and rescued what was in their hands from them. And in the saying of others: The king who invaded them released what was in his hands of their prisoners, and returned to them what he had taken of their money without fighting. And in the saying of Ibn Abbas, which Atiyah narrated from him, it is God’s victory over their enemy Goliath until they killed him. And we have mentioned all of that with its chains of transmission previously. And We provided you with wealth and children means: And We increased what We gave you of wealth and children. And His saying, And We made you more numerous, means: And We made you more numerous and numerous than them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We made you more numerous: meaning in number, and that was during the time of David. Musa told me, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi: And We made you more numerous. He said: in number. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, Then We gave you back the upper hand over them, for the Children of Israel, after they had been defeated and the others had turned away from them, and made you more numerous, he said: We made you more numerous after this. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then We gave you back the upper hand over them. Then the upper hand was given to the Children of Israel. Muhammad bin Sinan Al-Qazzaz told me: Abu Asim told us, on the authority of Sufyan, regarding his statement, And We provided you with wealth and children, he said: Four thousand.
17:7: God Almighty says to the Children of Israel in what He decreed for them in the Torah: If you do good, O Children of Israel, and obey God and correct your affairs, and adhere to His commands and prohibitions, you do good, and do what you do of that for yourselves, because you only benefit from your actions, what you do of that, yourselves in this world and the Hereafter. As for this world, God will repel from you whoever seeks to harm you, and will increase your wealth and increase your strength. As for the Hereafter, God Almighty will reward you with His Paradise. But if you do evil, He says: If you disobey God and commit what He has forbidden you from, then you will do evil to yourselves, because you will thereby anger your Lord with yourselves, so He will give power to your enemy over you in this world, and will enable those who seek to harm you to prevail over you, and He will make you abide in the Hereafter in humiliating torment. And He, the Most High, said: And if you do evil, it is against her, meaning: it is to her, just as He said: Because your Lord has inspired her, meaning: He inspired her. And His saying, So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, means: So when the promise of the last time of your corruption, O Children of Israel, in the land comes, to disfigure your faces, means: So that the coming of that promise for the last time will disfigure your faces and make them ugly. The reciters differed in reading his statement li-yasu'u wujukm to make your faces ugly. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it li-yasu'u wujukm meaning: to make your faces ugly by the servants of great power whom God sends against you. The reciters of that cited as evidence for the correctness of their reading his statement and to enter the mosque and said: That is report about all of them, so it is necessary for his statement li-yasu'u to be like that. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it li-yasu'u wujukm on the singular and with the ya'. This may bear two interpretations, one of them is what I have mentioned, and the other of them is: to make your faces ugly. So from the interpretation of that to li-yasu'u wujukm, the answer to his statement if is omitted, and what is apparent from it is dispensed with, and that omitted came, so the interpretation of the statement is: So when the promise of the Hereafter came to make your faces ugly, it came. And from the aspect of its interpretation to: so that God may disfigure your faces, there was also something omitted in the speech, which was dispensed with here by what was apparent from it, except that that omitted thing was except for came, so the meaning of the speech then would be: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will raise them so that God may disfigure your faces, so the implied is We will raise them, and that is the answer to if then. And some of the Arab scholars from Kufa read that as a statement from God, blessed and exalted be His name, about Himself. The promise of the last time was to come when they killed Yahya. He mentioned the narration of that, and the report of what came to them from God at that time: As Musa told us, he said: Amr told us, he said: Asbat told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi in the hadith whose chain of transmission we mentioned before, that a man from the Children of Israel saw in a dream that the destruction of the Holy House and the destruction of the Children of Israel were at the hands of an orphan boy, the son of a widow from the people of Babylon, called Bukhtanasr, and they believed, so their vision came true, so he came and asked about him until he went down to his mother while he was gathering firewood, and when he came with a bundle of firewood on his head, he threw it, then sat on the side of the house and hugged him, then gave him three dirhams, and said: Buy us food and drink with them, so he bought meat for one dirham, bread for one dirham, and wine for one dirham, and they ate and drank until the second day he did the same to him, until the third day he did the same, then he said to him: I would like you to write me a pledge of security if you rule one day, so he said: Are you mocking me? He said: I am not mocking you, but what is wrong with you taking a hand with me? His mother spoke to him and said: What is wrong with you if that is the case, otherwise it will not decrease you in anything. So he wrote him a letter of security and said to him: What do you think, if I become dry and the people around you have come between me and you, then make me a sign by which you will recognize me? He said: Raise your document on a reed by which I will recognize you. So he clothed him and gave it to him. Then the king of the children of Israel honored John the son of Zakariya, brought him close to his council, consulted him in his affairs, and did not decide a matter without his permission. He wanted to marry the daughter of his wife, so he asked John about that, and he forbade him from marrying her and said: I do not accept her for you. Her mother heard about that and she hated John when he forbade him from marrying her daughter. So the mother of the slave girl went to the king when he sat drinking, and dressed her in thin red clothes, perfumed her, and dressed her with oaths. It was said that she dressed her in black over that. And with what did she send her to the king? She ordered her to give him a drink and to offer herself to him. If he wanted her to have sex with him, she would refuse him until he gave her what she asked for. When he gave her that, she asked him to bring the head of John the son of Zakariya in a basin, so she did, and she began to give him a drink and offer herself to him. When he took the drink from him, he wanted her to have sex with him, but she said: I will not do it until you give me what I ask you. So he said: What do you ask me? She said: I ask you to send for Yahya bin Zakariya, so his head was brought to him in this basin. He said: Woe to you, ask me for something other than this. She said to him: I do not want to ask you anything but this. He said: When she insisted, he sent for him, and his head was brought to him, and the head was talking until it was placed in front of him, and he said: This is not permissible for you. When morning came, his blood was boiling, so he ordered that dirt be thrown on him, and the blood rose above the dirt, so dirt was thrown on him again, and the blood rose above it, and he kept throwing dirt on him until he reached the wall of the city and it was boiling and reached Sahibain, so he revolted among the people, and wanted to send an army against them, and to appoint a man over them, so Bukhtanasr came to him and spoke to him and said: The one you sent that time is weak, and I have entered the city and heard the words of its people, so send me, so he sent him, and Bukhtanasr marched until they reached that place, and they fortified themselves against him in their cities, but he could not stand them, and when the stay became difficult for them and his companions were hungry, they wanted to return, so an old woman from the old women of the Children of Israel came out to them and said: Where is the commander of the army? So she was brought to him, and she said to him: It has reached me that you want to return with your army before you conquer this city, he said: Yes, my stay has been long, My companions were hungry, and I could not stay longer than I had been. She said: Tell me, if I opened the city to you, would you give me what I asked for, kill whomever I ordered you to kill, and refrain from doing so if I ordered you to refrain? He said: Yes. She said: When morning comes, divide your army into four quarters, then station a quarter at each corner, then raise your hands to the sky and call out: We ask you to open, O God, with the blood of John the son of Zachariah, for it will fall. So they did, and the city fell, and they entered from its sides. She said to him: Kill for this blood until it subsides. She went with him to the blood of John, which was on a lot of dirt, and he killed seventy thousand and women for it until it subsided. When the blood subsided, she said to him: Restrain your hand, for when God, the Blessed and Exalted, kills a prophet, He is not pleased until he kills the one who killed him, and whoever is pleased with him kills him. The owner of the document came to him with his document, so he refrained from him and his family, and he destroyed the Holy House, and ordered that the corpses be thrown into it, and he said: Whoever throws a corpse into it will have his reward that year. The Romans helped him in its destruction because the Children of Israel killed John. When Bukhtnasr destroyed it, he went with him with the faces of the Children of Israel and made them evil and went away. Nial, Elijah, Azariah, and Mishael, all of them sons of the prophets, appeared and he went with him with the head of Goliath. When he arrived in the land of Babylon, he found two companions who had come, so he reigned in his place. The most honorable people to him were Daniel and his companions. The Magi envied them for that, so they slandered him and said: Daniel and his companions do not worship your God, nor do they eat of your sacrifice. So he called them and asked them, and they said: Yes, we have a Lord whom we worship, and we do not eat of your sacrifice. So he ordered a thigh to be dug for them, and they threw them in it, and they were six, and he threw with them a ferocious lion to eat them. So he said: Go, let us eat and drink. So they went and ate and drank, then they went and found them sitting and the lion spread its arms among them, and it did not scratch any of them, nor did it hurt them in any way. They found a man with them, so they counted them and found them seven, so they said: What is the matter with this seventh? There were only six. So the seventh came out to them, and he was a king from the angels, and he slapped him a slap, so he became a wild beast. And he was among them for seven years, and no one saw him except that Wahshi came to him and had intercourse with him, and took revenge on him for what he had done to the men. Then he returned and God restored his kingdom to him, and they were the most honorable of God’s creation to him. Then the Magians slandered him a second time, so they threw a lion into a well that had been filled with fire, and they would throw a rock to it so that it would grab it. So they threw Daniel to him, and the lion stood on one side, and Daniel stood on the other side without touching him, so they took him out. Before that, he had made a pit for them, and he had lit a fire in it, and when he had kindled it, he threw them into it, and God extinguished it on them and they did not get anything from it. Then Nebuchadnezzar saw in his dream an idol whose head was of gold, whose neck was of bronze, whose sash was of iron, whose belly was a mixture of gold, silver, and glass, and whose feet were of copper. While he was standing and looking, a rock fell from the sky from the direction of the qiblah, and broke the idol into pieces. He woke up frightened and forgot what had happened, so he called the magicians and priests and asked them, saying: Tell me what you saw. They said to him: No, rather you tell us what you saw and we will interpret it for you. He said: I do not know. They said to him: These are the young men whom you honor, call them and ask them. If they do not tell you what you saw, what will you do with them? He said: I will kill them. So he sent for Daniel and his companions, and called them and said to them: Tell me what you saw. Daniel said to him: Rather you tell us what you saw and we will interpret it for you. He said: I do not know, I have forgotten it. Daniel said to him: How do we know a vision if you do not tell us about it? Then Daniel said to the gatekeeper: The king has ordered us to be killed because of his vision, so give us three days' delay. If we tell the king about his vision, otherwise strike off our heads. So he gave them a delay and they called upon God. On the third day, each of them saw a vision of Nebuchadnezzar separately. They went to the gatekeeper and told him. He went in to the king and told him. He said: Bring them in to me. Nebuchadnezzar did not know anything about his vision, except what they mentioned. They said to him: You saw such and such. They told him about it, and he said: You have spoken the truth. They said: Shall we interpret it for you? As for the idol whose head you saw was of gold, it is a king, beautiful like gold, and he had ruled the whole earth. As for the neck, which is of resemblance, it is the king of your son after him, who will rule and his kingdom will be beautiful, but it will not be like gold. As for its chest, which is of iron, it is the king of the people of Persia, who will rule after you, your son, and their kingdom will be strong like iron. As for its belly, which is of mixture, it will take away the kingdom of the people of Persia, and the people will dispute over the kingdom in every village, until the king rules for a day or two days, and a month or two months, then he will be killed, and the people will have no support for that, just as the idol could not have supported two men of clay. While they were like that, God Almighty sent a plant from the land of the Arabs, and made it prevail over the rest of the kingdom of the people of Persia, and the rest of the kingdom of your son and your kingdom, so it destroyed it and annihilated it until nothing of it remained, just as the rock came and demolished the idol. Then Nebuchadnezzar took pity on them and loved them. Then the Magi slandered Daniel, saying: When Daniel drinks wine, he cannot control himself from urinating, and that was a disgrace to them. So Nebuchadnezzar made them food, and they ate and drank. Then he said to the doorman: Look for the first one who comes out to urinate on you, and hit him with a stick, and if he says I am short, say you lied, Nebuchadnezzar ordered me. So God stopped Daniel from urinating, and the first of the people to get up to urinate was Nebuchadnezzar. So he got up hanging down, and that was at night, dragging his clothes. When the doorman saw him, he attacked him and said: Nebuchadnezzar. So he said: You lied, Nebuchadnezzar ordered me to kill the first one to come out. So he hit him and killed him. Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu al-Mu'alla: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: God sent Sennacherib against them the first time. He said: God restored the upper hand to them as He had said. He said: Then they disobeyed their Lord and returned to what they were forbidden from. So He sent Bukhtanasr against them the second time, so he killed the fighters, took the children captive, and took whatever money he found, and they entered the Holy House, as God Almighty said: And let them enter the Temple as they entered it the first time and destroy what they had taken over with utter destruction. They entered it, destroyed it, and ruined it, and threw into it whatever they could of dung, menstruation, carcasses, and filth. So God said: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you; but if you return [to sin], We will return [to sin]. So He had mercy on them, restored their kingdom to them, and freed those of the descendants of the Children of Israel who were in their hands, and He said to them: If you return [to sin], We will return. Abu al-Mu'alla said: I do not know that, except from this hadith, and He did not return them to their kingdom. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, So when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will disfigure your faces, he said: God sent the king of Persia to Babylon with an army, and he put Nebuchadnezzar in charge of them, so they came to the Children of Israel and destroyed them, and this was the Hereafter and its promise. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ya`la bin Muslim told me, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, he said: When the king Bukhtnasr struck Jarana, he said: Three, so whoever among you stays behind after that, let him walk to his wood, so he invaded the Levant, and that was when he was killed and he took out the Holy House, and took off his ornaments, and made them into vessels to drink wine from, and a table to eat pigs on, and he carried the Torah with him, then he threw it into the fire, and he brought with him among what he brought a hundred servants, including Daniel, Azariah, Hananiah, and Mishael, so he said to a man: Repair the bodies of these for me so that I may choose the path of four who will serve me, so Daniel said to his companions: They were victorious over you only because you changed the religion of your fathers, do not eat pork, and do not drink wine, so they said to the one who was repairing their bodies: Would you feed us food that is easier for you in terms of expenses than what you feed our companions, and if we do not get fat before them, I will see your opinion, he said: What? He said: Barley bread and leeks. So he did so and they grew fat before their companions. Then Nebuchadnezzar took them to serve him. While they were like that, Nebuchadnezzar saw a vision, so he sat down and forgot it. Then he went back to sleep and saw it again. Then he got up and forgot it. Then he saw it again and went out to the room and forgot it. When morning came, he called the scholars and soothsayers and said: Tell me what you saw last night, and interpret my vision for me. Otherwise, each one of you should walk to his wood. We will meet again the third time. They said: If he tells us his vision and mentions words that I have not memorized. He said: And whenever one of his relatives passed by Daniel, he would say: If the king called me, I would tell him his vision and interpret it for him. He said: So they said: How foolish is this Israelite boy until an old man passed by him and said that to him. So he went back to him and told him. Then he called him and said: What did you see? He said: I saw a statue. He said: What? He said: Its head was made of gold. He said: What? He said: Its neck was made of silver. He said: What? He said: Its chest was made of iron. He said: What? He said: Its stomach was made of brass. He said: What? He said: Its legs were made of ink. He said: What? He said: Its feet were made of pottery. He said: Is this what you saw? He said: What? He said: Then a pebble came and hit its head, then its neck, then its chest, then its stomach, then its legs, then its feet. He said: So it destroyed it. He said: What is this? He said: As for the gold, it is your property. As for the silver, it is the property of your son after you, then the property of your grandson. He said: As for the pottery, it is the property of women. So he dressed him in a Tarthon robe, and he made him walk around the village, and he gave him his ring. When the Persians saw that, they said: The matter is nothing but the matter of this Israelite. They said: Go to him from around the three youths, and do not mention Daniel to him, for he will not believe you about him. So they went to him, and they said: These three youths are not of your religion, and the proof of that is that if you offer them pork and wine, they will not eat or drink. So he ordered a lot of firewood to be placed, then he made them ascend it, then he lit a fire in it, then he went out at the end of the night to urinate, and behold, they were talking, and a fourth one was with them, going to pray to them. He said: Who is this, O Daniel? He said: This is Gabriel, you have wronged them. He said: You have wronged them, order them to come down. So he ordered them to come down. He said: And God transformed Nebuchadnezzar from all the beasts, and made from each kind of beast the head of a wild animal: from the wild animals the lion, and from the bird the eagle, and his son became king. He saw a hand come out between two boards, then it wrote two lines. So he called the soothsayers and scholars, but they did not find any knowledge in that. So his mother said to him: If you restore to Daniel the position that he had with your father, I will tell you. But he had been rude to him, so he called him and said: I am restoring to you your position with my father, so tell me what these two lines are. He said: As for restoring to me my position with your father, I have no need of it, but as for these two lines, you will be killed tonight. So he brought out everyone in the palace, and ordered it to be locked. So the doors were locked on him, and he entered with him the most secure of the people of the village in his heart with a sword. So he said: Whoever comes to you from God’s creation, kill him, even if he says I am so-and-so. And God sent a plague upon him, so he walked until it was half the night, then he slept and his companion slept, then his stomach woke him up, so he went walking while the other was asleep, so he returned and woke him up, and he said to him: I am so-and-so, so he struck him with the sword and killed him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “If you do good, you do good for yourselves, but if you do evil, it is against yourselves. So when the promise of the Hereafter comes,” the last of the two punishments, to disfigure your faces and to enter the temple as they entered it the first time, as their enemy had entered it before that, and to destroy what they had exalted with utter destruction, so God sent upon them in the Hereafter the Babylonian Bukhtanasr, the most hated of God’s creation, so he took captive, killed, and destroyed the Holy House, and afflicted them with terrible torment. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: So when the promise of the Hereafter comes of the two times, to disfigure your faces he said: to disfigure your faces, and to destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction he said: to destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction, he said: He is Bukhtanasr, God sent him to them the last time. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: So when they caused corruption, God sent upon them the last time Bukhtanasr, so he destroyed the mosques and they became very tired and exhausted. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us: He said, as far as I have been informed: God appointed a man from among them called Nasha bin Amwaz as a successor over the Children of Israel after that, meaning after they killed Isaiah. Then God sent al-Khidr as a prophet. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say, as far as I have been informed: Al-Khidr was called al-Khidr because he sat on a white fur and got up from it while it was shaking green. He said: And the name of al-Khidr, according to what Wahb bin Munabbih claimed about the Children of Israel, was Jeremiah bin Halfiah, and he was from the tribe of Aaron bin Imran. Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn Askar and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Malik ibn Zanjawayh told me: Ismail ibn Abd al-Karim told us: Abd al-Samad ibn Muqal told us, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih, and Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of someone who is not accused, on the authority of Wahb ibn Munabbih al-Yamani. The wording is from the hadith of Ibn Humayd, that he used to say: God Almighty said to Jeremiah when He sent him as a prophet to the Children of Israel: O Jeremiah, before I created you, I chose you, and before I formed you in your mother’s womb, I sanctified you, and before I brought you out of your mother’s womb, I purified you, and before you reached the age of puberty, I announced your narration, and before you reached maturity, I chose you, and for a great matter, I hid you. So God sent Jeremiah to that king from the Children of Israel to guide him and direct him, and to bring him the report from God between him and God. He said: Then the events became great among the Children of Israel, and they committed sins, and made permissible the forbidden things, and forgot what God had God Almighty did to them, and did not save them from their enemy Sennacherib and his soldiers. So God Almighty inspired Jeremiah: Go to your people from the Children of Israel, and tell them what I have commanded you, and remind them of My blessings upon them, and tell them their events. Jeremiah said: I am weak if you do not strengthen me, and helpless if you do not inform me, and mistaken if you do not guide me, and forsaken if you do not support me, and humiliated if you do not honor me. God Almighty said: Did you not know that all matters proceed from My will, and that all hearts and tongues are in My hand, I turn them as I wish, so they obey Me? And I am God, there is nothing like Me. The heavens and the earth and what is in them were established by My word, and I spoke to the seas, so they understood My word, and I commanded them, so they understood My command, and I set a boundary over them in the plain, so they do not transgress My limit. They come with waves like mountains, until when they reach My limit, I clothe them with the humiliation of My obedience, out of fear and acknowledgment of My command that I am with you, and nothing will reach you with Me. And I have sent you to a great creation of My creation, to convey to them My messages and to deserve thereby the same reward as those who follow you from among them, without that detracting from their rewards in the slightest. And if you fall short of them, then you will have the same burden as those who ride blindly, without that detracting from their burdens in the slightest. Go to your people and say: God has mentioned to you the righteousness of your fathers, and that has prompted Him to ask you to repent, O group of children. And ask them how their fathers found the consequences of obeying Me, and how they found the consequences of disobeying Me. Did they know that anyone before them obeyed Me and was miserable because of my obedience, or disobeyed Me and was happy because of my disobedience? For the beasts are among those who remember their good homelands, so they are tempted. And these people have grazed in the meadows of destruction. As for their rabbis and monks, they have taken My servants as slaves to worship them instead of Me, and they have ruled over them without My Book until they have made them ignorant of My command, and made them forget My remembrance, and deceived them from Me. As for their leaders and commanders, they have been arrogant about My blessings and have believed in Me. They have deceived me, rejected my book, forgotten my covenant, and changed my way. So my servants have permitted them to obey me, which is only due to me. They obey them in disobeying me, and they follow them in the innovations that they innovate in my religion, out of audacity towards me, deception, and slander towards me and my messengers. Glory be to my majesty, the loftiness of my position, and the greatness of my status. Is it appropriate for a human being to be obeyed in disobeying me? Is it appropriate for me to create servants whom I make lords besides me? As for their readers and jurists, they worship in the mosques, and adorn themselves by building them for other than me, seeking the world through religion, and they gain understanding in them for other than knowledge, and they learn in them for other than action. As for the children of the prophets, they are numerous, subjugated, and jealous. They engage in squabbling with those who engage in squabbling, and they wish from me the same victory as their fathers and the honor with which I honored them, and they claim that no one is more deserving of that than me, without truth, thought, or deliberation. They do not mention how patient their fathers were with me, and how Their grandfather was in my affair when the invaders changed, and how they sacrificed their souls and blood, so they were patient and truthful until my affair became strong and my religion became apparent, so I was patient with these people so that they might respond, so I prolonged it for them, and pardoned them so that they might return, so I multiplied and extended their lives so that they might remember, so I excused, in all of that I rained down upon them from the sky, and caused the earth to grow for them, and clothed them with health and made them victorious over the enemy so that they only increase in transgression and distance from me, so until when will this happen? Will they practice their father or will they deceive me? Because I swear by my glory that I will arouse for them a trial in which the forbearing will be perplexed, and the opinion of the wise will go astray, and the wisdom of the wise will go astray, then I will set upon them a tyrant, harsh and violent, I will clothe him with awe, and from his chest I will extract compassion, mercy and eloquence, followed by a number and blackness like the blackness of the dark night, with armies like pieces of clouds, and ships like dust, as if the fluttering of his banners were the flight of eagles, and that the bearers of his cavalry were like copper Then God revealed to Jeremiah: I will destroy the children of Israel with Japheth. Japheth is the people of Babylon, and they are from the descendants of Japheth, son of Noah. Then when Jeremiah heard the revelation of his Lord, he cried out and wept and tore his clothes and threw ashes on his head and said: Cursed is the day I was born, and the day I met the Torah, and from the worst of my days is the day I was born, for I did not leave the last of the prophets except for what is worse for me. If He had wanted good for me, He would not have made me the last of the prophets from the children of Israel, for it is because of me that misery and destruction will befall them. When God heard the supplication of Al-Khidr and his weeping, and how he was saying, He called to him: O Jeremiah, is that difficult for you in what I revealed to you? He said: Yes, O Lord, destroy me before I see in the children of Israel what I do not like. God said: By My mighty glory, I will not destroy the Holy House and the children of Israel until the command in that is from you. Jeremiah was happy at that when his Lord said to him, and his soul was at peace, and he said: No, by He who sent Moses and His prophets with the truth, I will not command my Lord. Then he came to the king of the children of Israel and told him what God had revealed to him, so he was glad and joyful and said: If our Lord punishes us, it is for many sins that we have brought upon ourselves, and if He pardons us, it is by His power. Then they remained after this revelation for three years, and they only increased in disobedience and persistence in evil, and that was when their destruction approached, so the revelation decreased when they did not remember the Hereafter, and it was held back from them when the world and its affairs distracted them, so their king said to them: O children of Israel, desist from what you are doing before the wrath of God touches you, and before He sends upon you a people who have no mercy for you, and your Lord is close to repentance, His hands are extended with goodness, and He is merciful to those who repent to Him. But they refused to give up anything of what they were doing, and God had put in the heart of Bukhtanasr bin Nijur-Zadhan bin Sennacherib bin Darias bin Nimrod bin Falakh bin Eber bin Nimrod, the companion of Abraham who argued with him about his Lord, to go to the Holy House, then do in it what his grandfather Sennacherib had wanted to do. He did so, and he went out with six hundred thousand banners, seeking the people of Jerusalem. When he had departed, the report reached the king of the children of Israel that Nebuchadnezzar had come with his soldiers seeking you. So the king sent to Jeremiah, and he came to him and said: O Jeremiah, where is what you claimed to us that your Lord revealed to you not to destroy the people of Jerusalem until you have the command to do so? So Jeremiah said to the king: My Lord does not break His promise, and I trust in Him. So when the time drew near and the end of their kingdom drew near and God was determined to destroy them, God sent an angel from Himself and said to him: Go to Jeremiah and ask him, and command him to do what he asks for a question about. So the angel came to Jeremiah, and he had appeared to him as a man from the children of Israel, so Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: A man from the children of Israel, seeking a question from you about some of my affairs. So he gave him permission, and the king said to him: O Prophet of God, I have come to you to ask you about my relatives, and I have connected their relatives with what God has commanded me to do. I have only treated them well, and I have not spared them any honor, so do not increase my honor to them. He said to him: Do good in what is between you and God, and do what God has commanded you to do, and be glad with good report. He turned away from him, and he stayed for a few days, then he came to him in the same state that he had come to him, and sat before him, and Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the man who came to you to ask you about the matter of my family. The Prophet of God said to him: Have their morals not yet become clear to you, and have you not seen from them what you like? He said: O Prophet of God, by the One Who sent you with the truth, I do not know of any honor that anyone can bestow upon his relatives except that I have done it to them and better than that. The Prophet said: Go back to your family and be good to them. I ask God, who sets right His righteous servants, to set right what is between you, and to gather you together for His pleasure, and to spare you from His wrath. The king rose from him, and he stayed for a few days, and Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers had descended around the Holy House, and with him were people from his people like locusts, so the Children of Israel were terrified by them, and that was difficult for the King of the Children of Israel, so he called out Jeremiah, he said: O Prophet of God, where is what God promised you? He said: I am confident in my Lord. Then the king came to Jeremiah while he was sitting on the wall of the Holy House, laughing and rejoicing in the victory of his Lord that He promised him. So he sat in front of him, and Jeremiah said to him: Who are you? He said: I am the one who came to you twice regarding my family. The Prophet said to him: Is it not time for them to refrain from what they are doing? The king said to him: O Prophet of God, everything that happened to me from them before today, I used to be patient with it, and I know that their intention in that is my anger. But when I came to them today, I saw them doing something that does not please God and that God Almighty does not love. The Prophet of God said to him: What action did you see them doing? He said: O Prophet of God, I saw them doing something great that angered God. If they were as they were before today, my anger would not have been intense with them, and I would have been patient with them and hoped for them. But I became angry today for God and for you, so I came to you to tell you about them, and I ask you by God who sent you with the truth, except that you call upon your Lord to destroy them. He said: Jeremiah: O Owner of the heavens and the earth, if they are right and correct, then keep them, but if they are angry with You and do not please You, then destroy them. No sooner had the word left Jeremiah’s mouth than God sent a thunderbolt from the sky into the Holy House, and the place of sacrifice was ignited, and seven of its gates were swallowed up. When Jeremiah saw that, he cried out, tore his clothes, and threw ashes on his head and said: O King of the heavens and the earth, in Your hand is the kingdom of all things, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful. Where is Your appointment that You promised me? Then Jeremiah was called: What happened to them did not happen except because of your fatwa that you issued to our Messenger. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was certain that it was his fatwa that he issued three times, and that he was the Messenger of his Lord. Then Jeremiah flew until he mingled with the wild beasts, and Nebuchadnezzar and his soldiers entered the Holy House, and he trampled on the Levant, and killed the Children of Israel until he annihilated them, and destroyed the Holy House. He ordered his soldiers to fill each man’s shield with dirt and then throw it into the Holy House, so they threw dirt into it until they filled it, then He returned to the land of Babylon, and took with him the captives of the children of Israel, and ordered them to gather all who were in Jerusalem, so every young and old of the children of Israel gathered before him, and he chose from them seventy thousand boys, and when the spoils of his army came out, and he wanted to divide them among them, the kings who were with him said to him: O king, all our spoils are yours, and divide among us these boys whom you have chosen from the children of Israel, so he did, and each man of them got four young men, and among those young men were Daniel, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael, and seven thousand from the people of the house of David, and eleven thousand from the tribe of Joseph, son of Jacob, and his brother Benjamin, and eight thousand from the tribe of Asher, son of Jacob, and fourteen thousand from the tribe of Zebulun, son of Jacob, and Naphtali, son of Jacob, and four thousand from the tribe of Judah, son of Jacob, and four thousand from the tribe of Reuben and Levi, sons of Jacob, and those who remained from the children of Israel, and Nebuchadnezzar made them into three groups, and a third settled in the Levant, He took a third of them captive, killed two thirds, and took the vessels of the Holy House and brought them to Babylon. He took the seventy thousand boys and brought them to Babylon. This was the first battle that God brought down upon the Children of Israel because of their events and their injustice. When Nebuchadnezzar turned away from them, returning to Babylon with the captives of the Children of Israel, Jeremiah came upon him on a donkey with juice. Then he mentioned his story when God caused him to die for a hundred years, then resurrected him, then he told the story of Nebuchadnezzar’s vision and Daniel’s matter, Nebuchadnezzar’s death, the return of those who remained of the Children of Israel in the hands of Nebuchadnezzar’s companions after his death to the Levant, the reconstruction of the Holy House, the matter of Ezra and how God returned the Torah to him. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, he said: Then the Children of Israel began to create events after that, meaning after the death of Ezra, and God returned to them and sent messengers among them, and a group of them denied, and a group of them killed, until the last of their prophets whom God sent among them were Zachariah, John the son of Zachariah, and Jesus the son of Mary, and they were from the house of David. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Urwah, on the authority of Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr, that he said, while he was narrating the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariya: Yahya ibn Zakariya was not killed except because of a prostitute from the prostitutes of the Children of Israel, and there was a king among them, and Yahya ibn Zakariya was under the authority of that king. The daughter of that king understood her father and said: If I were to marry my father, his authority would be given to me without women. So she said to him: O my father, marry me and invite him to herself. So he said to her: O my daughter, Yahya ibn Zakariya is not permissible for us to do this. So she said: Who will give me Yahya ibn Zakariya? He has made things difficult for me and has prevented me from marrying my father, so that I may gain control of his kingdom and his world without women. So she ordered the players and did that for the sake of killing Yahya ibn Zakariya, so she said: Go in to him and play, until when you are done, he will judge you, then say: The blood of Yahya ibn Zachariah and do not accept anyone other than him. The king's name was Rawad, and his daughter's name was Al-Baghi. When a king among them spoke and lied, or made a promise and broke it, he was deposed and replaced by another. When they played with him and his amazement at them increased, he said: Ask me and I will give you. They said to him: We ask you for the blood of John the son of Zachariah, give it to us. He said: Woe to you, ask me for something other than this. They said: We will not ask you for anything other than this. He feared for his kingdom if he broke it to them, that he would consider it permissible to depose him. So he sent for John the son of Zachariah while he was sitting in his prayer niche, praying. They slaughtered him in a basin, then cut off his head. A man carried it in his hand while the blood was being carried in the basin with him. He said: A camel climbed up with its head until it stood before the king and his head was saying in the hand of the one carrying it, This is not permissible for you. A man from the Children of Israel said: O king, if you were to give me this blood! He said: What would you do with it? He said: Purify the earth from it, for he had made it too narrow for us. He said: Give him this blood. So he took it and put it in a jug, then he took it to a house in the altar, and put the jug in it, then he closed it, and it evaporated in the jug until it came out of it from under the door of the house in which he was. When the man saw that, he was terrified by it, so he took it out and put it in a deserted area, and it began to evaporate, and the events were great among them. Some of them say: He confirmed his place in the sacrifice and did not change it. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Salamah told us, he said: Ibn Ishaq said: When God raised Jesus from among them and they killed Yahya bin Zakariya - and some people say: They killed Zakariya - God sent against them a king from the kings of Babylon called Khordos, so he marched against him with the people of Babylon until he entered Syria. When he gained victory over them, he ordered a chief of his army called Nabur Zadan, the master of killing, and he said to him: I have sworn by my God that if we gain victory over the people of Jerusalem, I will kill them until their blood flows in the midst of my army, unless I find no one to kill.
