So he ordered that they be killed until Nabur Zadan reached that point. So he entered Jerusalem and stood in the spot where they were offering their sacrifices, and he found blood boiling there. So he asked them, saying: O children of Israel, what is the matter with this boiling blood? Tell me his story and do not hide anything from me about his affair. They said: This is the blood of a sacrifice that was ours. We offered it but it was not accepted from us. That is why it is boiling as you see. We offered sacrifices eight hundred years ago and they were not accepted from us except for this sacrifice. He said: You did not believe the report. They said to him: If it were like the beginning of our time, it would have been accepted from us, but the kingdom, prophecy and revelation have been cut off from us, so it was not accepted from us. So Nabur Zadhan slaughtered from them seven hundred and seventy souls from their heads over that blood, but it did not calm down. So he ordered seven hundred of their boys to be slaughtered over the blood, but it did not calm down. Then he ordered seven thousand of their followers and wives to be slaughtered over the blood, but it did not cool down or calm down. When Nabur Zadhan saw that the blood would not calm down, he said to them: Woe to you, O children of Israel! Believe me and be patient with the command of your Lord. For you have ruled the earth for a long time, doing in it what you wish before I do not leave among you a fire-blower, neither female nor male. Except that he killed him. When they saw the effort and severity of the killing, they believed him in the report. They said to him: This is the blood of a prophet from among us who used to forbid us from many things that anger God. If we had obeyed him in them, it would have been better for us. He used to inform us about your affair, but we did not believe him, so we killed him. This is his blood. Nabur Zadan said to them: What was his name? They said: Yahya bin Zakariya. He said: Now you have believed me. With the likes of this your Lord will take revenge on you. When Nabur Zadan saw that they had believed him, he fell down in prostration and said to those around him: Close the gates, the gates of the city, and take out whoever was here from the army of Khordos and leave. In the Children of Israel, then he said: O Yahya bin Zakariya, my Lord and your Lord knows what has befallen your people because of you, and what has been killed from them because of you, so calm down by God’s permission before I leave no one of your people. So the blood of Yahya bin Zakariya calmed down by God’s permission, and Nabur Zadan lifted the killing from them and said: I believe in what the Children of Israel believed in, and I am certain and certain that there is no Lord other than Him, and if there was another with Him, He would not be righteous, and if He had a partner, the heavens and the earth would not have held together, and if He had a son, He would not be righteous. So blessed and sanctified be He, glorified and magnified be He, the King of Kings, to Him belongs the kingdom of the seven heavens and the earths and what is in them and what is between them, and He is over all things competent. To Him belongs patience and knowledge and might and power, and He is the One who spread out the earth and placed firm mountains in it so that it would not move, so it is appropriate for my Lord to be and his kingdom will be. So God revealed to the head of one of the remaining prophets that Nabur Zadan is a truthful Habur, and Habur in Hebrew means the talk of faith. Or Nabur Zadan said to the Children of Israel, O Children of Israel, the enemy of God, Khordos, has ordered me to kill so many of you that your blood will flow in the midst of his army, because I cannot disobey him. They said to him, Do what you are ordered to do. So he ordered them to dig a trench and ordered their wealth of horses, mules, donkeys, cows, sheep, and camels to be slaughtered until the blood flowed in the army. He ordered the dead who were before that to be thrown on what had been killed of their livestock until they were on top of them. Khordos thought that what was in the trench was from the Children of Israel. When the blood reached his army, he sent to Nabur Zadan to remove it from them, for their blood has reached me, and I have taken revenge on them for what they did. Then he turned away from them to the land of Babylon, and he had destroyed the Children of Israel or almost, and this is the last battle that God sent down upon the Children of Israel, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “And We decreed to the Children of Israel in the Scripture, ‘You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach great haughtiness.’ But when the promise of the first of the two came to pass, We sent against you servants of Ours of great might, and they ravaged through the dwellings, and it was a promise fulfilled. Then We gave you back the upper hand over them and reinforced you with wealth and children and made you more numerous in manpower. If you do good, you do good for yourselves, and if you do evil, it is against yourselves. But when the promise of the last came to pass, they will disfigure your faces and enter the temple as they entered it the first time and destroy what they had exalted with utter destruction. Perhaps your Lord will have mercy on you. But if you return [to evil], We will return [to evil] and We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison.” And perhaps from God is true, so the first battle was: Bukhtanasr and his soldiers, then God gave you back the upper hand over them, and the second battle was Khordos and his soldiers, and it was the greater of the two battles, in it was the destruction of their country, and the killing of Their men, and their children and women were taken captive. God Almighty says, And that they may destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction. Then God turned against them, increasing their numbers and spreading them throughout their lands. Then they changed and created events, and replaced their book with another, and committed sins, and made permissible the forbidden things and neglected the limits. Ibn Humayd narrated: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Atab, a man from Taghlib who was a Christian for a long time, then converted to Islam later, and he read the Qur’an and gained knowledge of the religion. It was mentioned that he was a Christian for forty years, then he lived for forty years in Islam. He said: The last of the prophets of the Children of Israel was a prophet whom God sent to them, and he said to them: O Children of Israel, God says to you: I have taken away your voices, and I have made you hateful because of your many events. So they intended to kill him, but God, the Blessed and Exalted, said to him: Go to them and give me and them an example, and say to them: God, the Blessed and Exalted, says to you: Judge between Me and My vineyard. Did I not choose the land for it, and make the crops good for it, and surround it with a fence, and cover it with gruel, thorns, hedges, and brambles, and surround it with My cloak, and prevent it from the world and its excess, so that it meets Me with thorns and trunks, and every tree that is not eaten? Why did you choose the land, and make the crops good, and I fenced him in, nor did I cover him with barley flour, nor did I enclose him with my cloak, nor did I prevent him from the world. I preferred you and completed my favor upon you, then you met me with everything I hate of disobeying me and going against my command. Indeed, a donkey knows its manger, and indeed, a cow knows its master. I swore by my mighty glory and my strong arm that I would take my cloak, and I would move the wall, and I would place you under the feet of the world. He said: So they attacked their prophet and killed him, so God struck humiliation upon them and took away their kingdom. They are not among any nation except that they are subject to humiliation, disgrace, and a tribute that they pay, while the kingdom is among other people. They will never cease to be like that, as long as they are on what they are. He said: This is what has reached us from the collection of the hadiths of the Children of Israel. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, So when the promise of the Hereafter comes to pass, they will disfigure your faces and enter the mosque as they entered it the first time and destroy what they had conquered with utter destruction, he said: The Hereafter was much more severe than the first, he said: Because the first was only defeat, and the Hereafter was destruction, and Nebuchadnezzar burned the Torah until not a single letter of it remained, and he destroyed the mosque. Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Jesus, son of Mary, sent John, son of Zakariya, with twelve of the disciples to teach the people. He said: Among the things he forbade them from was marrying their brother’s daughter. He said: Their king had a brother’s daughter whom he liked and wanted to marry. She had a need that he would fulfill every day. When her mother heard about that, she said to her: When you enter upon the king and he asks you for your need, say: My need is that you slaughter John, son of Zakariya. When she entered upon him, he asked her for her need, and she said: My need is that you slaughter John, son of Zakariya. He said: Ask for something other than this. She said: I ask you nothing but this. He said: When she refused, he called John and called for a basin and slaughtered him, and a drop of his blood splattered on the ground. It continued to boil until God sent Nebuchadnezzar upon them. An old woman from the Children of Israel came to him and showed him the blood. He said: So God cast into His mind that they should kill for that blood until it subsided, so He killed seventy thousand of them of the same age and it subsided. And His statement, And let them enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, means: And let your enemy whom I send against you enter the mosque of Jerusalem by force and domination over you, as they entered it the first time when you spread corruption in the land. As for His statement, And let them destroy what they have gained control over, He says: And let them destroy what they have gained control over of your lands, completely. It is said from this: He destroyed the country, if you ruined it and killed its people, and he destroyed it, and he destroyed it, he destroyed it, he destroyed it. And from this is the statement of God, the Most High, And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction, meaning: destruction. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: And that they may destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction. He said: Destruction. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And that they may destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction. He said: They may destroy what they have exalted with utter destruction.
17:8: God Almighty says: Perhaps your Lord, O Children of Israel, will have mercy on you after taking revenge on you through the people whom God will send against you, so that his mission will make your faces ugly, and that they will enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, so that He will rescue you from their hands, and rescue you from the humiliation that he will inflict upon you, and raise you from the obscurity that you will fall into, and then honor you. Perhaps it is obligatory from God. And God did that to them, so their numbers increased after that, and their baseness was removed, and He made from them kings and prophets, so He, the Most High, said to them: And if you return, O Children of Israel, to disobeying Me and opposing My command, and killing My messengers, We will return to you with killing and captivity, and bringing humiliation and disgrace upon you. So they returned, so God returned to them with His punishment and bringing His wrath upon them. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Atiyah told us, on the authority of Umar ibn Thabit, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. But if you return [to sin], We will return [to sin].” He said: They returned, so he returned, then they returned, so he returned, then they returned, so he returned. He said: So God gave power over them to three kings from the kings of Persia: Sinbadan, Shahrabadan, and another. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: God Almighty said after the first and the last: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you, but if you return [to sin], We will return [to sin]. He said: So they returned, so God gave power over them to the believers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. So God returned to them with His return and mercy. And if you return, We will return. He said: The people returned with evil that was present to them, so God sent upon them whatever He willed to send of His vengeance and punishment. Then the conclusion of that was that God sent upon them this tribe of Arabs, so they are in torment from them until the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty said in another verse: And when your Lord proclaimed that He would send upon them until the Day of Resurrection. So God sent upon them this tribe of Arabs. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you, but if you return [to sin], We will return [to sin]. So they returned, and God sent Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to them, and they pay the jizyah willingly, and they are humiliated. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you, he said after this, And if you return to what you did like this of killing Yahya and other prophets, We will return to you with something like this. And His statement, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers in which they are imprisoned. Who said that? Muhammad bin Mas`adah told us: Ja`far bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of Abu Imran: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. He said: A prison. Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, meaning: God made their abode in it. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. He said: A confined and imprisoned place. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. He said: a prison. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, a confined place, he said: They are confined in it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers. He said: They will be confined in it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, a prison in which they are imprisoned, they are confined in it. Ali bin Dawud said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We have made Hell a prison for the disbelievers, meaning: a prison. Others said: Its meaning is: We made Hell a bed and a resting place for the unbelievers. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar: Al-Hasan said: Al-Hasir is a mattress and a rug. Al-Hasan said this to the effect that in this place the word hasir means a mat that is spread out and spread out, because the Arabs call a small rug a hasir. Al-Hasan directed the meaning of the statement to the fact that God Almighty has made Hell a rug and a rug for the disbelievers in Him, as He said: For them are beds of Hell, and above them are coverings. This is a good explanation and a correct interpretation. As for the others, they directed it to the fact that it is a verbal noun from confinement, which means confinement. I have explained this with evidence in Surat al-Baqarah. The Arabs call a kingdom a hasir in the sense that it is confined, meaning that it is veiled from the people, as Labid said: And the standing of the necks as if they were jinn at the door of the mat He means by mat: the king. The miser is called: hasur and hasr? Because he prevents the money he has from the needy, and withholds it from spending, as Al-Akhtal said: A drinker who drinks from the cup, make me regret neither the presence nor the bracelet It is narrated: With a rope. And from it is the confinement in speech because it is impossible for him to do so, and his being held back if he wants to do so, and from it also the abstinence from women because it is impossible for him to do so, and his abstinence from intercourse, and likewise the confinement in excrement: his being held back from exiting, and the origin of all of that is one even if its wording differs. As for the two hasirs: they are the two sides, as Al-Tirmaah said: A little bit is recited, then it is said that it is a must on every mat spread out. He means by the two mats: the two sides. The correct thing to say about that in my opinion is to say: The meaning of that is: And We have made Hell a mat for the disbelievers is a bed and a resting place that does not depart from the mat which means a rug, because if that is the case then it includes the meaning of confinement and relaxation, although the mat in the sense of a rug in the speech of the Arabs is more famous than it is in the sense of confinement, and that when she wants to describe something in the sense of confining something, she says: it is its confiner or confined, but the mat is not found in their speech, except if she describes it as a direct object, in which case it is in the word fa’ya, and its meaning is direct object, do you not see the verse of Labid: At the door of the mat, so he said at the door of the mat, because he meant: At the door of the confined, so he changed the direct object to fa’il, but fa’il in confinement means describing it as the confiner, and that is what we do not find in the speech of the Arabs, so I said: The statement of al-Hasan is more correct in that. Some of the Arabists from Basra claimed that this is permissible, but I do not know of any valid reason for what he said, except for a remote one, which is that it is said: Ja’a Hasir means Ja’a besieger, just as it was said: Alim means a scholar, and Shahid means witness. And this was not heard used in hasir as we heard it in alim and shahid.
17:9: God Almighty says: This Qur’an that We revealed to our Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, guides and directs whoever is guided by it to that which is most upright. He says: To the path that is most upright than other paths, and that is the religion of God with which He sent His prophets, which is Islam. God Almighty says: This Qur’an guides God’s servants who are guided by it to the path from which all the people of the religions who deny it have strayed. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Indeed, this Qur’an guides to that which is most upright, he said: To that which is most correct: it is the correctness and the truth. He said: And that which is contrary is falsehood. And he recited the statement of God, the Most High, In it are upright books, he said: In it is the truth, there is no crookedness in it. And he recited, And He has not made therein any crookedness, “upright,” he said: upright and straight. And His statement, And He gives good tidings to the believers, he said: And He also gives good tidings along with His guidance to those who are guided by Him to the most correct path, who believe in God and His Messenger, and do in their worldly life what God has commanded them to do, and refrain from what He has forbidden them from, that for them is a reward from God for their faith and righteous deeds, great, meaning a great reward and a generous recompense, and that is the Paradise that God, the Most High, has prepared for those whose deeds are pleasing to Him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, That they will have a great reward. He said: Paradise. And everything in the Qur’an that is a great reward, a generous reward, and a generous provision is Paradise. And that in His saying, That they will have a great reward, there is an accusative because the good report falls upon it, and that the second is conjoined with it.
17:10: And His statement, And those who do not believe in the Hereafter, God Almighty says: And those who do not believe in the return to God, and do not acknowledge reward and punishment in this world, and therefore do not avoid committing sins against God, We have prepared for them, meaning: We have prepared for them, for their coming before their Lord on the Day of Resurrection, a painful punishment, meaning painful. That is the punishment of Hell.
17:11: God Almighty says, reminding His servants of His hand in their affairs: And a person calls upon evil upon himself, his children, and his wealth, saying: O God, destroy him and curse him when he is annoyed and angry, like his call upon good, saying: Like his call upon his Lord to grant him well-being and safety in himself, his wealth, and his children, saying: So if his call upon evil upon himself, his wealth, and his children were answered as he is answered in his call upon good, he would be destroyed, but God, by His grace, does not answer him in that. And similar to what we have said in that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And man invokes evil as he invokes good, and man is ever hasty, meaning man’s saying, O God, curse him and be angry with him. If that were to be hastened for him as good is hastened for him, he would perish. He said: And it is said, And when harm touches man, he invokes Us lying on his side, or sitting, or standing: that He removes the harm that is afflicting him. God Almighty says, If only he remembered Me and obeyed Me, and followed My command when it is good, as he invokes Me when afflicted, it would be better for him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And man invokes evil as he invokes good, and man is ever hasty, he invokes against his wealth, cursing his wealth and his children, and if God had answered him, He would have destroyed him. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And a person prays for evil as he prays for good. He said: He prays against himself for something that, if answered, he would perish, or against his servant, or against his money. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, “And man invokes evil as he invokes good. And man is ever hasty.” He said: That is man’s invocation of evil for his child and his wife, so he is hasty and invokes evil against them, not wanting it to befall them. There is a difference of opinion regarding the interpretation of His statement, And man is ever hasty. Mujahid and those whose words I have mentioned said: Its meaning is: And man is ever hasty, in invoking what he does not like to be answered for. Others said: What is meant by that is that Adam was hasty when the soul was breathed into him before it had circulated throughout his body, so he wanted to get up, so he described his son as being hasty, because of the haste of their father Adam to get up before his creation was complete. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, that Salman al-Farsi said: The first thing that God created of Adam was his head, and he began to watch while it was being created. He said: His legs remained, and when it was after the afternoon prayer he said: O Lord, hasten before nightfall. That is what He said: And man is ever hasty. Abu Kurayb told us: Uthman bin Saeed told us: Bishr bin Ammarah told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When God breathed into Adam of His spirit, the breath came from his head, and nothing of it ran through his body except that it became flesh and blood. When the breath reached his navel, he looked at his body and was amazed by what he saw of his body, so he went to get up but was unable to. This is the saying of God Almighty: And man is ever hasty. He said: Impatient, he has no patience for ease or hardship.
17:12: God Almighty says: And of His blessings upon you, O people, is the difference between the signs of the night and the signs of the day, by His darkness as a sign of the night, and His light as a sign of the day, so that you may dwell in this, and act in seeking the provision of God that He has decreed for you by His grace in this, and so that you may know by their difference the number of years and their passing, and the beginning of their entry, and the calculation of the hours of the day and night and their times. And We have explained everything in detail. He says: And everything We have explained is healing for you, O people, so that you may thank God for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, and devote worship to Him, not to the gods and idols. God And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, who said: Ibn al-Kaw’a said to Ali: O Commander of the Faithful, what is this spot on the moon? He said: Woe to you! Do you not read the Qur’an: So We erased the verse of the night. This is its erasure. Abu Kurayb told us: Talq told us, on the authority of Zaydah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ali ibn Rabi’ah, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali, saying: What is this blackness in the moon? Ali said: So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible. That is the erasure. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Umar, he said: I was with Ali, and Ibn al-Kawwa asked him about the blackness in the moon? He said: That is the sign of the night that was erased. Ibn Abi Al-Shawareb told us: Yazid bin Zari’ told us: Imran bin Hudayr told us, on the authority of Rafi’ bin Abi Katheer, who said: Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said: Ask whatever you wish. Then Ibn Al-Kawwa’ stood up and said: What is the blackness in the moon? He said: May God kill you! Why did you not ask about your religion and your afterlife? He said: That is the erasure of the night. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Aban Al-Masry told me, he said: Ibn Ufair told us, he said: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Hayy bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Abd Al-Rahman Al-Habli, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-As, that a man said to Ali: What is the blackness in the moon? He said: God says, And We have made the night and the day two signs, and We have erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We made the night and the day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night, he said: It is the darkness of the night. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: The moon used to shine as the sun shines, and the moon is a sign of the night, and the sun is a sign of the day, so We erased the sign of al-Layl 92:the blackness in the moon. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj mentioned, on the authority of Mujahid, in his statement, And We made the night and the day two signs, he said: The sun is a sign of the day, and the moon is a sign of the night. Then We erased the sign of the night, he said: The blackness in the moon, and that is how God created it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Two of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, And We have made the night and the day two signs, he said: Night and day, that is how God created them. Ibn Jurayj said: And Abdullah Ibn Kathir informed us, he said: So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible, he said: The darkness of the night and the veil of the day. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We made the night and the day two signs, and We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day visible: meaning illuminating, and the creation of the sun is more luminous than the moon and greater. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And We have made the night and the day two signs, he said: Night and day, that is how God made them. The Arab scholars differed over the meaning of His statement, And We have made the sign of the day visible, so some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It means: luminous, and likewise His statement, and the day seeing, means: luminous, as if he had gone to the opinion that it was said seeing because it illuminates people’s sight. Others said: Rather, it is from absara’ an-nahar: if people see in it, then he is seeing, like their saying: a cowardly man, if his family and companions are cowards, and a weak man, if his narrators are weak, so likewise the day is seeing, if its people are seeing. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, That you may seek bounty from your Lord. He said: He made for you a long rosary. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We have explained everything in detail: that is, We have clarified it clearly.
17:13: God Almighty says: And every person We have made his omen binding upon him, and he will come to it, whether misery or happiness, by his deeds, around his neck and will never leave it. His statement, We have made his omen binding upon him, is an example of what the Arabs used to take as good omens or bad omens from the occurrences of birds and their departures. So He, the Most High, informed them that every person among them has been made binding upon his omen by his Lord, whether it be bad luck that He has imposed upon him from the bird, or misery that will lead him to a blazing fire, or happiness that will lead him to the Gardens of Eden. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told me, he said: Muadh bin Hisham told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is no contagion and no bad omen, and we have bound every person’s bad omen around his neck. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We have fastened every person’s fate to his neck. He said: The fate is his deeds. He said: The fate is in many things, and among them is the pessimism that people have about one another. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Hussein narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, saying: Ata’ Al-Khurasani informed me, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We have fastened every man’s fate to his neck, he said: His deeds and what he was destined for, so it accompanies him wherever he is, and it disappears with him wherever he goes. Ibn Jurayj said: And he said: His fate is his deeds. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Kathir informed me, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: His deeds and what God has decreed for him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: His bird: his work. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, all on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, And We have fastened every person’s fate to his neck, he said: his deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Wasil ibn Abd al-A'la told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Amr al-Fuqaimi, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And We have fastened the fate of every human being to his neck, he said: No newborn is born except that there is a piece of paper around his neck written on it whether he is wretched or blessed. He said: And I heard him say: Those will receive their share of the Book. He said: It is what was mentioned previously. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We have fastened every person’s fate to his neck: Yes, by God, his happiness and misery are due to his deeds. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: His bird is his action. If someone were to say: How could He say, We fastened his bird to his neck, if the matter is as you have described, and not say, We fastened it to his hands and feet, or other parts of the body? It would be said: Because the neck is the place of marks, necklaces, collars, and other things that adorn or disgrace. So the speech of the Arabs came to attribute the necessary things of the sons of Adam and others to their necks, and they used that so much that they attributed the necessary things of the rest of the bodies to the necks, just as they attributed the crimes of the limbs of the bodies to the hand, so they said: That is because of what his hands earned, even if what he did was his tongue or his private parts. So too is His statement, We fastened his bird to his neck. The reciters differed in their reading of the verse, And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread open. Some of the people of Medina and Mecca, including Nafi’, Ibn Kathir, and the majority of the reciters of Iraq, read it as, And We will bring forth with a nun for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread open,” with a fatha on the ya’ of yalqahu and a light qaf, meaning: And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection, in response to his statement, We have imposed it on him, and We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book of his deeds spread open. Some of the reciters of the people of Ash-Sham agreed with them in their reading of the verse, And We will bring forth and disagreed with them in their saying, he will find it, so they read it as, he will find it, with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the qaf, meaning: And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find, then he will return it to that which did not name its agent, so he said, The human being will find that book spread open. It was mentioned on the authority of Mujahid that: Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to us, saying: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, on the authority of Jarir bin Hazim, on the authority of Hamid, on the authority of Mujahid, that he recited it: And a book will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection. Yazid said: meaning, the bird will bring out a book. I think he recited it with a fat-ha on the ya’, and it is the reading of Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Ibn Muhaisin. It seems that whoever recited this reading directed the interpretation of the statement to: And the bird which We have fastened to the neck of man will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection, and it will become a book which he will read spread out. Some of the people of Madinah recited it with a damma on the ya’, according to the doctrine of what does not specify the agent, and it seems that the meaning of the statement was directed to: And the bird will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection as a book, meaning: And God will bring out that bird which He has made into a book, except that he moved it towards what does not specify the agent. The most correct of the readers in this regard is the reading of those who read it And We will bring forth with a nun and a damma on it, for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out with a ya open and a qaf softened, because the report came before that from God Almighty that He is the One who obligated His creation to do what He obligated from that, so what comes after it is the report from Him, that He is the One who will bring it forth for them on the Day of Resurrection, so that it is with a nun as the report before it was with a nun. As for his saying, He will meet it, then the consensus of the proof from the reciters on the correctness of what we have chosen from the reading in that, and the anomaly of what contradicts it, is sufficient proof for us of the closeness of the meaning of the two readings: I mean the damma and fatha of the ya’ in that, and the shaddah and softness of the qaf in it. So if the correct reading is what we have chosen based on what we have proven, then the interpretation of the statement is: And every human being among you, O company of Adam, We have decreed for him his misfortune and his happiness, his wretchedness and his happiness, according to what has preceded in Our knowledge that he will come to it, and the good and evil that is upon him, so he does not exceed in any of his deeds what We have decreed that he will do, and what We have written for him that he will come to. And We bring out for him, when he comes to Us, a book that he finds spread out with the deeds that he did in this world, and the omen that We have written for him, and which We have bound him to, in which his Lord has counted for him everything that he did in the past in this world. And similar to what we have said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And We will bring out for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out. He said: It is his deeds that he did that were counted against him, so what was written against him of deeds will be brought out for him on the Day of Resurrection and he will find it spread out. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out: meaning his deeds. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, We have fastened his deeds around his neck, he said: his deeds. And We will bring forth for him, he said: We will bring forth that deed, a book which he will find spread wide. Muammar said: Al-Hasan recited, On the right and on the left, seated. O son of Adam, your record has been spread out for you, and two noble angels have been assigned to you, one on your right and the other on your left. The one on your right will record your good deeds. As for the one on your left, he will record your bad deeds. So do what you wish, little or much, until when you die, your record will be put around your neck and placed with you in your grave, until you bring forth on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread wide. “Read your record. Sufficient for you this Day is yourself as a reckoner against you.” God has been just toward you by making you your own reckoner. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: His bird is his work, and we will produce for him a book with that work that he will find spread out. Some of the Arabists interpreted his statement, And We have fastened every man’s fate to his neck, as meaning his share, as in their saying, So-and-so’s share flew with such-and-such, if his share fell on a portion of the portions. Although this statement has merit, the interpretation of the interpreters is as I have explained, and it is not permissible to go beyond what they said in interpreting the Qur’an to something else. However, if what this speaker said meant by his statement his share of work, misery, and happiness, then the meaning of his statement is not far from the meaning of their statement.
17:14: God Almighty says, And We will produce for him on the Day of Resurrection a book which he will find spread out. He will be told, “Read your book. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner.” So He omitted mentioning His saying, We will say to him, being satisfied with the indication of the speech to it. And what He meant by His saying, Read your book is: Read the book of your deeds that you did in the world, which two scribes used to write down, and We will count them against you. Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner. He says, Sufficient is yourself against you this Day as a reckoner. He will count your deeds against you, and He will count them against you. We do not seek any witness against you other than it, and we do not seek any counter against you other than it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Read your record. Sufficient for you today is yourself as accountant against you.” On that day, whoever was not a reader in this world will read.
17:15: God the Almighty says: Whoever adheres to the path of truth and follows it, and that is the religion of God with which He sent His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, is only guided for himself meaning: his adherence to righteousness and his belief in God and His Messenger will not benefit anyone other than himself. And whoever goes astray meaning: whoever deviates from the straight path, and takes a path other than guidance, and disbelieves in God and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and in what he brought from God of the truth, his straying and deviation from guidance will not harm anyone other than himself, because he thereby incurs the wrath of God and His painful punishment.... What He meant by His statement is only to go astray is that he only gains the sin of his straying on his own behalf, not on anyone else. And His statement: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another means, Almighty God the Almighty, and no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another other than herself. He said, And a soul shall bear the burden of another, because its meaning is: And no soul shall bear the burden of another soul. It is said, And I bore such-and-such, and burden is the sin, the plural of burdens, as God Almighty said, But we bore burdens of the adornments of the people, and it is as if the meaning of the statement is: And no soul shall bear the sin of another, but upon every soul is its own sin, not the sin of any other soul. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another, and by God, God does not hold a servant responsible for the sin of another, and He does not punish him except for his deeds. And His statement, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger, God Almighty says: And We never destroy a people except after giving them an excuse through messengers, and establishing proof against them through verses that cut off their excuse. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger, God Almighty does not punish anyone until report from God precedes him, or evidence comes to him from God, and He does not punish anyone except for his sin. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God, the Blessed and Exalted, will gather together the souls of those who died during the interval, the insane, the deaf, the mute, and the old men to whom Islam came and they had become senile. Then He will send a messenger, saying: Enter the Fire. They will say: How can that be, when no messenger has come to us? By God, if they had entered it, it would have been cool and safe for them. Then He will send a messenger to them, and whoever wanted to obey him before will obey him. Abu Hurairah said: Read, if you revile, And We never punish until We have sent a messenger. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Hammam, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, something similar.
17:16: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, We commanded its affluent ones. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read it as we commanded with a shortened alif, without a long one, and with a lightened and open meem. If it is read in this way, then the most common interpretation is: We commanded its affluent ones to obey, but they committed wickedness in it by disobeying God and disobeying His command. Many of those who read it in this way interpreted it in this way. Who said that? Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: We commanded its affluent ones he said: To obey God, but they disobeyed. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Sharik narrated to us, on the authority of Salamah or someone else, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, he said: We commanded obedience, but they disobeyed. It may also be possible, if it is read in this way, that its meaning is: We made them leaders, but they committed corruption in it, because the Arabs say: He is a leader who is not commanded. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: Its meaning, if it is read in this way, may change to the meaning: We made most of its affluent ones. And he used as evidence to correct this the hadith that was narrated on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: The best wealth is a well-mannered mare or a well-trodden path. And he said: The meaning of his saying: well-mannered: is one with many offspring. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Kufa used to reject this from its saying, and they did not accept the meaning of our command in the sense of most of us except by extending the alif from our command. He says about his statement, an ordered mare: It was said that in imitation of the coming of mabourah after it, just as it was said, return visited, not rewarded, so he hamzated ma’zurat for the hamzah of ma’jurat, and it is from wazarat, in imitation of some words with others. Abu Uthman read that as our command with a shaddah on the mim, meaning: the emirate. 22152 - Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Abu Uthman Al-Nahdi, that he read our affair with emphasis on the word emirate. A group of people of interpretation interpreted this statement in this way. Who said that? 22153 - Ali bin Dawud told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, We commanded its affluent ones, meaning: We gave authority to its wicked ones, so they disobeyed therein, and if they did that, We destroyed them with punishment, and this is His statement, And thus We have appointed in every city the greatest of its criminals, that they may plot therein. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: I heard Al-Kisa’i narrating on the authority of Abu Ja’far Al-Razi, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, that he read it as He commanded us and said: He gave us authority. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Hafs, on the authority of Al-Rabi’, on the authority of Abu Al-Aaliyah, he said: Our command is heavy: We made its affluent ones: its arrogant ones. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, We commanded its affluent ones, he said: We sent. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. And it was mentioned on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri that he read it as amrana with an extension of the alif of amrana, meaning: we made most of them so we made them immoral. A group of the people of interpretation directed the interpretation of this letter to this interpretation, except that those who narrated to us did not distinguish for us the difference of the readers in that, and how the interpreters read that, except for a few of them. Those who interpreted that in this way mentioned: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein, meaning: We increase their number. Hanad told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, We commanded its affluent ones, he said: We made them many. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, We commanded its affluent ones, he said: We made them more numerous. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Abd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, We commanded its affluent ones, meaning: Most of us are its affluent ones: meaning its leaders. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein; so the word comes into effect upon it, meaning: We increase its affluent ones, meaning its tyrants, so they defiantly disobey therein and commit acts of disobedience to God. So We destroy it with [complete] destruction. And it was said: And when He desires to destroy it, He increases its affluent ones. 22163 - Muhammad bin Abdul-A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: We commanded its affluent ones he said: We made them more numerous. 22164 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered upon Zaynab one day and he was saying: There is no god but God. Woe to the Arabs from an evil that has drawn near. Today a hole has been opened in the barrier of Gog and Magog like this, and he made a circle between his thumb and the one next to it. She said: O Messenger of God, will we perish while there are righteous people among us? He said: Yes, if evil increases. 22165 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And when We desire to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defiantly disobey therein, he said: Some of the people of knowledge mentioned that We command: We increase. He said: The Arabs say about something that is abundant, Amr common, because of its abundance. But if a people are described as having become numerous, then it is said: Banu so-and-so commanded, and the people commanded an affair, and that is when they became numerous and their affair became great, as Labid said: If they are angered, they will be lowered, and if they are commanded one day, they will become weak and exhausted. The imperative is the source, and the imperative noun, as God Almighty said: You have certainly done something terrible. He said: Great, and it was said in a similar verse: evil, meaning a lot. The most correct reading in my opinion is the reading of those who read amrana mutrafeeha with a shortened alif in amrana and a lightened meem, because the authoritative readers unanimously agreed to correct it and not any other. If that is the most correct reading, then the most correct interpretation of it is the interpretation of those who interpreted it: We commanded its people to obey, but they disobeyed and committed wickedness therein. So the word was justified against them, because the most common meaning of our command is the command, which is the opposite of the prohibition and nothing else. And directing the meanings of the words of God, may He be glorified, to the most famous and well-known of its meanings is more deserving of finding a way to it than anything else. The meaning of His statement, So they disobeyed therein is: they disobeyed God’s command therein and went out of His obedience. So the word came into effect upon it means: it became incumbent upon them because of their disobedience to God and their disobedience therein, and the threat of God that He threatened those who disbelieved in Him and disobeyed His messengers, of destruction after the excuse and warning through the messengers and proofs. So We destroyed it with complete destruction means: so We destroyed it with complete destruction, and We destroyed whoever was in it from its people with complete destruction, as Al-Farazdaq said: And they were like the firstborn of Thamud when he roared at noon and destroyed them completely.
17:17: This is a threat from God, the Most High, to the polytheists of Quraysh who denied His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a threat to them with punishment, and an announcement from Him that if they do not stop what they are doing of denying His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, then He will bring down upon them His wrath and punishment as He brought down upon the nations before them who followed the path of disbelief in God and the denial of His Messengers. God, the Most High, says: And We have destroyed, O people, before you, from after Noah until your time, many generations who denied the signs of God, disbelieved in Him, and denied His Messengers, as you are doing, and you are not more honorable to God than they are, because there is no connection between anyone and God, the Most High, so He punishes some people in a way He does not punish others, or He pardons the sins of some people and punishes others for them. God the Almighty says: “Then turn to the obedience of God, your Lord. We have sent to you a Messenger who will alert you to Our proofs against you and awaken you from your heedlessness. We would never punish a people until We send to them a Messenger alerting them to the proofs of God, while you persist in your transgression. And sufficient is your Lord, O Muhammad, as Knower of the sins of His servants.” He says: And God is sufficient for you, O Muhammad, as Knower of the sins of His creation, for nothing of the actions of these polytheists of your people, or the actions of others of His creation, is hidden from Him. He is All-Knowing, All-Aware, and All-Seeing of all that. He says: He sees all of that, so nothing of it is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom on the earth or in the heavens is hidden from Him, nor anything smaller or larger than that. There is disagreement about the length of a century. Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Abu Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, he said: The century is one hundred and twenty years, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent in the first century, and the last of them was Yazid bin Muawiyah. And others said: Rather, it is one hundred years. Who said that? Hassan bin Muhammad bin Abdul Rahman Al-Himsi Abu Al-Salt Al-Ta’i told us: Salamah bin Hawas told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Qasim, on the authority of Abdullah bin Busr Al-Mazini, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, placed his hand on his head and said: This boy will live for a century. I said: How long is a century? He said: One hundred years. Hassan bin Muhammad told us: Salamah bin Hawas told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Al-Qasim, who said: We continued to count for him until he was one hundred years old, then he died. Abu Al-Salt said: Salamah told me that this Muhammad bin Al-Qasim was the son-in-law of Abdullah bin Busr. Others said about that as follows: Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari narrated to us, saying: Omar bin Shakir narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The century is forty years. And his saying, And your Lord is sufficient for you, the preposition Ba was inserted in his saying, And your Lord is sufficient for you, and it is in the nominative case, because the meaning of the statement is: And your Lord is sufficient for you, and your Lord is sufficient for you as an expert on the sins of His servants, indicating praise. And the Arabs do the same in every statement that has the meaning of praise or, they insert the preposition Ba in the noun and the noun that the preposition is inserted in the nominative case to indicate by its insertion praise or blame, like their saying: He honored a man with him, and he is sufficient for you as a man, and he was generous with your garment, and he tasted good food, and similar statements. And if the preposition Ba was dropped from what it enters from these nouns, it would be in the nominative case, because it is in the nominative case, as the poet said: And he tells me about the absent man, his gift is sufficient as a gift for what the absent man tells me. If there is no praise or blame in the speech, then they do not include the preposition ba. It is not permissible to say: Your brother stood up, and you mean: Your brother stood up, unless you mean: Another man stood up with him, and that is a meaning other than the first meaning.
17:18: God Almighty says: Whoever seeks the immediate world and works and strives for it, and seeks it, has no certainty of the afterlife, and does not hope for reward or punishment from his Lord for his work, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We will. He says: God hastens for him in this world what He wills of the expansion of this world for him, or its stinginess for whomever God wills to do that to him, or his destruction with whatever punishments He wills. Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn. He says: Then We will cast him into Hell when he comes to Us in the Hereafter, censured for his lack of gratitude to Us, and his bad deeds in what we have done to him in this world, rejected. He says: banished: cast out in the Fire. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whomever We intend, meaning: Whoever’s concern, his obsession, his desire, and his intention is the world, God hastens for him therein what he desires, then He forces him to Hell. He said, Then We have made for him Hell, which he will burn, censured and banished, censured in God’s blessing, banished in God’s wrath. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Taybah, a sheikh from the people of Misisa, told me that he heard Abu Ishaq Al-Fazari say: We hastened for him in it what We will for whomever We will. He said: For whomever We will, His destruction. Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying blameworthy means: blameworthy. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will for whom We intend, he said: The immediate is the world.
17:19: God the Most High says: Whoever desires the Hereafter and seeks it, and for it he works its work, which is obedience to God and what pleases Him. He added striving to the ha and the alif, which is a metaphor for the Hereafter, so He said: And strives for the Hereafter with the striving of the Hereafter, and its meaning is: And does its work for it so that the listeners know the meaning of that, and that its meaning is: And strives for it with his striving for it and he is a believer, he says: He is a believer who believes in God's reward and His great recompense for his striving for it, not denying it as one who desires the immediate, God the Most High says: Then those meaning: whoever does that their striving meaning their work in obedience to God will be appreciated and God's thanks to them for their striving is His good reward for their good deeds, and His overlooking of their bad deeds with His mercy. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever desires the Hereafter and strives for it with the necessary effort while he is a believer - for those, their effort is ever appreciated, God will appreciate their good deeds and overlook their bad deeds.
17:20: God Almighty says: Your Lord, O Muhammad, provides for both groups of those who desire this worldly life and those who desire the Hereafter, the one who strives for it as he should, and he is a believer in this world, from His gift. He provides for them both from His gift until they reach their term and complete the appointed time that was written for them. Then their conditions differ after death, and they are separated after reaching the sources. The group of those who desire this worldly life is Hell as their source, and the group of those who desire the Hereafter is Paradise as their destination. And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden. He says: And the gift of your Lord, which He gives to whomever He wills of His creation in this world, is not forbidden to whomever He extends it to. None of His creation is able to prevent him from that, and God has given it to him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr ibn Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “To both We provide from the bounty of your Lord. And the bounty of your Lord is not restricted,” meaning diminished. And God Almighty divided the world between the righteous and the wicked, and the Hereafter is especially with your Lord for the righteous. Muhammad Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the gift of your Lord is not restricted. He said: It is diminished. Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Mukhrami told us: Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us: Sahl bin Abi Al-Salt Al-Siraj told us: I heard Al-Hasan say: We give to both these and those from the bounty of your Lord. He said: We give to both the righteous and the wicked from this world. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: On the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Ibn Abbas said: Whoever desires the immediate, We hasten for him therein what We will. The verse: And whoever desires the Hereafter. Then He said: To both We provide from the gift of your Lord. Ibn Abbas said: He provides for whoever desires this world, and He provides for whoever desires the Hereafter. Ibn Jurayj said: And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden. He said: It is forbidden. Bishr told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, To both We provide, these and those, the people of this world and the people of the Hereafter, “from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden,” he said: forbidden. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, No, We provide for these and those, the people of this world and the people of the Hereafter, “from the gift of your Lord. And the gift of your Lord is not forbidden,” from the righteous or the wicked, he said: And the forbidden: the prohibited, and he read: See how We have preferred some of them over others, and the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in preference.
17:21: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart at these two groups, one of which is the immediate home, which he seeks and works for, and the other which wants the Hereafter and strives for it, certain of God’s reward for its striving. How did We give preference to one group over the other, by Our sight, which guided it to the path that is most upright, and made easy for it that which is most rightly guided and most correct, and We let down this other group, so We led it astray from the path of truth, and covered its sight from the path of right guidance. And the Hereafter is greater in degrees. He says: And the group of those who desire the Hereafter is greater in degrees in the Hereafter than the others, due to the difference in their stations according to their deeds in Paradise, and greater in preference by God’s preference of some of them over others than these other group in this world in what We have expanded for them in it. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, See how We have favored some of them over others: meaning in this world. And the Hereafter has greater degrees and greater preference. And the believers have mansions in Paradise, because they have virtues due to their deeds. And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: There is a degree between the highest and lowest of the people of Paradise like a star that is seen in the middle and middle of the earth.
17:22: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, do not make a partner with God in His divinity and worship, but be sincere in worshipping Him and single out divinity for Him, for there is no god but Him. If you make a god other than Him and worship other than Him, will you become blameworthy? He says: You will be blamed for what you have neglected in thanking God for the blessings He has bestowed upon you, and for making thanks to someone other than the one who has done you good, and for associating in praise someone with whom no one else has shared in the blessings upon you, you will be forsaken. Your Lord has surrendered you to someone who wants to harm you, and if your Lord, who is the supporter of His friends, surrenders you, then you will have no protector other than Him to support you and defend you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Do not make with God another god, lest you sit down blamed and forsaken, he said: blamed in God’s blessings. And even though this statement was addressed to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it is intended for all of God’s servants who are obligated to perform duties, the Exalted and Majestic.
17:23: By this, the Most High means: Your Lord, O Muhammad, has decreed that you worship none but God, for none but Him should be worshipped. The interpreters of the Qur’an have differed in their interpretation of His statement, And your Lord has decreed, even though the meaning of all of them is the same. Mention what they said about that: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Sarawiya told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him. He said: He commanded. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Zakariya bin Salam told us: A man came to Al-Hasan and said: He divorced his wife three times. He said: You disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has left you. The man said: Did God decree that for me? Al-Hasan, who was eloquent, said: What did God decree? What did God command. And he recited this verse: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him. The people said: Al-Hasan has spoken about predestination. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him: meaning, your Lord has commanded that you worship none but Him, so this is the immediate decree of God. And it was said in some wisdom: He who pleases his parents has pleased his Creator, and he who angers his parents has angered his Lord. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. He said: He commanded that you worship none but Him. In the wording of Ibn Mas’ud, Your Lord has commanded that you worship none but Him. Abu Kuraib told us: Yahya bin Isa told us: Nasir bin Abi Al-Ash’ath told us: Ibn Habib bin Abi Thabit told us, on the authority of his father: Ibn Abbas gave me a copy of the Qur’an and said: This is according to the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka’b. Abu Kuraib said: Yahya said: I saw the Qur’an with Nasir, in which was And your Lord has commanded meaning: And your Lord has decreed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him. He said: And your Lord has commanded. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, he said: He commanded that you worship none but Him. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq Al-Kufi, on the authority of Al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, that he read it as And your Lord has commanded, and he said: They attached the waw to the sad, so it became a qaf. And His statement, And to parents, do good, means: And He has commanded you to do good to your parents, that you be good to them and be dutiful to them. The meaning of the statement is: And He has commanded you to do good to your parents. So when the an was deleted, the decree is connected to the good, as is said in the statement: He commanded you to do good to him, and I advise you to do good to him, meaning: I command you to do good to him, then the an is deleted, so the command and the advice are connected to the good, as the poet said: I was amazed at Dahma when he complained about us, and at Abu Dahma when he advised us to do good. It was as if we were dry And he recommended us to do good. The reciters differed in their reading of the statement, Either one of them or both of them reach old age with you. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the reciters of Kufa, read it as either they reach old age in the singular, directing that to one of them because one of them is one, so they made yubulghan singular because of its singularity, and made his statement, or both of them conjoined with the one. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as either they reach old age in the dual, with the kasra and shaddah of the noon, and they said: The parents were mentioned before, and his statement they reach old age is a report about them after he mentioned their names. They said: When the verb comes after the noun, the statement is to be evidence that it is a report about two or a group. They said: The evidence that it is a report about two in the future verb is the alif and the noon. They said: His statement, one of them or both of them is a renewed statement, as was said: So they became blind and deaf, then God forgave them, then And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age with you, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them but speak to them a generous word. many of them became blind and deaf and like his statement, And they whispered a secret: then he began and said, Those who wronged. The first of the two readings that is more correct in my opinion is the reading of the one who reads it Either they attain old age with the singular as report about one of them, because the report about the command to be kind to parents ended with His statement And to parents, do good and then He began with His statement Either one of them or both of them attain old age with you. And His statement So say not to them a word of disrespect means: Do not be disgusted by something that you see from one of them or both of them that people are offended by, but be patient with that from them, and expect reward for your patience with them, just as they were patient with you when you were young. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Muhammad bin Muhibb told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And do not say to them a word of disrespect, nor repel them, he said: If they reach such old age in your life that they urinate and defecate, do not say to them a word of disrespect, to disgust them. Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: If they reach old age with you, do not say to them uff when you see something offensive, and remove pee and toilet from them, as they used to remove it from you when you were young, and do not harm them. The people of knowledge of the Arabic language differed about the meaning of uff. Some of them said: Its meaning is: everything that is coarse and ugly in speech. Others said: Uff is the dirt of the fingernails, and uff is everything that you lift with your hand from the ground of something insignificant. The Arabs have six dialects for raising the letter af with tanween and without tanween, lowering it and making it accusative. Those who lowered it with tanween, which is the general reading of the people of Medina, likened it to sounds that have no meaning, like when they say in the story of a sound ghaq ghaq, so they lowered the qaf and added a nun to it, and its rule was sukun, because nothing can make it sukun because it comes after a silent letter, which is the alif. They hated to combine two silent letters, so they moved it to the closest vowel to sukun, which is kasra, because when a jussive letter is moved, it is only moved to kasra. As for those who lowered it without tanween, which is the general reading of the readers of Kufa and Basra, they said: They only include tanween in sounds that come incomplete, like that which comes with two letters like mah, “sah,” and bakh, so it is completed with tanween because it is incomplete in the structures of nouns. They said: And af is complete, and we do not need to complete it with anything else, because it came with three letters. They said: We only broke the second fa so that we do not combine two silent letters. As for the one who added a damma and a noon, he said: It is a noun like all other nouns that are declined but do not have a sound, and he deviated from the sounds with it. As for the one who added it without a tanween, he said: It is not a proper noun, so it is declined like the proper nouns. They said: We add it as we add the word God’s is the matter before and after and as we add the noun in a singular vocative, so we say: O Zayd. And whoever puts it in the accusative without a tanween, which is the reading of some of the Meccans and the people of Syria, he likens it to their saying: Extend, O this one, and return. And whoever puts it in the accusative with a tanween, he has made the verb work on it and made it a proper noun, so he says: I did not say to him: Afa nor tafa. And some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: It was read: Af, and Afa is a language that they made like its description. And some of them read Af, and that is because some of the Arabs say: Af laka on the narration: meaning do not say this to them. He said: And raising is ugly, because it is not followed by a lam, and those who said: Af, many broke it, and that is better. And some of them broke the noon.
