Some of them said: Afi, as if he added this statement to himself, so he said: Afi this for you both, and the broken form of this has a tanween and without a tanween, as it is an incomplete noun, such as ams and the like, and the open form without a tanween is the same. Some of the Arabists said: All of these six movements are included in af a, as a way of resembling the noun at one time and the sound at another. He said: The sounds are mostly broken with the tanween if they are on two letters, such as sah and mah and bakh. And if they are on three letters, they are likened to the tools af “m’il”: layt and madd, and af like madd is like the tools. And if he said af like sah. And they said I heard mad, ya hana and mad. And it was narrated from Al-Kisa’i that he said: I heard what your family taught you except mad and mad, and this is like if and if. And whoever said afa made it like sahqan and ba’d. What is more correct in my opinion in reading this is the reading of the one who read it fa-la-quluhu-u-fa with a kasra on the fa’ without a tanween for two reasons: One of them is that it is the most famous of the languages in it and the most eloquent among the Arabs, and the second is that the portion of every word that does not have an inflected object is sukoon, so since that was the case. And the portion of the fa’ in af was to stop, then there was no way for that to happen because of the two quiescent letters coming together in it. And the rule for a quiescent letter when it is moved is that it is moved to a kasra, so it is moved to a kasra, as it was said: mad and shadd: and ward of the door. And His saying: And do not scold them, God Almighty says: And do not rebuke them. Muhammad bin Ismail Al-Ahmasi told us: Muhammad bin Ubaid told us: Wasil Al-Raqashi told us, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, regarding his statement, So do not say to them a word of disrespect, nor repel them, he said: Do not shake your hand against your parents. It is said from this: he rebuked him, he rebuked him, he rebuked him, he rebuked him. As for his saying, And speak to them a noble word, He, the Most High, says: And speak to them a beautiful, good word. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And speak to them a generous word. He said: The best word you can find. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Hussein narrated to us, he said: Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman narrated to us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhtar, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Umar bin Al-Khattab, A noble word. They said: Do not refrain from anything they want. Abu Ja`far said: This hadith is wrong, I mean the hadith of Hisham bin Urwah. Rather, it is on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father. It does not include Umar. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Ulayyah and others, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhtar. Bishr bin Muadh told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And speak to them a noble word: meaning, a gentle, easy word. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Harmalah ibn Imran told me, on the authority of Abu al-Haddaj al-Tahbibi, he said: I said to Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: Everything that God Almighty mentioned in the Qur’an about being kind to one’s parents, I have understood, except His saying: And speak to them a generous word. What is this generous word? Ibn al-Musayyab said: The words of a sinful servant to a rude master.
17:24: God Almighty says: And be submissive to them out of mercy from you towards them. Obey them in what they command you to do that is not disobedience to God, and do not disobey them in what they like. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, he said: Do not refrain from anything they love. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Al-Ashja’i told us, he said: I heard Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, he said: It means that you are gentle with them so that you do not refuse them anything that they love. Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Abdul Hakam told me: Ayoub bin Suwaid told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, he said: Do not refrain from something they love. Yaqoub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Al-Mukhtar, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, he said: It is that you do not refrain from anything they want. Abu Kuraib narrated: Al-Muqri’ Abu Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, on the authority of Harmalah ibn Imran, on the authority of Abu al-Hudaj, who said: I said to Saeed ibn al-Musayyab: What does his statement, And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy, mean? He said: Have you not seen the words of the sinful slave to the rude and harsh master? Humiliation, with a damma on the dhal, and humiliation are two sources of the verb dhaleel, which means to humble oneself, and there is no one who is humbled in creation from the saying of the speaker: I have humbled myself to you, humiliated and humbled. This is similar to qal and qal, if you drop the ha’, you add a dhammah on the dhal from humiliation, and the qaf from qal, and if you keep the ha’, you make a kasrah on the dhal from humiliation, and the qaf from qal, because al-A’sha said: I was not a little girl before that He means: paucity. As for humiliation with the breaking of the dhal and the dropping of the ha, it is a source of humiliation from their saying: a docile animal: clearly humiliated, and that is if it is soft and not difficult. And from this is the saying of God, the Most High, It is He who made the earth docile for you, which includes humiliation, as He, the Most High, said: So follow the ways of your Lord docilely. And Mujahid interpreted that to mean that the place she followed would not be difficult for her. The readers differed in reading this. The majority of the readers of Hijaz, Iraq and Syria read it as and lower to them the wing of humility with a damma on the dhal, as a source of humiliation. Saeed bin Jubair and Asim al-Jahdari read it as wing of humiliation with a kasra on the dhal. Ibn Hamid told us: Bahz bin Asad told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he recited: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. He said: Be humble to them, but do not be humble to them. Nasr bin Ali told us, he said: Omar bin Shaqiq told me, he said: I heard Asim Al-Jahdary reciting: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. He said: Be humble to them, but do not be humble to them. Ibn Bashar told us: Omar bin Shaqiq told us, on the authority of Asim, similarly. Abu Ja`far said: According to this interpretation that Asim interpreted, it should have been read with a damma on the dhal, not a kasra. Nasr and Ibn Bashar told us, and I was told by Al-Farra’, who said: Hisham told me, on the authority of Abu Bishr Ja’far Ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id Ibn Jubayr, that he recited: And lower to them the wing of humiliation. Al-Farra’ said: Al-Hakam Ibn Zuhair informed me, on the authority of Asim Ibn Abi Al-Najud, that he also recited it as humiliation, so I asked Abu Bakr and he said: Asim recited it as humiliation. As for his saying, And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small,’ he is saying: Ask God for mercy for your parents, and say, My Lord, have mercy upon them, and be kind to them with Your forgiveness and mercy, as they were kind to me when I was small, and had mercy on me and brought me up when I was small, until I became independent and no longer needed them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, Qan told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.’ This is how you have learned, and this is how you have been commanded. Take the teachings and manners of God. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out one day with his hands outstretched and his voice raised saying: Whoever finds his parents or one of them and then enters the Fire after that, God will distance him and crush him. But they saw that it was from being dutiful to his parents, and there was in it the slightest piety, for that is the extent of his great goodness. A group of the people of knowledge said: The statement of God, may He be glorified and exalted: And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.’ is abrogated by His statement: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives, after it has become clear to them that they are companions of the Fire. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying, And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.’ Then God Almighty revealed after this, It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said in Surat Bani Israel: If one or both of them reach old age with you... until His saying: And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.’ Then it was abrogated by the verse in Bara’ah: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists, even if they were relatives. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said, Ibn Abbas said: And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them both.’ He said: It was abrogated by the verse in Bara’ah: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists. This verse may be interpreted as general in meaning to all fathers, without the meaning of abrogation, so that its interpretation is specific, and the meaning of the statement is: And say, My Lord, have mercy upon them if they are believers, just as they brought me up [when I was] young. So it is intended to be specific, as we said, and nothing of it is abrogated. And what he meant by his statement brought me up is: gave me growth. Fourteenth: The Almighty said: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy. This is a metaphor for compassion and mercy towards them and humility towards them is the humility of the subjects to the prince and the slaves to the masters, as Saeed bin Al-Musayyab indicated. He gave the lowering of the wing and raising it as an example of the wing of a bird when it raises its wings for its child. Humility is softness. The majority read it with a damma on the dhal, from dhala yadhil dhalan wa dhalah wa dhalah, so it is dhaal and dhaleel. Saeed bin Jubayr, Ibn Abbas, and Urwah bin Az-Zubayr read dhaal with a kasra on the dhal, and it was narrated from Asim, from their saying: a docile animal with humility in it. Humility in animals is easy and submissive, not difficult. So, by virtue of this verse, a person should make himself with his parents in the best humility, in his words, his stillness, and his looks, and he should not fix his gaze on them, for that is the look of an angry person. Fifteenth: The address in this verse is to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by that is his nation, since he, peace be upon him, did not have parents at that time. Humiliation was not mentioned in the Almighty’s saying: And lower your wing to those who follow you among the believers. It was mentioned here according to the greatness of the truth and its emphasis. The word min in His saying min (of mercy) is to clarify the type, meaning that this lowering is from the mercy hidden in the soul, not that it is used. It is correct that the end is the goal, then the Almighty commanded His servants to have mercy on their fathers and to pray for them, and to have mercy on them as they had mercy on you, and to be gentle with them as they were gentle with you, when they took care of you when you were young, ignorant and in need and preferred you over themselves, and stayed up all night while they were hungry and they fed you, and they were naked and they clothed you, so you will not be sufficient for them unless they reach the same age as you were young, then you will take from them what they took from you, and then they will have the advantage of precedence. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A child cannot repay his father unless he finds him a slave, buys him, and frees him. This hadith will be discussed in Surah Maryam. Sixteenth: The Almighty’s statement: As they brought me up. He specifically mentioned upbringing so that the servant would remember the compassion and effort of his parents in raising him, and this would increase his compassion for them and tenderness towards them. All of this applies to the believing parents. The Qur’an has forbidden asking forgiveness for dead polytheists, even if they were relatives, as mentioned above. It was mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Qatadah that all of this was abrogated by His statement: It is not for the Prophet and those who have believed to ask forgiveness for the polytheists... until His statement: the companions of Hellfire. The Muslim’s parents were dhimmis, so he used with them what God commanded him here, except asking for mercy for them after their death in disbelief, because this alone was abrogated by the aforementioned verse. It was said: This is not a place for abrogation, as it is a supplication for worldly mercy for the polytheist parents as long as they are alive, as mentioned above. Or the generality of this verse may be specific to that, not mercy for the Hereafter, especially since it was said that His statement: And say, ‘My Lord, have mercy upon them.’ It was revealed about Sa`d ibn Abi Waqqas, who converted to Islam and his mother threw herself into the hot sand, naked. This was mentioned to Sa`d, who said: May you die. So the verse was revealed. It was said: The verse is specific to supplication for Muslim parents. The correct view is that it is general, as we have mentioned. Ibn Abbas said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Whoever spends the night pleasing his parents and wakes up, he will spend the night and wake up with two open doors to Paradise, one after the other. Whoever spends the night and wakes up displeasing his parents, he will spend the night and wake up with two open doors to Hellfire, one after the other. A man said: O Messenger of God, even if they wronged him? He said: Even if they wronged him, even if they wronged him, even if they wronged him. We have narrated with a continuous chain of transmission on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man came to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, my father has taken my money. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to the man: Bring your father to me. Gabriel (peace be upon him) came down to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: God the Almighty sends you His peace and says to you: When an old man comes to you, ask him about something he said to himself that your ears have not heard. When the old man came, the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What is wrong with your son that he complains about? Do you want to take his money? He said: Ask him, O Messenger of God, should I spend it on anyone but one of his paternal aunts or my own self? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: Okay, let us leave this. Tell me about something you said to yourself that your ears have not heard. The old man said: By God, O Messenger of God, God the Almighty has continued to increase our certainty in you. I said something to myself that my ears have not heard. He said: And I was listening. I said: I fed you as a newborn and gave you birth as a young man, learning from what I bestowed upon you and drinking from it. If one night I am sick, I will not spend the night without eating your food, except awake, tossing and turning. As if I am the one who was knocked on without you by what you knocked on without me, so my eyes are neglectful My soul fears death for you, and it knows that death is a postponed time. When I reached the age and the goal that I had hoped for in you You made my punishment harsh and rude, as if you were the generous benefactor. If only you had not respected my fatherhood, you would have done as the neighbor next door does. You gave me the rights of neighborliness and were not stingy with me with money other than yours. He said: Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took hold of his son’s collar and said: You and your wealth belong to your father. Al-Tabarani said: Al-Lahmi does not narrate this hadith from Ibn Al-Munkadir in this complete form and with this verse except with this chain of transmission, and Ubayd God ibn Khalsa is the only one who narrated it. And God knows best.
17:25: God Almighty says, Your Lord O people, knows more than you what is in your souls of your veneration of your fathers and mothers and your honoring them, and your righteousness towards them, and what is in it of believing in belittling their rights, and disobeying them, and other than that from the secrets of your hearts, nothing of that is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for the good and bad of that, so beware of harboring evil towards them, and concluding disobedience towards them. And His statement, if you are righteous means: if you correct your intentions towards them, and obey God in what He has commanded you to do of being righteous towards them, and fulfilling their rights upon you, after a slip-up on your part, or a mistake in an obligation upon them, while fulfilling what He has obligated you in other than that of His obligations, then He is Forgiving to those who turn back after the slip-up, and those who repent after the mistake. And in a similar manner to what we said in the interpretation of that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abu Kuraib said: Ibn Idris told us: I heard my father and my uncle on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, Your Lord knows best what is in your souls. He said: The initiative is from a man to his parents, intending nothing but good by that, so he said, Your Lord knows best what is in your souls. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Ibn Idris told us: My father told me, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us, he said: Amr told us, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, regarding his statement, For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. He said: He is the man who hastens to his parents and in his intention and heart is that he will not be held accountable. The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of his statement, For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. Some of them said: They are those who glorify Him. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Muhammad ibn al-Salt told us: Abu Kudayna told us. Ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz told me: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Ashqar told us: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn to Him. He said: Those who glorify God. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abu Khaithama Zuhair told us, he said: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abu Maysarah, on the authority of Amr bin Shurahbil, he said: The one who repents is the one who glorifies God. And others said: They are the obedient and doers of good. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn to Him, meaning: to the obedient and righteous. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, For He is Forgiving to those who turn back to Him, he said: They are the obedient and the people of prayer. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: For He is Forgiving to those who turn to Him. He said: To those who are obedient and pray. Others said: Rather, they are those who pray between Maghrib and Isha. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, on the authority of Abu Sakhr Hamid bin Ziyad, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. He said: The prayer is between sunset and night prayers. Others said: They are those who pray the Duha prayer. Who said that? Amr bin Ali told us, he said: Rabah Abu Sulayman Al-Raqqa’ told us, he said: I heard Awn Al-Uqayli say about this verse, For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn to Him. He said: Those who pray the Duha prayer. Others said: Rather, he is the one who returns from his sin and repents from it. Who said that? Asmad bin Al-Walid Al-Qurashi told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, that he said regarding this verse, For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back to Him. He said: The one who commits a sin and then repents, then commits a sin and then repents. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sulayman bin Dawud told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: He is the one who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents in this verse: For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. Mujahid bin Musa told us: Yazid told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us that he heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab being asked about this verse: For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. He said: He is the one who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Jarir bin Hazim told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, something similar. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, in a similar manner. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Malik told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, For He was Forgiving to those who turn to Him. He said: He is the servant who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Al-Layth bin Saad told me, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, he said: I heard Saeed bin Al-Musayyab say, and he mentioned something similar. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri and Muammar told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Ibn al-Musayyab, who said: The one who repents is the one who sins and then repents, then sins and then repents, then sins and then repents. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse, For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back to Him, he said: Those who return to goodness. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad, Abu Dawud, and Hisham told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Abu Bishr, Saeed bin Jubair, in a similar manner. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, and Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, all of them on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Umair, For He is Forgiving to those who turn to Him. He said: The one who remembers his sins in the toilet, and seeks forgiveness from God for them. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The one who constantly repents is the one who remembers his sins in the privacy and seeks forgiveness from God for them. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, that he said regarding this verse, Indeed, He is Forgiving to those who turn back to Him. He said: He who remembers his sin and then repents. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty, Forgiving to those who turn back, he said: Those who turn back are those who return and repent. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Ibn Jurayj said, on the authority of Yahya ibn Saeed, on the authority of Saeed ibn Al-Musayyab: A man commits a sin and then repents three times. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, regarding his statement, For He is Forgiving to those who turn back to Him. He said: He who remembers his sins and seeks forgiveness from God for them. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Shuraih told me, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Muslim, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, that he said regarding His statement, For He is ever Forgiving to those who turn back [to Him], the servant sins and then repents, so God accepts his repentance. Then he sins and repents, so God accepts his repentance. Then he sins a third time, and if he repents, God accepts his repentance with a repentance that will not be erased. It was narrated on the authority of Ubaid bin Umair, other than the statement we mentioned on the authority of Mujahid, which is: Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muhammad bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Amr bin Dinar, on the authority of Ubayd bin Umair, regarding His statement, For He is, to those who turn back [to Him], Forgiving. He said: We used to consider the one who turns back to Him to be the Preserver, who says: O God, forgive me for what I have done in this gathering of mine. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The one who repents is the one who repents from sin, who returns from disobeying God to obeying Him, and from what he dislikes to what pleases Him, because the one who repents is only an action, from the saying of the one who says: So-and-so returned from such-and-such, either from his journey to his home, or from one state to another, as Ubayd ibn al-Abrash said: Everyone who is absent will return, but the one who is absent from death will not return. He is a man who returns from his journey and repents from his sins.
17:26: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his saying, And give to the near of kin. Some of them said: What is meant by it is the relatives of the deceased on his father’s and mother’s side. God, the Most High, commanded His servants to maintain ties with them. Who said that? Imran bin Musa told us: Abdul-Warith bin Saeed told us: Habib al-Mu’allim told us: A man asked al-Hasan: Should I give my relatives the zakat of my wealth? He said: They have a right to it other than the zakat. Then he recited this verse: And give the relative his right. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, And give the relative his right, he said: The connection that you want to make with him is what you wanted to do for him. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And give the relative his right, and [also] the needy and the traveler, he said: It is to maintain ties with the relative and the needy and to be good to the traveler. Others said: Rather, it refers to the relatives of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Amara Al-Asadi told me: Ismail bin Abaan told us: Al-Sabah bin Yahya Al-Muzni told us, on the authority of Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Al-Daylam, who said: Ali bin Al-Hussein, peace be upon them both, said to a man from the people of Ash-Sham: Have you read the Qur’an? He said: Yes. He said: Have you not read in the Children of Israel: And give the relative his right? He said: And you are the relatives whom God, the Most High, has commanded to be given his right? He said: Yes. The first of the two interpretations, in my opinion, is the correct interpretation, the interpretation of those who interpreted it as meaning God’s commandment to His servants to maintain ties of kinship with their own fathers and mothers, and that is because God Almighty followed that with His urging His servants to be dutiful to fathers and mothers, so it is obligatory that it be an urging to maintain ties of kinship with their own, not with the kinship of others that were not mentioned. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: And, O Muhammad, give your relative his right of maintaining ties with him, being dutiful to him, and showing kindness to him, and that was presented in the form of an address to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and what is meant by its ruling is all those upon whom God’s obligations are obligatory. This is indicated by his beginning the commandment with the words of God Almighty: “And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one of them reaches old age while you are alive,” so he directed the address with his words And your Lord has decreed to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then he said that you worship none but Him, so he returned the address to everyone, then he diverted the address with his words Whether they reach old age while you are alive to singling him out. The meaning of all of this is all those who are bound by the duties of God Almighty. The address was directed specifically to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, or it was directed to him and all of his nation. His statement, and the needy, which is the weak among the needy. We have previously demonstrated the meaning of the needy in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. His statement, and the wayfarer, means the stranded traveler. God Almighty says: Keep in touch with your relatives, so give them their right from your connection with them. And the needy one who is in need, and the one passing by you who is stranded, so help him and strengthen him to complete his journey. And it has been said: What is meant by the command to give the wayfarer his right is that he be hosted for three days. The first statement is more correct in my opinion, because God Almighty did not specify one of His rights over another in His Book, nor on the tongue of His Messenger. This is general in every right He has, that He should be given hospitality, a load, or assistance on his journey. And His statement, And do not squander wastefully, means: And do not squander, O Muhammad, what God has given you of wealth - in disobeying Him. The root of squandering is to squander in extravagance, and from this the poet said: People who sheltered us, but their shelter was a storm of Iraq’s profligate debauchery. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaidin, who said: Abdullah said regarding his statement, And do not squander wastefully, he said: Squandering is not right, which is extravagance. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Muslim al-Batin, on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, who said: Abdullah was asked about the spendthrift, and he said: Spending without right. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: I heard Yahya ibn al-Jazzar narrating on the authority of Abu al-Ubaydayn, the blind man, that Abdullah ibn Mas`ud was asked about this verse: And do not spend wastefully. He said: Spending money in ways other than its rightful use. Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Yahya bin Al-Jazzar, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, on the authority of Abdullah, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam Ibn Utaybah, on the authority of Yahya Ibn Al-Jazzar, that Abu Al-Ubaydayn was blind. He asked Ibn Mas’ud, saying: What is extravagance? He said: Spending money in a way that is not right. Khallad bin Aslam told us: Al-Nadr bin Shumayl told us: Al-Mas’udi told us: Salamah bin Kuhayl told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, and he had a period of time, and Abdullah knew that about him, so he said: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, what is extravagance? And he mentioned something similar. Ahmad bin Mansour Al-Ramadi told us, he said: Abu Al-Hawb told us, on the authority of Ammar bin Zuraiq, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Haritha bin Mudrab, on the authority of Abu Al-Ubaydayn, on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: We, the companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say that extravagance is spending on something that is not right. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Katheer Al-Anbari told us: Shu’bah told us: I was walking with Abu Ishaq on the road to Kufa, and he came upon a house that was being built and tiled, and he said: This is extravagance in the words of Abdullah, spending money in ways that are not right. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not spend wastefully, he said: The spendthrift is the one who spends in an unjust manner. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Ibad told us, on the authority of Hisain, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The spendthrift is the one who spends in a way that is not right. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Do not spend on falsehood, for the spendthrift is the one who spends extravagantly without right. Ibn Jurayj said and Mujahid said: If a person spent all his money on what is right, it would not be extravagance, but if he spent a mudd on what is wrong, it would be extravagance. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not spend wastefully, he said: Wastefulness is spending in disobedience to God, in what is not right, and in corruption. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And give the relative his right, and [also] the needy and the traveler, he said: He began with the parents before this, then when he finished with the parents and their right, he mentioned these and said, Do not spend wastefully, do not give in disobedience to God.
17:27: As for his saying, Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, it means: Those who scatter their wealth in disobeying God and spend it in disobedience to Him are allies of the devils. Likewise, the Arabs say about every person who adheres to the way of a people and follows their path: He is their brother. And the devil was ungrateful to his Lord, meaning: The devil was ungrateful for the blessing that his Lord bestowed upon him, not thanking Him for it, but rather disbelieving in it by abandoning the obedience of God and committing His disobedience. Likewise, his brothers from the children of Adam who waste their wealth in disobeying God, do not thank God for His blessings upon them, but rather disobey His command and disobey Him, and follow the example of the wealth that God bestowed upon them, which He granted them, and the Almighty, the Exalted, has bestowed upon them, of not being thankful for it, and receiving it with ingratitude. Like the one who: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Indeed, the wasteful: Indeed, those who spend in disobedience to God were brothers of the devils, and ever was Satan to his Lord ungrateful.
17:28: God the Most High says: And if you, O Muhammad, turn away from those whom I have commanded you to give their rights to, if you find a way to them, turn your face when they ask you for something that you cannot find a way to, out of shyness from them and mercy for them, seeking mercy from your Lord. He says: Waiting for a provision that you expect from your Lord, and you hope that God will make it easy for you, then do not make them despair, but speak to them a gentle word. He says: But promise them a beautiful promise, by saying: God will provide, so I will give to you, and similar words that are gentle and not harsh, as God the Most High said: And as for the beggar, do not repel him. And in the same way as we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: waiting for provision. Then speak to them a gentle word, he said: gently, promise them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, Seeking mercy from your Lord. He said: Provision. Do they distribute the mercy of your Lord? We have divided among them their livelihood. Imran bin Musa told us, he said: Abd al-Warath told us, he said: Amara told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: Waiting for provision from God to come to you. Al-Qasim narrated to us, Q: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding his statement, But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: If they ask you and do not find with you what you can give them, seeking mercy, he said: A provision that you await and hope for. Then speak to them a gentle word, he said: Count them a good number: if that happens, if that comes to us, we will do it, we will give you, so it is the gentle word. Ibn Jurayj said, Mujahid said: If they ask you and you do not have anything to give them, so you turn away from them seeking mercy, he said: It is a provision that you are waiting for. So speak to them a gentle word. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, Seeking mercy from your Lord, he said: Waiting for God’s provision. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Ubaidah, regarding his statement, Seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: Seeking provision. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Saeed: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, he said: meaning provision which you await. Then speak to them a gentle word, meaning a kind word. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, So speak to them a gentle word. He said: Promise them good. Al-Hasan said: Speak to them a gentle, easy word. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement, But if you turn away from them, meaning: you do not find anything to give them, seeking mercy from your Lord, meaning: waiting for provision from your Lord. It was revealed regarding those who used to ask the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from among the poor. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Harami bin Amara told us: Shu’bah told us: Amara told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, regarding the statement of God, So speak to them a gentle word, he said: Kindness. And Ibn Zayd used to say what about that. He told me about it, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, But if you turn away from them, from those whom We have enjoined upon you, seek[ing] mercy from your Lord which you hope for, if you fear that if you give them, they will be strengthened by it to disobey God Almighty, and will seek help from it in doing so, so you see that you should prevent them from doing good, then if they ask you, then speak to them a gentle word, a beautiful word: May God provide for you, may God bless you. This statement that we have mentioned about Ibn Zayd, despite its contradiction with the statements of the people of interpretation in the interpretation of this verse, is far-fetched in meaning, as indicated by its apparent meaning, and that is that God Almighty said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: But if you turn away from them, seeking mercy from your Lord which you hope for, so He commanded him to say, if his turning away from the people whom he mentioned was awaiting mercy from Him which he hopes for from his Lord, an easy word. And that turning away is seeking mercy, and it will not be without one of two matters: Either it is turning away from him seeking God’s mercy which he hopes for himself, in which case the meaning of the statement is as we have said, And the people of interpretation whose statement we have mentioned said this, and it is contrary to his statement, or it is a turning away from him seeking mercy from God that he hopes for the questioners whom the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, allegedly ordered to prevent them from what they asked him for fear that they would spend it in disobeying God. So it is known that God’s wrath upon someone who is not trusted to spend what he was given in order to strengthen himself with it to obey God in disobeying Him is more feared than hoping for His mercy for him, and that is because God’s mercy is only hoped for for the people of His obedience, not for the people of His disobedience, unless he intended to direct that to the fact that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered them to prevent what they asked him for, so that they would repent from disobeying God and repent by preventing them from what they asked for, so that this would be a face that the interpretation of the verse can bear, even if it is contrary to the statement of the people of interpretation.
17:29: This is a parable that God, the Blessed and Exalted, has given for the one who refrains from spending on the rights that He has made obligatory on the wealth of those who have money, making him like someone whose hand is tied to his neck, unable to take it or give it. The meaning of the words is: O Muhammad, do not hold back your hand out of miserliness from spending on the rights of God, so that you do not spend anything on it like someone whose hand is tied to his neck, unable to extend it. And do not extend it completely means: Do not extend it completely in giving, so that you remain with nothing, and you do not find anything to give to the one who asks you, and so you sit blamed and regretful means: So you sit, and those who ask you blame you if you do not give them when they ask you, and you blame yourself for rushing with your money and its going away, regretful, meaning: faulty, cut off from you, with nothing to spend. Its origin is from their saying about an animal that has been driven until its pace has stopped, and it has become worn out and exhausted from walking, that it is exhausted. It is said from it: I exhausted the animal, so I exhaust it, and I exhaust it with exhaustion, and that is if you exhaust it from walking, and I exhausted it with begging if you asked it, so you insisted, and the sight is exhausted, so it is exhausted, and that is if it reaches the furthest point of view and is exhausted. And from it is the saying of the Almighty: The sight will return to you humbled and exhausted. And so it is with everything, I crawl until I am exhausted. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And do not make your hand chained to your neck, he said: Do not make it chained from spending, and do not extend it: spend extravagantly. Ibn Hamid told us: Yusuf ibn Bahz told us: Hawshab told us: When Al-Hasan recited this verse, And do not make your hand chained to your neck nor stretch it forth to its utmost stretching, lest you sit down blamed and destitute, he would say: Do not reduce My provision without My pleasure, and do not place it in My wrath, lest I take away from you what is in your hands, and you become destitute, with nothing of it in your hands. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not make your hand to be chained to your neck nor extend it completely and you will sit down blamed and regretful, he says this about spending. He says, And do not make your hand to be chained to your neck, he says: Do not extend it with good, nor extend it completely and you will sit down blamed, he says: He blames himself for what he has lost of his money, regretful, he means: all his money is gone, so he is regretful. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And do not make your hand chained to your neck, means by that miserliness. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not make your hand to be chained to your neck: meaning, do not hold it back from obeying God, nor from His right. And do not extend it completely: he says, do not spend it in disobeying God, nor in what is good for you, nor is it appropriate for you, which is extravagance. His statement, So you will sit down blamed and regretful: he said, blamed among the servants of God, regretful for what has passed of his time and what was lost. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And do not make your hand chained to your neck. He said: In spending, meaning: do not hold back from spending. And do not extend it completely. He said: do not spend wastefully. So that you sit blamed among the servants of God. Regrettable. He said: regretting what you have neglected. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Do not withhold spending on what I have commanded you to do of truth, and do not extend it completely on what I have forbidden you, lest you sit blamed, he said: guilty, regretful, he said: cut off from you. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not make your hand chained to your neck, he said: Chained, do not extend it with good or with a gift, and do not extend it completely in truth and falsehood, so that what you have and what is in your hands runs out, and someone comes to you wanting you to give to him, but he regrets you and blames you when you gave to these people and did not give to them.
17:30: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Indeed, your Lord, O Muhammad, expands His provision for whomever He wills of His servants, so He makes it abundant for him, and restricts it for whomever He wills, meaning: And He restricts it for whomever He wills of them, so He makes it difficult for him. Indeed, He is ever, with His servants, All-Aware. He says: Your Lord is All-Aware of His servants, and who is reformed by abundance in provision and who is corrupted by poverty and narrowness, and who is reformed by poverty and narrowness and who is destroyed. All-Seeing. He says: He is All-Seeing of their management and their politics, meaning: So, O Muhammad, abide by Our command regarding what We have commanded you and forbidden you from extending your hand in what you extend it for, and for whom you extend it, and from withholding it from whom you withhold it, and withholding it for, for We know better than you the interests of the servants, and We are All-Aware of all creation’s management. Like what Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: Then the Blessed and Exalted informed us of how He does it, and He said: Indeed, your Lord expands provision for whom He wills and restricts it. He said: He restricts: He reduces, and everything in the Qur’an is restricted like that. Then He informed His servants that He does not diminish them nor burden them if He expanded it for them, but He is looking at them, so He said: “And if God were to expand provision for His servants, they would rebel on the earth, but He sends down in due measure as He wills. Indeed, He is, of His servants, Knowing and Seeing.” He said: When the Arabs were fertile and had plenty of wealth, they would rebel, kill each other, and corruption would come. But when it was the year, they would be distracted from that.
17:31: God Almighty says, And your Lord has decreed, O Muhammad, that you worship none but Him, and to parents, good treatment, “and do not kill your children for fear of poverty,” so the position of kill is in the accusative case, in apposition to do not worship. What he means by his saying fear of poverty is fear of scarcity and poverty. We have explained this with evidence previously, and we have mentioned the narration about it. Because God Almighty said that to the Arabs, because they used to kill their female children out of fear of losing their livelihood by spending on them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty: meaning fear of poverty. The people of ignorance used to kill their children for fear of poverty, so God admonished them about that, and informed them that their sustenance and the sustenance of their children is from God, so He said, “We provide for them and for you. Indeed, killing them is a great sin.” Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: For fear of poverty. He said: They used to kill the girls. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. He said: Need and poverty. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, fear of poverty, meaning: poverty. As for his saying, Indeed, killing them was a great mistake, the readers differed in their reading of it. The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq read it as, Indeed, killing them was a great mistake, with a kasra on the kha’ from khatāt and a sukun on the ta’. If it is read in this way, it has two interpretations: One of them is that it is a noun from the saying of the speaker: I made a mistake, so I made a mistake, meaning: I sinned and I was sinful. It is narrated from the Arabs: I made a mistake: if you sinned intentionally, and I made a mistake: if you committed a sin unintentionally. The second: that it means khatāt with a fatha on the kha’ and the ta’, then the kha’ was broken and the ta’ was sukun, as it was said: qatab and qatab, and ḍarā and ḍarā, and najis and najis. Khatā’ with a kasra is a noun, and khatā’ with a fatha on the kha’ and the ta’ is a verbal noun from their saying: khata’ al-rajul, and it may be a noun from their saying: akhtā’. As for the verbal noun from it, it is ikhtā’. It has been said: khatī’ means akhtā. As the poet said: Oh, Hind's sorrow when she made a mistake Meaning: two mistakes. Some of the readers of Medina read that their killing was a mistake with a fatha on the kha and the ta, restricting it to the fact that it is a noun from their saying: someone made a mistake. Some of the readers of Mecca read that their killing was a mistake with a fatha on the kha and the ta, and lengthened the khata in a similar sense to the one who read it khata with a fatha on the kha and the ta, except that he differs from him in lengthening the letter. The majority of the scholars of the Arabic language from the people of Kufa and some of the Basrans among them saw that khāt and khātā have the same meaning, except that some of them claimed that khāt with a kasra on the khā’ and a sukūn on the tā’ in reading is more common, and that khāt with a fathah on the khā’ and a tā’ in people’s speech is more widespread, and that khāt with a sukūr on the khā’ and a sukūn on the tā’ has not been heard in any of their speech or poetry, except in a verse recited by some poets: A mistake is a grave sin, and a sin is a voluntary sin, like a date palm planted in the ground, which is to be considered. I mentioned the difference between the letter kha’ with a kasra on the letter kha and the letter ta’ with a sukoon and a fatha on both of them. The most correct of the readings in this regard, in our view, is the reading that the readers of Iraq and the majority of the people of Hijaz follow, due to the consensus of the proof of the readers on it, and the exception of what is not. The meaning of that was a sin and a mistake, not an error in the action, because they were killing them intentionally, not by mistake, and for their intention in that, their Lord rebuked them and forbade them from it. And in a similar manner to what we said, the people of interpretation said. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, A great mistake, he said: meaning a sin. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, killing them was a great mistake. He said: A sin. Ibn Jurayj said, and Ibn Abbas said: Error: meaning sin.
17:32: God Almighty says: And He also decreed that do not approach O people, adultery, for it is ever an immorality. He says: Adultery was ever an immorality. And an evil way. He says: And the way of adultery is an evil way, because it is the way of those who disobey God and oppose His command, so the worst way is for it, for it leads its follower to the fire of Hell.
17:33: God the Most High says: And He also decreed that do not kill O people the soul which God has forbidden to be killed except by right and its right is that it not be killed except for disbelief after Islam, or fornication after marriage, or fornication after marriage, and if she was a disbeliever whose disbelief was not preceded by Islam, then if her killing was not preceded by Islam, then she has a covenant and safety. 284 2 2 - As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right and by God we do not know of any lawful killing of a Muslim man except in one of three cases, except a man who killed intentionally, in which case he is subject to retaliation, or who committed adultery after marriage, in which case he is subject to stoning, or who disbelieved after his Islam, in which case he is subject to killing. Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Ibn Uyaynah narrated on the authority of Az-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah or someone else who said: It was said to Abu Bakr: Will you kill someone who does not pay zakat? He said: If they withheld from me anything of what they confessed to the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace), I would fight them. It was said to Abu Bakr: Did not the Messenger of God (may God bless him and grant him peace) say: I was commanded to fight the people until they say: There is no god but God. If they say it, their blood and wealth are protected from me except for a right, and their reckoning is with God. Abu Bakr said: This is its right. Musa bin Sahl told me: Amr bin Hashim told us: Sulayman bin Hayyan told us, on the authority of Humayd al-Tawil, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, There is no god but God. If they say it, their blood and their wealth are protected from me, except for a right, and their reckoning is with God. It was said: What is its right? He said: Adultery after marriage, disbelief after faith, and killing a soul, for which he is killed. And His statement, And whoever is killed unjustly, means: And whoever is killed for a reason other than the one we mentioned, if he is killed for it, it is a rightful killing. We have given his heir authority, meaning: We have given the heir of the one who is killed unjustly authority over the killer of his heir. If he wishes, he may seek retribution from him and kill him through his heir, or if he wishes, he may pardon him, or if he wishes, he may seize his hand. The people of interpretation have differed regarding the meaning of the authority given to the heir of the one who is killed, and some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And do not kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority.” He said: Evidence from God Almighty that He revealed and the heir of the murdered person seeks it, the blood money, or retaliation, and that is the authority. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak bin Muzahim, regarding His statement, Then We have given his heir authority, he said: If he wishes, he may pardon, and if he wishes, he may take the blood money. Others said: Rather, that authority is killing. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, which is the retaliation that God Almighty has given. The most correct of the two interpretations of that is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it: that the authority that God Almighty mentioned in this place is what Ibn Abbas said, that the heir of the murdered person has the right to kill if he wishes, or to take the blood money, or to pardon if he wishes, due to the authenticity of the report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said on the day of the conquest of Mecca: “And whoever has someone killed for him, he has the choice of two options: to kill or to take the blood money.” I have explained the ruling on that in our book: The Book of Wounds. And his saying, So do not be excessive in killing. The reciters differed in reading that. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it as so do not be excessive, meaning addressing the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and what is meant by it is him and the Imams after him. He says: Do not kill unjustly for the one killed other than his killer. This is because the people of ignorance used to do that. If a man killed a man, the guardian of the killed man would go to the noble of the killer’s tribe, and kill him through his guardian, and leave the killer. So God, the Almighty, forbade His servants from doing that, and said to His Messenger (peace and blessings of God be upon him): Killing someone other than the killer for the one killed is a sin and an excess, so do not kill someone other than his killer. If you kill the killer for the one killed, do not mutilate him. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it as so do not be excessive with a ya, meaning: The guardian of the killed man should not be excessive, so he should kill someone other than the killer of his guardian. It has been said that what is meant by it is: The first killer should not be excessive, not the guardian of the killed man. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is to say: They are two readings that are close in meaning, and that is because God Almighty’s addressing of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with a command or prohibition in the rulings of religion is a decree from Him regarding all of His servants, and likewise His command and prohibition of some of them is a command from Him and a prohibition from all of them, except in what indicates that it is specific to some and not others. So if that is the case with what we have explained in our book, Kitab al-Bayan, on the foundations of rulings, then it is known that His Almighty’s addressing of His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, with His saying, So do not exceed limits in killing, is to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because it was directed to him, that it is intended for all of His servants. Likewise, His prohibition of the guardian of the one killed or the killer from excess in killing and transgression in it is a prohibition for all of them, so whichever way the reader reads it, then he is correct in his reading of that. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, just as the reciters differed in their reading of it. Those who interpreted this as meaning addressing the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Talq ibn Habib, regarding his statement, So do not exceed the limits in killing, he said: Do not kill anyone other than his killer, and do not mutilate him. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Talq bin Habib, in a similar manner. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, So do not exceed the limits in killing, he said: Do not kill two people for one. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn ibn Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, “So do not exceed limits in killing. Indeed, he will be supported.” This was in Mecca, and the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was there. It was the first thing revealed in the Qur’an concerning killing. The polytheists used to assassinate the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: “Whoever kills you from among the polytheists, do not let killing lead you. Beware of killing his father or brother or any of his relatives. And if they are polytheists, then do not kill anyone except your killer.” This was before Bara’ah was revealed, and before they were commanded to fight the polytheists. So His statement, So do not exceed limits in killing, means: Do not kill anyone other than your killer. And today it is in that position with the Muslims, it is not permissible for them to kill anyone other than their killer. It was mentioned that he said: It refers to the guardian of the murdered person. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, he said: A man would be killed and his heir would say: I will not be satisfied until I kill so-and-so and so-and-so from the nobles of his tribe. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Do not be excessive in killing. He said: Do not kill anyone other than your killer, and do not mutilate him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, He should not be excessive in killing. He said: He should not kill anyone other than his killer. Whoever kills with an iron object should be killed with an iron object, whoever kills with a piece of wood should be killed with a piece of wood, and whoever kills with a stone should be killed with a stone. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say that the three most disobedient people to God, may His praise be exalted, are: a man who kills someone other than his killer, or who kills with smoke in the pre-Islamic era, or who kills in the sanctuary of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard him, meaning Ibn Zayd, say about the statement of God, the Most High, And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, he said: When one of the Arabs was killed, they would not be satisfied to kill the killer of their companion until they killed someone more honorable than the one who killed him. So God, the Most High, said, We have given his heir authority, to support him and take revenge for his right, so let him not exceed limits in killing, killing an innocent person. Mention of what the killer said about me: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid: So let him not be excessive in killing. He said: The killer should not be excessive in killing. We have mentioned the correct reading of this in our view, and if both aspects of the reading are correct in our view, then so are all aspects of its interpretation that we have mentioned, except for one aspect of it being correct, because the speech is possible in this way, and in God’s prohibition of some of His creation from extravagance in killing, He prohibits all of them from it. As for his saying, He was victorious, the people of interpretation differed about who was meant by the ha in his saying, He was, and what it refers to. Some of them said: It refers to the guardian of the murdered one, and he is the one meant by it, and he is the one victorious over the murderer. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: He was victorious. He said: The imam was handed over to him, meaning to the guardian, so if he wanted to kill him, he could kill him, and if he wanted to pardon him, he could pardon him. Others said: Rather, it refers to the one who was killed. According to this statement, it refers back to the one in his statement, And whoever was killed unjustly. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Abdullah bin Katheer, on the authority of Mujahid: He was victorious. The one who was killed was victorious. Others said: It refers to the blood of the murdered person. They said: The meaning of the statement is: The blood of the murdered person was victorious over the murderer. And what is most likely to be correct in my opinion is the statement of the one who said that it refers to the guardian, and it is based on that, because he is the oppressed one, and his guardian is the murdered one, and it is closer to mentioning him than mentioning the murdered one, and he is also the victorious one, because God, may He be glorified and exalted, decreed in His revealed Book that He gave him power over the murderer of his guardian, and His judgment in it is that he may kill him if he wishes, and keep him for the blood money if he likes, and pardon him if he sees fit, and that is enough victory for him from God, may He be glorified and exalted, so for that reason we said: He is the one meant by the ha’ in His statement, Indeed, he was victorious.
17:34: God Almighty says: And He also decreed that you should not approach the orphan's property by consuming it extravagantly and hastily, lest they grow old. But approach it with the best action and the most beautiful trait, which is to dispose of it for him in a productive manner, in a prudent manner, and with caution. Qatada used to say about that what: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, when this verse was revealed, it was difficult for the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so they would not mix with them in food or eating or anything else, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed, But if you mix with them, they are your brothers, and God knows the corrupter from the reformer. So they had a license for this. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best. He said: They did not mix with them in terms of money, food, or transportation, until the verse was revealed: And if you mix with them, then they are your brothers. Ibn Zayd said about this: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in a way that is best, he said: Eating in a reasonable manner, that you eat with him if you need him, my father used to say that. And His statement, until he reaches maturity, means: until he reaches the time of maturity in his mind, managing his money, and improving his condition in his religion. And fulfill the covenant, means: fulfill the contract that you make with people in peace between the people of war and Islam, and also among yourselves, and sales, drinks, rents, and other contracts. Indeed, the covenant will be questioned about, means: Indeed, God, the Most High, will question the covenant breaker about his breach of it. He says: So do not break the valid covenants between you and those with whom you have made a covenant, O people, lest you break them and betray the one to whom you gave them. And what He meant by that is that the covenant was required. It is said in speech: So-and-so will be questioned about the covenant of so-and-so.
17:35: God Almighty says: “And He has decreed that you should give full measure to people when you measure their rights before you, and do not defraud them. And weigh with a straight balance.” He says: And He has decreed that you should also weigh with a straight balance, which is justice in which there is no crookedness, deceit, or trickery. The interpreters differed about the meaning of the scale. Some of them said: It is the balance. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Safwan bin Isa told us: Al-Hasan bin Dhakwan told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And weigh with the straight balance. He said: The scales. Others said: It is justice in Roman. Who said that? Ali bin Sahl told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Al-Qistas is justice in Roman. Others said: It is the scale, whether small or large. There are two pronunciations for it: Al-Qistas with a kasra on the qaf, and Al-Qistas with a damma on it, like Al-Qirtas and Al-Qirtas. The majority of the reciters of Kufa read it with a kasra, and the majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra read it with a damma. Some of the reciters of Kufa also read it with it. Whichever of them the reciter recites, he is correct, because they are two well-known pronunciations, and two readings that are widespread among the reciters of the regions. His statement: That is better means: Your giving back to those to whom you measure, and your weighing justly for those to whom you give, is better for you than your withholding that from them and wronging them in it. His statement: And better in the end means: And better in the return to you and more appropriate for Him in it is your doing that, because God, the Blessed and Exalted, is pleased with that from you, so He rewards you well for it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: “And give full measure when you measure, and weigh with a straight balance. That is better and more suitable for final outcome.” That is, better in reward and outcome. And he informed us that Ibn Abbas used to say: O group of Mawali, you have been entrusted with two matters by which the people before you were destroyed: this measure and this balance. He said: And it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: No man is able to do something forbidden and then abandons it for no other reason than fear of God, except that God will replace it for him in this world before the Hereafter with something better for him than that. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the best interpretation. He said: The consequence and reward.
17:36: The interpreters differed in their interpretation of his statement: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Some of them said: Its meaning is: And do not say that of which you have no knowledge. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge, meaning: do not say. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those one will be questioned.” Do not say, I saw when you did not see, and I heard when you did not hear, for God, the Blessed and Exalted, will ask you about all of that. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. He said: Do not say, I saw and you did not see, “I heard and you did not hear,” I knew and you did not know. It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rabi’ah, on the authority of Ismail al-Azraq, on the authority of Abu Umar al-Bazzar, on the authority of Ibn al-Hanafiyyah, who said: False testimony. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Do not throw. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge means: Do not accuse anyone of that of which you have no knowledge. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And do not stop and do not throw. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. These two interpretations are close in meaning, because saying what the speaker does not know includes false testimony, accusing people of falsehood, claiming to have heard what one did not hear, and seeing what one did not see. The root of qafw is: to bite and slander. And from it is the saying of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We are the sons of Al-Nadr bin Kinanah, we do not follow the lineage nor do we deny our father. And some of the Basrans used to recite a verse about that: Like dolls, the two naked ones are filled with modesty, not shyness. By taqāfī he means: throwing. And it is claimed that the meaning of his saying: Do not stop is do not follow what you do not know, and that does not concern you. Some of the Arabists from Kufa claimed that its origin is qiyāfah, which is following the trace, and since it is as they mentioned, the reading must be do not stop with a ḍammah on the qaf and a sukūn on the fa’, like in the verse: do not say. He said: The Arabs say: qafut atharhu, waqfat atharhu, so sometimes the waw comes before the fa’ and sometimes it comes after it, as it is said: qa’ al-jamal an-naqah: if he rides it, he falls and ravages and ravages, and it was recited by listening to the following from the Arabs: Even if I threw you from close by, you would be as ungrateful as a wolf prays. It means an obstacle, and there are many similar words in Arabic speech. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Do not say to people, while they are not aware of something about which you have no knowledge, so that you accuse them of falsehood and testify against them without the truth, for that is backbiting.
