Rather, we said that this is the most correct of the sayings about it, because that is the most common usage of the Arabs in the word qafwa. As for his saying: Indeed, the hearing, the sight, and the heart - about all those one will be questioned, its meaning is: God will ask these organs about what their owner said, that he heard or saw or knew, and his limbs will bear witness against him at that time with the truth. And he said those, and he did not say those, as the poet said: Blame the houses after the house of Al-Lawa and life after those days It was said: those, because those and those are for the small plural that occurs for the masculine and feminine, and this and those are for the large plural. So the masculinity for the small is like the masculinity in the nouns before the femininity, so the masculinity for the first plural, and the femininity for the second plural, which is the large plural, because the Arabs make the plural based on the example of the nouns.
17:37: God Almighty says: And do not walk on the earth arrogantly. You will never tear the earth apart. He says: You will not tear the earth apart with your arrogance, as Ru’bah said: Dark and empty of penetration What is meant by the verse and you will never reach the mountains in height is the passage with your pride and arrogance. Rather, this is a prohibition from God to His servants from arrogance, pride, and conceit. He presented it to them in it, informing them that they will not attain, with their arrogance and pride, anything that others fall short of. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “And do not walk upon the earth exultantly. Indeed, you will never tear the earth [apart], and you will never reach the mountains in height,” meaning with your arrogance and exultation. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And do not walk on the earth exultantly. He said: Do not walk on the earth with pride and arrogance, for that will not make you reach the mountains, nor will you tear through the earth with your pride and arrogance. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And do not walk on the earth. He said: Do not boast. It was said: And do not walk exultantly, and he did not say exultantly, because he did not mean by the speech: Do not be exultant, making it from the verb of the one walking, but rather he meant: Do not walk on the earth exultantly, so he explained the intended meaning of his saying: And do not walk, as Al-Zajir said: He loves hot food, juice and dates with a love that has no end. He said: Love, because in his saying: He likes it, there is the meaning of He loves, so he excluded his saying: Love, from its meaning, not its wording.
17:38: And his saying: All of that was evil in the sight of your Lord and detestable, the reciters differed concerning it, so some of the reciters of Medina and most of the reciters of Kufa recited it: All of that was evil in the sight of your Lord and detestable with the addition meaning: All of this that we mentioned of these matters that we enumerated from the beginning of our saying: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him... to our saying: And do not walk on the earth exultantly "was evil" meaning: What we enumerated for you was evil in the sight of your Lord and detestable. The reciters of this reading said: All of that was bad was said with the addition, because among what we have enumerated from His statement, And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, there are matters that are a command to do good, such as His statement, And to parents, good treatment, and His statement, And give the relative his right, and the like. They said: Not everything in it is a prohibition of bad, rather it contains a prohibition of bad and a command to do good, so that is why we read asihi. The majority of the reciters of the people of Medina and Basra and some of the reciters of Kufa read all of that was bad and they said: What is meant by that is: everything we have enumerated from our statement, And do not kill your children for fear of poverty, and what came before that is not included in it. They said: Everything we have enumerated from that place to this place is bad and has no good in it, so the correct reading is with the tanween. Whoever recites this reading, his intention should be that the disliked should precede the bad, and the meaning of the speech should be: All of that was disliked and bad, because if he makes his saying: disliked, we count the bad as a description of the bad, then the reading should be: All of that was bad and disliked by your Lord, and that is contrary to what is in the copies of the Muslims’ Qur’ans. The first of the two readings in my opinion is the correct reading of the one who reads All of that was his badness with the addition of the bad to the ha’, meaning: All of that which we have enumerated from And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. “It was his badness” because in that there are matters that are forbidden and matters that are commanded, and the beginning of the will and covenant from that place without his saying: And do not kill your children is only a conjunction to what came before from his saying: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him. So if that is the case, then his reading with the addition of the bad to the ha’ is more appropriate and more deserving than his reading it as badness with the tanween, meaning a single badness. The interpretation of the words then is: All of the things that we mentioned to you and that we enumerated against you were bad and hated by your Lord, O Muhammad. He hates it and forbids it and is not pleased with it, so avoid committing it and acting upon it.
17:39: God Almighty says: This which we have shown you, O Muhammad, of the beautiful morals that we have commanded you to do and forbidden you to do, is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. He says: from the wisdom that we have revealed to you in this book of ours. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: This is from what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom, he said: The Qur’an. We have explained the meaning of wisdom in the previous part of this book, so there is no need to repeat it here. And do not make with God another god, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed and banished. He says: And do not make with God partners in your worship, lest you be thrown into Hell, blamed, blamed by yourself and by those who know you among the people. Banished. He says: Far away and excluded from the Fire. Rather, sincerely worship God, the One, the Subduer, and you will be saved from His punishment. And similar to what we said about his statement: Blameable and rejected, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Blamed and expelled, he said: banished. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Blamed and rejected. He said: Blamed in the worship of God, rejected in the Fire.
17:40: God Almighty says to those polytheists of the Arabs who said: The angels are daughters of God: Has your Lord chosen you, O people, for sons? He says: Has your Lord chosen you for male children? And taken for Himself females from among the angels? And you are not pleased with them for yourselves, rather you bury them alive and kill them. So you have attributed to God what you are not pleased with for yourselves. Indeed, you are saying a terrible saying. God Almighty says to these polytheists who said the slander against God that we have mentioned: “O people, you are saying with your saying: The angels are daughters of God, a terrible saying, and you are fabricating a slander against God from you.” Qatada used to say about that: Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And He took from among the angels females. He said: The Jews said: The angels are the daughters of God.
17:41: God the Most High says: And We have certainly presented to these polytheists who slander God in this Qur'an lessons, verses, and arguments, and We have given them examples in it, and We have warned them and admonished them in it that they may remember meaning: that they may remember those arguments against them, so that they may understand the error of what they are doing, and take heed from the lessons, so that they may learn from them, and turn from their ignorance, for they do not take heed from them, nor do they remember what is brought to them of verses and warnings, and what increases their reminding of them except in aversion meaning: except in turning away from the truth, and in distancing from it and fleeing. And aversion in this place is a source from their saying: So-and-so was averse to this matter, he is averse and averse.
17:42: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who have made another god with God: If the matter were as you say, that there were gods with Him, and it is not as you say, then those gods would have sought closeness to God, the Lord of the Mighty Throne, and sought nearness to Him and a position from Him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “Say: If there were with Him gods as they say, then they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne.” He says: If there were gods with Him, then they would have known His virtue, His rank, and His position over them, and they would have sought what would bring them closer to Him. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then they would have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne. He said: They would have sought closeness to Him, even though it is not as they say.
17:43: This is a purification from God Almighty, who mentioned Himself, from what the polytheists described Him with, who made gods other than Him, and attributed daughters to Him. He said: Purification of God and exaltation of Him from what they say, O people, of slander and lies, for what you attribute to Him of these matters is not from His attribute, and it is not appropriate for Him to have an attribute. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Glory be to Him, and He is far above what they say, far above. He glorifies Himself when slander is said about Him. And the Most High said: far above what they say, and He did not say: exalted, as He said: And devote yourself to Him with a complete devotion, as the poet said: You are the ransom for the Kaaba that you demolished and dug up with your own hands, every hole in it The pigeons were prevented from taking a nap from the roof and from the debris, so every bird flew away.
17:44: And His statement: The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him means: God is far removed, O polytheists, from what you have described Him with in glorification and reverence for Him, the seven heavens and the earth, and whoever is in them of the believers in Him from the angels, mankind and jinn, and you, despite His blessings upon you and His beautiful favors with you, fabricate against Him what you fabricate. And His saying: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. God Almighty says: There is not a thing of His creation but glorifies Him with praise. As Nasr ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi narrated to me, he said: Muhammad ibn Ya`la narrated to us, on the authority of Musa ibn Ubaydah, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Shall I not tell you of something that Noah commanded his son to do? Noah said to his son: O my son, I command you to say: Subhan God wa bihamdihi, for it is the prayer of creation and the glorification of creation, and with it creation is provided for. God said: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Isa bin Ubaid told us: I heard Ikrimah say: No one should criticize his animal or his clothing, for everything glorifies Him with praise. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wazeh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah: There is nothing but glorifies Him with praise. He said: The tree glorifies, and the column glorifies. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh and Zaid bin Habbab told us: Jarir Abu Al-Khattab told us: We were with Yazid Al-Raqashi and Al-Hasan was with him at a meal, and they brought the tray. Yazid Al-Raqashi said: O Abu Saeed, does this tray glorify God? He said: It used to glorify God once. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak and Yunus, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that they said regarding His statement: And there is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, they said: Everything that has a soul. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abdul Kabir bin Abdul Majeed told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Food glorifies God. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise. He said: Everything that has a soul glorifies Him, whether it is a tree or something that has a soul. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Ubay, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr, that when a man says: There is no god but God, it is the word of sincerity, and God will not accept any action from anyone until he says it. When he says: Praise be to God, it is the word of gratitude, and no servant has ever thanked God until he says it. When he says: God is Great, it fills what is between the heavens and the earth. When he says: Glory be to God, it is the prayer of the creation, and God has not left any of His creation without illuminating it with prayer and glorification. When he says: There is no power or strength except with God, He says: My servant has submitted and surrendered. And His statement, But you do not understand their glorification, God Almighty says: But you do not understand the glorification of anything other than the glorification of those who glorify with the same tongues as you. Indeed, He is Forbearing, meaning: God is Forbearing and does not hasten His creation, who disobey His command and disbelieve in Him. If it were not for that, He would have hastened the punishment of these polytheists who call upon gods and rivals with Him. Forgiving, meaning: He covers their sins if they repent from them by pardoning them from Him. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, He was Forbearing with regard to His creation, so He does not hasten as some of them hasten with others, Forgiving of them if they repent.
17:45: God Almighty says: And when you, O Muhammad, recite the Qur’an to these polytheists who do not believe in the Resurrection, nor acknowledge reward and punishment, We place between you and them a veil, which prevents their hearts from understanding what you recite to them, so that they may benefit from it, as a punishment from Us to them for their disbelief. The veil here means the screen. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. The invisible veil is coverings over their hearts so that they do not understand it and benefit from it. They obeyed Satan, so he took control of them. Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, A concealed veil. He said: It is the coverings. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil. He said: My father said: They do not understand it, and He recited: Their hearts are covered and in their ears is deafness? That does not reach them. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: The meaning of his saying a veil that is concealed is a concealing veil, but he excluded it while it is an agent in the form of the object, just as it is said: You are ominous for us and auspicious, but it is sha’im and yaman because it is from shamahum and yamanhum. He said: The veil here is the concealer. He said: concealed. Others from the Arab scholars said: The meaning of that is: a veil concealed from worship so that they do not see it. This second statement is more evident in the meaning of the speech, that what is covered is the veil, so its meaning is: God has a veil from the sight of people, so their sight does not perceive Him, even though the first statement has an understandable aspect.
17:46: God the Almighty says: And We have placed over the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter, when you recite the Qur’an to them, coverings, which is the plural of Kinan, and that is what covers them because God has let them down from understanding what is recited to them. And in their ears is deafness. He says: And We have placed in their ears a deafness from hearing it, and a deafness. The word waqar in the... Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn away, and when the Muslims said, There is no god but God, the polytheists denied it and it was too great for them, so Satan and his soldiers opposed it, but God refused except to carry it out and support it and triumph over it and make it prevail over whoever opposes it. It is a word that whoever disputes with it will triumph, and whoever fights with it will be victorious. Only the people of this peninsula among the Muslims know it, which a rider can cross in a few nights and time passes among groups of people who do not know it or acknowledge it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn back in aversion, he said: Some of what he said so that they would not hear him, just as the people of Noah used to put their fingers in their ears so that they would not hear what he commanded them to do of seeking forgiveness and repentance, and they would cover themselves with their clothes, he said: They would wrap themselves in their clothes and put their fingers in their ears so that they would hear and not be looked at. Others said: What he meant by his saying: And they turned their backs in aversion is the devils, and that they flee from reading the Qur’an and remembering God. Who said that? Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Dhar’i’ told me: Ruh ibn al-Musayyab Abu Raja’ al-Kalbi told us: Amr ibn Malik told us, on the authority of Abu al-Jawza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur’an, they turn back in aversion, they are the devils. The statement that we have made about that is more similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation, and that is that God Almighty followed that with His statement, And when you recite the Qur’an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter an invisible veil, so it is more appropriate for that to be report about them, since it is connected to their report than it is report about someone who is not permitted to be mentioned. As for aversion, it is the plural of nafir, just as qa’ud is the plural of qa’id, and jilus is the plural of jalis. It is permissible for it to be a source that was extracted from other than its wording, since His statement turned means: nafiran, so the meaning of the statement is: they fled in aversion, as Imru’ al-Qays said: I was satisfied and was humiliated Since radhat means I humiliated, then humiliation was removed from its meaning, not from its wording.
17:47: God Almighty says: We know best, O Muhammad, what these polytheists of your people who do not believe in the Hereafter are listening to, as they listen to you while you are reciting the Book of God, And when they are whispering. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say: The whispering is their action, so he made them the whispering, just as he says: They are a people of contentment, but contentment is their action. And His statement, When the wrongdoers say, ‘You follow none but a man bewitched,’ means: When the polytheists say, You follow none but a man bewitched. And what is meant by what was mentioned by the whispering is: those who consulted about the matter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the House of Assembly. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, When they listen to you, he said: It is like what was said by Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and those with him in the House of Assembly. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, When they listened to you and when they were in private conversation, when the wrongdoers said, and their private conversation was that they claimed that he was crazy, and that he was a magician, and they said, Legends of the ancients. Some of the Arabists from Basra used to say, You follow none but a man bewitched, to mean: You follow none but a man who has magic: that is, he has a lung. The Arabs call the lung magic, and the bewitched comes from their saying to a man who is cowardly: his magic has blown up. Likewise, everything that is eaten or drunk, whether human or otherwise, is called bewitched or bewitched, as Labid said: If you ask us what we are, then we are birds from this enchanted people Others said: And we are enchanted by food and drink, meaning we are nourished by them. So its meaning, according to him, was: You are only following a man with lungs, who eats food and drinks drink, not a king who has no need for food and drink. And what he said about that is not far from the truth.
17:48: God Almighty says: Look, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart and consider how they have presented examples to you and likened to you similitudes, by saying: He is bewitched, he is a poet, he is crazy. They have gone astray means: they have deviated from the right path by saying what they said. They cannot find a way means: they cannot find guidance to the path of truth because of their straying from it and their distance from it, and because God has let them down from finding it, so they are unable to find a way out of what they are in from their disbelief by being guided to faith in Him. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Thata Warqa’a told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They cannot find a way out, he said: a way out, Al-Walid bin Al-Mughirah and his companions as well. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, Look how they have set forth parables for you, and have gone astray and are unable to find a way. Narrated by Al-Walid bin Al-Mughira and his companions.
17:49: God Almighty says, informing us about what was said by those polytheists of Quraysh who do not believe in the Hereafter, and they said with their curse: If we are bones that have not been crushed or broken after our death and decay, and dust meaning dust in our graves. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, God says, dust, he said: dust. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they said, ‘Shall we then be bones and fragments?’ He said: dust. There is no singular for fragments, and it is like dust and debris. It is said from it:َهَدت یَهَدت َهَدت َهاًطا َهْد ًمََفو: if it becomes like debris and rubble. And his saying, Indeed, we will be resurrected as a new creation, they said, denying the resurrection after death. Indeed, we will be resurrected after our fate in the graves as unbroken bones and broken remains, and we have been worn out and have become dust in them, a creation created as we were before death, new, and we will be returned as we began? So He, the Most High, the Majestic, answered them, informing them of His power to resurrect them after their death and create them as they were before their affliction, a new creation, whatever their condition, bones or remains or stones or iron, or anything else that they find too great to create something like it, like them, living: Say, O Muhammad, be stones or iron or any creation that is too great in your hearts.
17:50: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those among your people who deny the resurrection after death, who say, When we are bones and dust, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? If you are amazed at God’s creation of you and His return of your bodies as a new creation after your decay in the dust and your fate as dust, and you deny that of His power, be stones or iron, or create something that is too great in your hearts if you are able to do that, then I will revive you and resurrect you as a new creation after your fate is the same as I began you the first time.
17:51: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of his statement, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts. Some of them said: He meant death by it, and what is meant by it is: Or be death, for if you were it, your nation would be resurrected after that on the Day of Resurrection. Who said that? Zakariya bin Yahya bin Abi Zaida told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Atiya, on the authority of Ibn Umar: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts. He said: Death. He said: If you were dead, I would have brought you back to life. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, meaning death, he says: If you are death, I will revive you. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told me, he said: Abu Malik Al-Junbi told us, he said: Ibn Abi Khalid told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, he said: Death. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Sulayman Abu Dawud told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, he said: Death. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Saeed bin Jubair said, regarding His statement, Or a creation of what is greater in your hearts, Become death if you are able, for death will die. He said: And nothing is greater in the soul of the son of Adam than death. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, who said: It was conveyed to me, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, who said: It is death. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abdullah bin Omar, that he used to say: Death will be brought on the Day of Resurrection like a white ram until it is placed between Paradise and Hell, and a caller will call out, and the people of Paradise and the people of Hell will hear, saying: This is death, we have brought it and we will destroy it, so be certain, O people of Paradise and people of Hell, that death has perished. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, meaning death, saying: If you were death for your nation. Abdullah bin Amr bin Al-Aas used to say: “God will bring death on the Day of Resurrection, when the people of Paradise and the people of Hell have already reached their homes. It will be like a white ram, and it will stand between Paradise and Hell. The people of Paradise and the people of Hell will call out: ‘This is death, and we are its slaughterers.’ They will be certain of eternity.” Others said: He meant the sky, the earth, and the mountains. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Or a creation of what is great in your hearts. He said: The sky, the earth, and the mountains. Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is: Be whatever you wish. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Be stones or iron * Or a creation of that which is great in your hearts. He said: Be whatever you wish, for God will return you as you were. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Say: Be you stones or iron, or some creation of that which is great in your hearts.” He said: From the creation of God, for God will cause you to die and then resurrect you on the Day of Resurrection as a new creation. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty disliked saying, Or a creation of what is great in your hearts, and it is possible that He meant death by it, because it is great in the hearts of the children of Adam, and it is possible that He meant by it the heavens and the earth, and it is possible that He meant by it something else, and there is no clearer explanation of that than what He, may His praise be glorified, has explained, which is everything that is great in the hearts of the children of Adam from His creation because He did not specify a thing from it over another. As for his statement, And they will say, ‘Who will bring us back?’ He is saying: So those who do not believe in the Hereafter will say to you, O Muhammad, Who will bring us back? a new creation, if we were stones or iron or a creation that is greater in our hearts, so say to them: He who created you the first time will bring you back. He says: He will bring you back as you were before you became stones or iron, living human beings, He who created you as human beings from nothing the first time. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, “Say: He who created you the first time,” meaning He created you. And they will nod their heads at you, he says: If you say that to them, they will nod their heads at you, raising and lowering them. And so is naghdh in the speech of the Arabs. It is a movement of rising and then lowering, or lowering and then rising. And for this reason the gazelle was called naghdh, because when it walks quickly, it rises and lowers, and moves its head, as the poet said: Walk naghdh, not slumbering, alert. It is said: Naghdat Sanah means that it moved and rose from its base. From this comes the saying of the rajaz poet: And she lowered her teeth And the other said: When she saw me, she lowered her head. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Then they will shake their heads at you, meaning they will move their heads in denial and mockery. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They will shake their heads at you. He said: They will move their heads. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then they will shake their heads at you, meaning: They will move them at you in mockery. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’ Al-Khurasani, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then they will shake their heads at you. He said: They will move their heads in mockery and say: When will it be? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then they will shake their heads at you, meaning they will mock. And His statement, And they say, ‘When will it be?’ God Almighty says: And they say, When will the Resurrection be? And in what state and time will He restore us as a new creation, as we were the first time? God Almighty said to His Prophet: Say to them, O Muhammad, when they say to you, When will it be? When is this Resurrection that you promise us? Perhaps it will be soon. Rather, its meaning is: It is soon, because perhaps is obligatory from God. Therefore, the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I and the Hour were sent like these two, and he pointed with his index and middle fingers, because God Almighty had informed him that He was near and responsive.
17:52: God Almighty says: Say: Perhaps your resurrection, O polytheists, is near. That is the Day when your Lord will call you to come forth from your graves to the place of Resurrection, and you will respond with praise to Him. The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His statement, Then you respond with His praise. Some of them said: Then you respond with His command. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told me, he said: Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, On the Day He calls you and you respond with His praise, meaning: with His command. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Then you respond with His praise. He said: With His command. Others said: The meaning of this is: Then you respond with knowledge and obedience to Him. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, On the Day He calls you and you respond with praise to Him: meaning with knowledge of Him and obedience to Him. The most correct of the sayings about this is to say: Its meaning is: So you respond to God from your graves with His power and His supplication to you, and praise be to God in every situation, as the speaker says: I did that action with the praise of God, meaning: Praise be to God for everything I did, and as the poet said: By the grace of God, I do not wear the garment of a wicked person, nor do I cover myself with treachery. Meaning: Praise be to God, I have not worn the clothes of an immoral person. And His statement, And you think that you have remained only a little, means: And you think, when the Day of Resurrection comes to you, from the horror of what you will witness therein, that you have remained on the earth only a little, as the Most High said, “He said, ‘How many years have you remained on the earth?’ They said, ‘We remained a day or part of a day. So ask the counters.’” And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you think that you have remained only a little: meaning in this world, the world became insignificant to them and became small, when they saw the Day of Resurrection.
17:53: And His saying, And tell My servants to say that which is best. God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And tell, O Muhammad, to My servants to say to one another that which is best of conversation and address. As Khallad bin Aslam told us, he said: Al-Nadr told us, he said: Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding this verse: And tell My servants to say that which is best, he said: That which is best. He does not say to him like he says to him: May God have mercy on you, may God forgive you. And His statement, Indeed, Satan sows dissension among them, means that Satan causes dissension among them, he sows discord among them, he says, he corrupts them, he stirs up evil among them. Indeed, Satan has been to man a clear enemy, means that Satan was an enemy to Adam and his descendants, he made his enmity clear to them by what he showed to Adam of envy and his deception of him until he expelled him from Paradise.
17:54: God Almighty says to these polytheists from Quraysh who said, When we are bones and dust, shall we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? "Your Lord, O people, is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you," so He will accept your repentance with His mercy, until you repent from your disbelief in Him and in the Last Day. "Or if He wills, He will punish you," by letting you down from the faith, so that you die in your polytheism, and He will punish you on the Day of Resurrection for your disbelief in Him. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abdul-Malik bin Jurayj, regarding his statement, “Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you.” He said: So you will believe. Or if He wills, He will punish you. So you will die in polytheism as you are. And His saying, And We have not sent you over them as a guardian, He says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have not sent you, O Muhammad, over those to whom We sent you to call them to obey Us as a Lord or a watcher. Rather, We have sent you to them to convey Our messages to them, and in Our hands is their direction and management. If We will, We will have mercy on them, and if We will, We will punish them.
17:55: God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And your Lord, O Muhammad, knows best who is in the heavens and the earth and what is good for them, for He is their Creator, Provider, and Manager. He knows best who is worthy of repentance and mercy, and who is worthy of punishment. I guide to the truth whoever has been granted mercy and happiness from Me, and I lead astray whoever has been granted misery and failure from Me. He says: Do not let that be too much for you, for that is from what I do with them, because I prefer some prophets over others, by sending some of them to some of creation, and some of them to all, and raising some of them above others in degrees. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “And your Lord is most knowing of who is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others,” God took Abraham as a friend, and spoke to Moses directly, and God made Jesus like Adam, He created him from dust, then said to him, Be, and he was, and he is the servant of God and His Messenger, from the word of God and His spirit, and Solomon was given a kingdom such as no one after him would have, and David was given the Psalms, we used to recite a supplication that David taught, praise and glorification, in which there is neither lawful nor unlawful, nor obligations nor limits, and Muhammad was forgiven for his past and future sins. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: And We have certainly preferred some prophets over others. He said: God spoke to Moses and sent Muhammad to all people.
17:56: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who worship other than God from among His creation: Call upon those you claim are lords and gods besides Him when a calamity befalls you, and see if they are able to repel that from you, or transfer it from you to someone else, so that you call them gods? They are not able to do that, nor do they possess it. Rather, it is your Creator and their Creator who possesses and has power over it. It was said that those to whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to say this statement, were worshipping the angels, Ezra, and the Messiah, and some of them were worshipping a group of jinn. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “Say: Call upon those you claim besides Him, for they do not possess the power to remove harm from you or to change it.” He said: The polytheists used to say: We worship the angels and Ezra, and they are the ones they call upon, meaning the angels, the Messiah, and Ezra.
17:57: God Almighty says: These are the ones whom these polytheists call upon as lords, they seek a means of approach to their Lord. He says: Those who are called lords seek nearness to their Lord and closeness, because they are people of faith in Him, and the polytheists worship them instead of God. Which of them is nearest? Which of them, through his good deeds and his effort in worshipping Him, is closest to Him in nearness. And they hope through their deeds for His mercy and they fear through their opposition to His command “His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord, O Muhammad, is to be feared.” The people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that, except that they differed about those who were called, and some of them said: They are a group of jinn. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, regarding His statement: Those are the ones they call upon, desiring a means of approach to their Lord, he said: There were people from among mankind who worshipped a group of jinn, then the jinn converted to Islam and mankind remained in their disbelief, so God Almighty revealed: Those are the ones they call upon, desiring a means of approach to their Lord, meaning the jinn. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah Al-Ajli told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Sulayman, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, who said: Abdullah said regarding this verse, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord - which of them is nearest? He said: A tribe of jinn who used to worship and then converted to Islam. Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: Al-Hussein told me, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ma’bad bin Abdullah Al-Zamani, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah bin Mas’ud, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding his statement, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, he said: It was revealed about a group of Arabs who used to worship and a group of jinn, so the jinn converted to Islam, but the humans who used to worship them were not aware of their conversion, so it was revealed, Those who call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, which of them is nearest. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Abdullah bin Utbah bin Masoud, on the authority of his uncle Abdullah bin Masoud, he said: This verse was revealed about a group of Arabs who used to worship a group of jinn, and the jinn and the group of Arabs converted to Islam without realizing it. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Those who call upon God, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. A people worshipped the jinn, and those jinn converted to Islam, so God Almighty said: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Abdullah: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. He said: A group of humans used to worship a group of jinn, then the group of jinn converted to Islam and the humans held fast to their worship, so he said: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Muammar, he said: Abdullah said: There were people who worshipped a group of jinn, then those jinn converted to Islam, and mankind remained steadfast in their worship, so God Almighty said: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, which of them is nearest, he said, there were people from the people of ignorance who worshipped a group of jinn, and when the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, they all converted to Islam, so they were seeking which of them was nearest. Others said: Rather, they are angels. Al-Husayn ibn Ali al-Sada’i told me: Yahya ibn al-Sakn told us: Abu al-Awam told us: Qatada told us, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Ma’bad al-Zamani, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, who said: There were tribes of Arabs who worshipped a class of angels called the jinn, and they said: They are the daughters of God. Then God Almighty revealed: Those are the ones whom they call upon, O company of Arabs, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. He said: Those who call upon the angels, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, Which of them is nearest and they hope for His mercy. Until he reached: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is to be feared. He said: And these are the ones who worshipped the angels from the polytheists. Others said: Rather, they are Ezra, Jesus, and his mother. Who said that? Yahya bin Ja`far told me, he said: Yahya bin Al-Sakn told us, he said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord, he said: Jesus, his mother, and Ezra. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abu Al-Nu’man Al-Hakam bin Abdullah Al-Ajli told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Ismail Al-Suddi, on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: Jesus, son of Mary, his mother, and Ezra are in this verse: Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of approach to their Lord. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, They seek a means of approach to their Lord, he said: Jesus, son of Mary, and Ezra, and the angels. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Ibn Abbas used to say regarding His statement, Those are the ones they call upon, seeking a means of access to their Lord, he said: It is Ezra, the Messiah, the sun, and the moon. The first interpretation of this verse is the statement of Abdullah bin Masoud, which we have narrated on the authority of Abu Muammar, that God, the Most High, mentioned that those whom the polytheists call gods, sought a means of approach to their Lord during the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. It is known that Ezra did not exist during the time of our Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he sought a means of approach to his Lord, and that Jesus had been taken up. Only the one who is alive and working in obedience to God and drawing near to Him through righteous deeds seeks a means of approach to his Lord. As for the one who has no means of action, how does he seek a means of approach to his Lord? Since there is no meaning to this statement, there is no statement in it except the statement of the one who said what we have chosen in the interpretation, or the statement of the one who said: They are the angels, and these are two statements that are borne out by the apparent meaning of the revelation. As for the means, we have explained that it means nearness and proximity. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Al-Wasilah is the closeness. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Al-Wasilah, he said: The means of closeness and proximity.
17:58: God Almighty says: There is no town among the towns but that We will destroy its people with annihilation, annihilating them completely before the Day of Resurrection, or punishing them, either by the affliction of being killed by the sword, or by other types of punishment, a severe punishment. 0 2 239 2 - As Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection, so We will annihilate it or punish it with killing and affliction, he said: Every city on earth will be afflicted with some of this. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, in a similar manner, except that he said: This or some of it will happen to her. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it, is a decree from God, as you hear, from which there is no escape. Either He will destroy it with death or He will destroy it with an exterminating punishment if they abandon His command and deny His messengers. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And there is no city but that We will destroy it, he said: We will annihilate it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Abd Al-Rahman bin Abdullah, he said: If adultery and usury appear among the people of a village, God will permit its destruction. His saying, That was written in the Book, means in the Book in which everything that will be is written, and that is the Preserved Tablet. As Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, That was inscribed in the Book, he said: In the most complete Book, and he read, Had it not been for a previous decree from God, and he means by his statement, inscribed, written and clear, and from this is the statement of Al-Ajjaj: Know that the Majestic One has decreed in the first books that were written This is your order, so keep it to the river
17:59: .God Almighty says: And what prevented Us, O Muhammad, from sending the signs that your people asked for, except that there were nations before them who denied the same thing, and when what they asked for came to them, they denied their messengers, and they did not believe in the coming of the signs, so they were hastened, so We did not send the signs to your people. Because if We had sent them to them and they denied them, then We would have followed in hastening the punishment for them the same path as the nations before them. And what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The people of Mecca asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to turn Safa into gold for them, and to remove the mountains from them so that they could farm. It was said to him: If you wish, we can wait with them so that we may be saved from them, and if you wish, we can give them what they asked for, but if they disbelieve, they will be destroyed as those before them were destroyed. He said: Rather, wait with them. Then God revealed: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them and And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign. Ishaq bin Wahb told me: Abu Amer told us: Masoud bin Abbad told us, on the authority of Malik bin Dinar, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God Almighty: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. He said: A mercy for you, O nation. If We had sent signs and you denied them, what had befallen those before you would have befallen you. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hammad bin Zaid narrated to me, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubair, he said: The polytheists said to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Muhammad, you claim that there were prophets before you, among them was he to whom the wind was subjected, and among them was he who brought the dead back to life. If it pleases you that we believe in you and believe you, then ask your Lord to turn Safa into gold for us. So God revealed to him: I have heard what they said, so if you wish that we do what they said, then if they do not believe, then the punishment will descend, for there is no debate after the revelation of the verse. If you wish to give your people some time, then give them some time. He said: O Lord, give me some time. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them, he said: The people of Mecca said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: If what you say is true, and it pleases you that we believe, then turn Safa into gold for us. Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said: If you wish, then what your people asked of you will happen, but if it happens and they do not believe, then they will not debate. If you wish, then you can wait with your people. He said: Rather, wait with my people. Then God revealed, And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her, and God Almighty revealed, “No city believed before them which We destroyed. Will they believe?” Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, that they asked that Al-Safa be turned into gold. God said: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. Ibn Jurayj said: No sign came to a town and they denied it except that they were punished. So if I had made Al-Safa into gold for them, and if they believed, they would have been punished. And the first, which is with Our prevention, is in the accusative case because Our prevention occurs on it, and the second is in the nominative case, because the meaning of the statement is: And nothing prevented Us from sending signs except that the former peoples denied them. So the verb is because of the second. God Almighty says: “O Muhammad, your people, Thamud, asked for signs before, so We gave them what they asked for. And We made that sign a seeing she-camel.” He made sight for the she-camel, just as you say for a wound: clear. And this is a clear argument. What He meant by seeing is the luminous, clear one, such that whoever sees it will have insight into it, that it is an argument for God, just as it was said: and the day is seeing. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign. That is, clear. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, The she-camel is seeing, he said: A sign. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. And His statement, So they wronged her, the Almighty says: So they wronged her, because they killed her and hamstrung her, so their wrong was in hamstringing and killing her. It has been said that the meaning of that is: So they disbelieved in her, and there is no basis for that unless the speaker says that he meant: So they disbelieved in God by killing her, and that would be a basis. As for his saying, We do not send the signs except as a warning, he is saying: We do not send the lessons and the reminder except as a warning to the servants. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We do not send the signs except as a warning, and God frightens people with whatever sign He wills, so that they may take heed, or remember, or return. It was mentioned to us that Kufa shook during the time of Ibn Masoud, so he said: O people, your Lord is seeking your repentance, so repent to Him. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Noah bin Qais told us, on the authority of Abu Raja, on the authority of Al-Hasan, And We do not send the signs except as a warning, he said: terrible death.
17:60: This is an urging from God Almighty to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to convey His message, and an announcement from Him that He had already said to him that He would protect him from anyone who built it with evil and destruction. God Almighty says: And remember, O Muhammad, when We said to you, “Your Lord has encompassed mankind with power, so they are in His grasp and are unable to escape His will, and We will protect you from them, so do not fear anyone from them, and go forward with what We have commanded you to do, conveying Our message.” And the people of Tawbil said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Abd Al-Samad told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, who said: I heard Al-Hasan say: He surrounded the people, He protected you from the people. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Abu Bakr al-Hudhali told us, on the authority of al-Hasan: And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,’ he said: He says: I have encompassed the Arabs for you so that they will not kill you, so he knew that he would not be killed. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, He surrounded the people, he said: They are in His grasp. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Sufyan told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah ibn Al-Zubayr, regarding his statement, He surrounded the people, he said: He prevented you from the people. Muammar said, Qatadah said, something similar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,’ he said: He prevented you from the people. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And when We said to you, ‘Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people,’ meaning He prevented you from the people until you conveyed the message of your Lord. And his saying, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. The people of interpretation differed about that, and some of them said: It is a vision of the eye, and it is what the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw when he was taken on the Night Journey from Mecca to Jerusalem. Those who said that are mentioned: Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Malik bin Ismail told us, he said: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: It is a vision that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was shown with his own eyes on the night of his ascension, and it is not a vision from a dream. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who was asked about his statement, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: It is a vision that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw on the night of his Isra’. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us: Amr told us, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubayr: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: That was on the night he was taken on the Night Journey to the Holy House, and he saw what he saw, so the polytheists denied him when he told them. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: He was taken on a night journey to Jerusalem, so he prayed there, and God showed him the signs that He showed him, then he was in Mecca in the morning, and he informed them that he had been taken on a night journey to Jerusalem, so they said to him: O Muhammad, what is the matter with you, that you spent the evening there, and then you came among us in the morning telling us that you had come to Jerusalem! They were amazed at that, to the extent that some of them apostatized from Islam. Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Hudha told us, he said: Aouf told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: The infidels of Mecca said: Is it not a lie from Ibn Abi Kabsha that he claims that he traveled two months’ journey in one night?! Abu Hasin told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hasin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: His journey to Jerusalem. Abu Al-Sa’ib and Ya’qub told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, regarding his statement, And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: When he was taken on the Night Journey. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: The night he was taken on the Night Journey. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: The vision which We showed you in the Holy House when it was taken on the Night Journey, and that was a trial for the unbeliever. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. He said: God showed him signs and lessons in his journey to the Holy House. It was mentioned to us that some people apostatized after their conversion to Islam when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, told them about his journey. They denied it and denied it, and were amazed by it, and said: You told us that you traveled a journey of two months in one night! Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: It is what he was shown in the Holy House on the night of his ascension. Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, And We did not make the vision which We showed you he said: God showed him signs on the way to Jerusalem when he was taken on the Night Journey. The obligation of prayer was revealed on the night of his Night Journey, one year and nine years before he emigrated out of the ten years he spent in Mecca. Then he returned that night, and the Quraysh said: He had dinner with us and spent the morning with us. Then he claimed that he had come to Ash-Sham in one night and then returned! By God, the hawk comes to her for two months: a month coming and a month going. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: {And We did not make the vision which We showed you except a trial for the people}, he said: This was when he was taken on the Night Journey to Jerusalem, and some people were tempted by it, and they said: He goes to Jerusalem and returns in one night! And he said: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me with Buraq to carry me on it, I stood by its ears, and some parts contracted towards each other, and Gabriel looked at it and said: By He Who sent me with the truth from Him, no one better than him has ridden you from the children of Adam. He said: So I stood by its ears and sweat dripped down from under it, and the end of its steps was at the end of its eyes. So when he came to them with that, they said: Muhammad would not stop until he came with a lie that would come out of its corners. So they came to Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, and they said: This is your companion who says such and such. So he said: And he said that? They said: Yes. So he said: If he said that, then he has told the truth. So they said: Do you believe him if he said he went to Jerusalem and returned in one night? Abu Bakr said: Yes, may God take away your minds. Should I believe him with the report from heaven, when heaven is farther than Jerusalem, and should I not believe him with the report from Jerusalem? They said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: We have come to Jerusalem, so describe it to us. When they said that, God, the Blessed and Exalted, raised him up and made him look like him between his eyes, and he began to say: It is such and such, and in it is such and such. Some of them said: By your father, if he makes a mistake in it! They said: This man is a magician. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, meaning the night he was taken on the Night Journey to the Holy House, then he returned that night, and it was a trial for them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: The vision which We showed you, he said: When Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar. And others said: He saw his dream in which he saw that he was entering Mecca. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, he said: It is said that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw that he and his companions entered Mecca, and he was in Medina at that time. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, hastened to travel to Mecca before the appointed time, and the polytheists were turned back. So some people said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, has been turned back, and he had told us that he would enter it, so his return was a trial for them. Others who said: It was a dream vision said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, only saw in his dream some people climbing his pulpit. Those who said that mentioned: It was narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Zabalah, who said: Abd al-Muhin ibn Abbas ibn Sahl ibn Sa`d narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of my grandfather, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw in the valley of Banu Fulan jumping on his pulpit like monkeys, and that upset him, so he could not stop laughing until he died. He said: And God Almighty revealed about that: And We have not made the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people. The most correct of the sayings about this is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by it is the vision of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of the signs and lessons he saw on his way to the Holy House on the night of his Isra’. We mentioned some of that at the beginning of this Surah. We said that this is more correct, because of the consensus of the scholars of interpretation that this verse was revealed in this regard and that is what God Almighty meant by it. If this is the case, then the interpretation of the statement: And We did not make your vision which We showed you on the night We took you on the Night Journey from Mecca to the Holy House, except as a trial for the people means: except as a trial for the people who turned away from Islam when they were informed of the vision that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw, and for the polytheists of Mecca who, upon hearing that from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, increased in their error and disbelief upon their disbelief. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: Except as a trial for the people. As for his saying: And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, the people of interpretation differed about it. Some of them said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Malik bin Ismail told us, he said: Abu Ubaidah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Abu Jahl said: Is Ibn Abi Kabsha frightening me with the tree of Zaqqum? Then he called for dates and butter, and began to say: It frightened me, so God the Most High revealed: Its fruit is like the heads of devils, and He revealed: And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression. Abu Al-Sa’ib and Ya’qub told me: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan bin Ubaid God, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq: And the cursed tree in the Qur’an he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ubayd God, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, the same. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding His statement: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an, for the Quraysh used to eat dates and butter, and they would say: You have swallowed this Zaqqum. Abu Raja’ said: Then Abd Al-Quddus told me, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: So God described it to them in As-Saffat. Ibn Bishmar told us: He said: We are told by Hudha, he said: We are told by Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Abu Jahl and the infidels of Mecca said: Is it not from the lies of Ibn Abi Kabsha that he promises you a fire in which stones will be burned, and he claims that a tree will grow in it and the cursed tree in the Qur’an he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Yunus told me, he said: Abthar told us, he said: Hisin told us, on the authority of Abu Malik, regarding this verse, And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hisin, on the authority of Abu Malik, he recited regarding his statement, And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: It is the tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of a man called Badr, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Israel told us, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, he said: Saeed bin Jubair was asked about the cursed tree, he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik al-Azraqi, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, And the cursed tree, he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told me, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: Zaqram. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Muhajjal, on the authority of Abu Ma’shar, on the authority of Ibrahim, that he used to swear, without exception, that the cursed tree was the tree of Zaqqum. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Israel told us, on the authority of Furat al-Qazzaz, who said: I asked Saeed bin Jubair about the cursed tree in the Qur’an. He said: The tree of Zaqqum. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: It is Zaqqum. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an - and We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression - it is the tree of Zaqqum. God frightened His servants with it, so they were tempted by that, until their speaker Abu Jahl bin Hisham said: Your companion claimed that there is a tree in Hell, and fire eats trees, but by God we do not know Zaqqum to be anything but dates and foam, so they were choked! So God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed when they were amazed that there was a tree in Hell: “Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the bottom of Hellfire. Its fruit is like the heads of devils.” I created it from fire, and I punished with it whomever I wished of My servants. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the cursed tree in the Qur’an: He said: Zaqqum. That is because the polytheists said: This one tells us that there is a tree in the fire, and the fire consumes the tree until it leaves nothing of it, and that is a trial. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn bin Al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd bin Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And the cursed tree in the Qur’an, he said: The tree of Zaqqum. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an, it is the Zaqqum from which they asked God to fill their homes.
