He said: It is the saffron with foam that it spews, and saffron is a type of date. He said: Abu Jahl said: It is the saffron with foam. And they were tempted by it. Others said: He sees the dust. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Abi Fadik told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Tha’lab, on the authority of a client of Banu Hashim, who told him that Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal sent him to Ibn Abbas, asking him about the cursed tree in the Qur’an. He said: It is this tree that is twisted on the tree and placed in the water, meaning the Kashuthi. The first of the two opinions on this matter, in our view, is the correct opinion of those who said: It refers to the tree of Zaqqum, because the evidence from the scholars of interpretation is unanimous on that, and the accursed tree was put in the accusative case in apposition to the vision. So the interpretation of the statement is: And We did not make the vision which We showed you, and the accursed tree in the Qur’an except as a trial for the people. So their trial in the vision was what I mentioned of the apostasy of those who apostatized, and the persistence of the polytheists in their polytheism, when the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) informed them of what God had shown him on his journey to the Holy House on the night of his Isra’. And their trial in the accursed tree was what we mentioned of the saying of Abu Jahl and the polytheists with him: Muhammad tells us that there is a tree growing in the Fire, and the Fire consumes trees, so how can it grow in it? And His statement: And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression. He says: And We frighten these polytheists with what We threaten them with of punishments and chastisement, but Our frightening only increases them in great transgression, meaning: except for persistence and great transgression in their disbelief. That is because when they were frightened by the fire in which their food is Zaqqum, they called for dates and butter, and said: Suck on this. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Mention of those who said that: Mention of some of those who said that has been mentioned before, and we will mention some of those who remain: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj said: And the accursed tree he said: Its fruit is like the heads of devils, and devils are accursed. He said: And the accursed tree in the Qur’an when he mentioned it, it increased their temptation and transgression. God Almighty said: And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
17:61: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And remember, O Muhammad, the persistence of these polytheists in their transgression and their apostasy in transgression against their Lord by frightening them with their fulfillment of the words of their enemy and the enemy of their father, when his Lord commanded him to prostrate to Him, but he disobeyed Him and refused to prostrate to Him, out of envy and arrogance: If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few. And how they believed his assumption about them, and disobeyed the command of their Lord and His obedience, and followed the command of their enemy and the enemy of their father. What he means by his saying: And when We said to the angels: And remember when We said to the angels, Prostrate to Adam, and they prostrated, except for Iblis, for he was arrogant and said, Should I prostrate to one You created from clay? He says: to one You created from clay. So when the word whom was deleted, it was attached to his saying, created, so it was placed in the accusative case. The ignorant person boasts about him that he was created from fire, and Adam was created from clay. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Lord of Glory, Blessed and Exalted be He, sent Iblis, so he took from the earth’s crust, from its sweetness and its salt, and created Adam from it. So everything He created from its sweetness is destined for happiness, even if it is the son of disbelievers, and everything He created from its salt is destined for misery, even if it is the son of prophets. Hence Iblis said, Should I prostrate to one You created from clay? meaning: This clay I brought. And hence he was called Adam, because he was created from the earth’s crust.
17:62: And His saying: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? God Almighty says: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me, so You commanded me to prostrate to him, and by that He means Adam. If You delay me? The enemy of God swore, and said to his Lord: If You delay my destruction until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few. He says: I will take control of them, and I will eradicate them, and I will win them over! It is said from this: So-and-so seizes what so-and-so has of money or knowledge or other than that, and from this is the saying of the poet: We complain to you about a year that has oppressed us from one effort to another, and has weakened us. And our money was seized and plundered And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few, he said: I will contain them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement: I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few, meaning: I will take control. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: I will surely seize his descendants, except for a few, he said: I will surely lead them astray. And these words, even though they differ, are close in meaning, because taking control and containing have one meaning, so when he took control of them, he led them astray.
17:63: God Almighty said to Iblis when He said to him, If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few. Go, for I have delayed you. Whoever follows you from among them, meaning from the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, and obeys you, then Hell is your reward and their reward. He says: Your reward for calling them to disobey Me, and their reward for following you and disobeying My command. A full reward, He says: A great and complete reward. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement: “He said: Go, and whoever follows you among them, then indeed, Hell is your recompense, an ample recompense.” The punishment of Hell is their recompense, and a punishment from God against His enemies, so nothing of its punishment will be spared from them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Indeed, Hell is your recompense, a full recompense. He said: Ample. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, mawfuran, he said: abundant.
17:64: The Most High means by His saying and provoke and to belittle and treat with disdain, from their saying: provoke someone to such and such, so he provokes him whoever you can among them with your voice. The people of interpretation differed about the sound that the Most High meant by His saying and provoke whoever you can among them with your voice. Some of them said: He meant by it: the sound of singing and playing. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, he said: with amusement and singing. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Layth mention, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice, he said: Playing and amusement. Others said: What he meant by and incite whomever you can among them is by calling him to obey you and disobey God. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And incite with your voice whomever you can among them. He said: His voice is every caller who calls to disobeying God. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice. He said: With your supplication. The most correct of the sayings about this is that it is said that God, the Blessed and Exalted, said to Satan: And incite from the descendants of Adam whomever you can incite with your voice. He did not specify one voice over another, for every voice was a call to Him and to His work and obedience, and unlike the call to obey God, it is included in the meaning of His voice about which God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: And incite whomever you can among them with your voice. And His statement: And assault them with your cavalry and infantry, meaning: And gather against them from the riders of your army and their foot soldiers those who will incite them with the call to obey You and divert them from My obedience. It is said from this: So-and-so incited against so-and-so inciting, meaning he shouted at him. And the noise is the voice, and it may be said: what is this incitement, just as it is said: victory and victory, and compassion and tenderness. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Salim bin Janada told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Layth mention on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And attack them with your cavalry and infantry, he said: Every rider and pedestrian who commits sins against God Almighty. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And attack them with your cavalry and infantry. He said: He has cavalry and infantry from among the jinn and mankind, and they are the ones who obey him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And attack them with your cavalry and your infantry. He said: The men, the infantry. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And attack them with your cavalry and your infantry, he said: His cavalry: every rider in disobedience to God, and his infantry: every foot soldier in disobedience to God. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And attack them with your cavalry and your infantry, he said: Whoever is riding and fighting in disobedience to God is from the cavalry of Satan, and whoever is on foot in disobedience to God is from the men of Satan. And man is the plural of man, just as trade is the plural of merchant, and companion is the plural of companion. As for his saying, And share with them in wealth and children, the people of interpretation differed regarding the sharing that was meant by his saying, And share with them in wealth and children. Some of them said: It is his command to them to spend their wealth in other than obedience to God and to acquire it in an unlawful manner. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Layth mention on the authority of Mujahid, And share with them in the money that they acquired illegally. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And share with them in the wealth, he said: What was eaten from the wealth without obeying God. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Talha bin Amr, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, he said: Shirk in usurious money. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: By God, he shared with them in their wealth, and God gave them wealth, and they spent it in obedience to Satan, in a way that is not due to God, blessed be His name, and this is the statement of Qatada. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Hasan said: And share with them in the wealth means he ordered them not to earn it from evil and to spend it on what is forbidden. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: All wealth is in disobedience to God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: His sharing with them in wealth and children, what he made attractive to them in it of the sins of God until they committed them. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid: And share with them in the wealth means everything that they spent in an unlawful manner. Others said: Rather, what was meant by that was everything that the polytheists forbade from what they forbade from livestock, such as the bahā’ir and the sawa’ib and the like. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: Wealth is what they were forbidden from their livestock. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Imran bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: His participation in wealth is that they made the bahīrah, the sā’ibah, and the wasīlah for other than God. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And share with them in the wealth. He did that. As for the wealth, he ordered them to make Bahirah, Sa’ibah, Wasilah, and Ham. Abu Jaafar said: The correct answer is: Hami. Others said: Rather, he meant what the polytheists used to slaughter for their gods. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: And share with them in wealth and children, meaning what they used to slaughter for their gods. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: What is meant by that is every wealth in which God was disobeyed by spending it in something forbidden or earning it from something forbidden, or slaughtering it for the gods, or letting it go, or giving it to Satan, and other things that were disobeyed by it or in it, because God said, And share with them in the wealth, so every wealth in which Satan was obeyed and God was disobeyed, the one who did that has Satan as a partner in it, so there is no reason to specify some of it and not others... And His saying, and the children, the people of interpretation differed regarding the nature of his sharing with the children of Adam, so some of them said: His sharing with them in them by their fornication with their mothers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: The children of fornication. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me, he said: Ibn Idris told us, he said: I heard Layth mention on the authority of Mujahid, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: The children of fornication. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us. And Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And share with them in the wealth and children, he said: The children of fornication. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: The children of fornication. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say: And share with them in wealth and children. He said: The children of fornication, meaning by that the people of polytheism. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and share with them in wealth and children, he said: The children are the children of fornication. Others said: What he meant by that is: burying their children alive and killing them. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And share with them in wealth and children, he said: What they killed of their children, and committed unlawful acts among them. Others said: Rather, what he meant by that is: their dyeing them in disbelief. Mentioned by Qom: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: And he shared with them in wealth and children. He said: By God, he shared with them in their wealth and children, so they became Zoroastrians, Jews, Christians, and dyed themselves a dye other than Islam, and they gave a portion of their wealth to Satan. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And share with them in wealth and children. He said: He did that, but as for the children, they made them Jews, Christians, and Magians. Others said: Rather, he meant by that that they named their sons Abd al-Harith and Abd Shams. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Imran bin Sulayman, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And he shared with them in wealth and children. He said: He shared with them in children. They were named Abd al-Harith, Abd al-Shams, and Abd so-and-so. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: Every child born to a female who disobeys God by naming him with something God hates, or by introducing him to a religion other than the one God has chosen, or by committing adultery with his mother, or by killing him or burying him alive, or other matters by which God is disobeyed by doing something to him or in him, then he has entered into the partnership of Satan in him with the child born to him or from him, because God did not specify in His statement and share with them in wealth and children the meaning of partnership in it with one meaning and not another. So everything in which God is disobeyed or with which Satan is obeyed, then he is a partner in it with the one in which God is disobeyed or with which Satan is disobeyed. And His statement, And He promised them, but Satan promises them nothing but delusion, is that God Almighty says to Satan: He promised your followers from the descendants of Adam victory over those who wanted to harm them. God says, And Satan promises them nothing but delusion, because he will not save them from God’s punishment if something befalls them. They are His enemies in falsehood and deception, as the enemy of God said to them when the truth became clear, “Indeed, God promised you the promise of truth, and I promised you, but I failed you. And I had no authority over you except that I called you and you responded to me. So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, and you cannot help me. Indeed, I have disbelieved in what you associated with Him before.”
17:65: God Almighty says to Satan: My servants who obeyed Me, followed My command and disobeyed you, O Satan, you have no argument against them. And His saying, And sufficient is your Lord as a Disposer of affairs, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And sufficient for you, O Muhammad, is your Lord as a Guardian and a Guardian of your affairs, so obey His command and convey His messages to these polytheists, and do not fear anyone, for He has entrusted you with protecting and supporting you. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “Indeed, My servants - you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs,” and His servants are the believers, and God said in another verse, His authority is only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate others with Him.
17:66: God Almighty says to those who associate others with Him: Your Lord, O people, is the One who makes ships for you in the sea, carrying you in them so that you may seek of His bounty so that you may reach the places of your trade, your demands, and your livelihoods by riding in them, and you may seek of His provision for He is ever Merciful to you. He says: God was merciful to you when He made the ship run for you in the sea, making it easy for you to seek His bounty in distant lands that, had He not made it easy for you to reach, would have been difficult for you to reach. And similar to what we said about His statement, He will direct it for you, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you in the sea, meaning: He makes the ship run. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you in the sea. He said: He makes it sail in the sea. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you through the sea. He said: It runs. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Your Lord is He who drives the ship for you in the sea, he said: He makes it run.
17:67: God Almighty says: And when hardship and distress befall you at sea, those you call upon go astray. He says: Then those you call upon besides God of rivals and gods have gone astray from your path and have not helped you, and you have not found any helper other than God to help you, you called upon Him, but when you called upon Him and He helped you, and answered your call and saved you from the terror of what you were in at sea, you turned away from what your Lord had called you to, of removing rivals, disavowing the gods, and singling Him out as divinity, out of disbelief on your part for His favor. And man is ever ungrateful. He says: And when man denies the favors of his Lord…
17:68: God Almighty says: Have you then felt secure O people, from your Lord, and you have disbelieved in His blessing in saving you from the terror you were in at sea, and the enormity of what you were on the verge of destruction, but when He saved you and you reached the land, you disbelieved and associated others with Him in His worship that He would cause a side of the land to swallow you up meaning the side of the land or send upon you a storm of stones meaning: or rain down upon you stones from the sky that would kill you, as He did with the people of Lot and then you would not find for yourselves a protector meaning: then you would not find for yourselves what would defend you from His punishment and what would protect you from it. And similar to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Do you then feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you up or send upon you a storm of stones? He said: stones from the sky. Then you will not find for yourselves a protector: meaning, protection or helper. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, Do you feel secure that He will not cause a part of the land to swallow you up or send upon you a storm of stones? He said: A rain of stones when you come out of the sea. Some Arabists interpreted his statement, Or He sends upon you a hailstorm, as: Or He sends upon you a violent wind that blows hailstones. He cited as evidence for his statement the following poet’s statement: We are receiving a reception in northern Syria that will strike us with hailstones like scattered cotton wool. The origin of the word hasib is the wind that throws pebbles, and pebbles are the ground that contains sand and small pebbles. It is said in speech that someone threw pebbles at someone, meaning he threw pebbles at him. The wind was described as throwing pebbles because people throw them at it, as Al-Akhtal said: I knew that when the tithes set out, the royal camels would throw them northward. The tree throws hailstones of its snow until it sleeps on the tree, stumbling over it.
17:69: God Almighty says: Or do you, O people, feel secure from your Lord, and you have disbelieved in Him after His favor upon you, the favor which you knew, that He will return you to the sea another time? He says: another time, and the letter ha in His statement in it is from the mention of the sea. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, That He may return you to it another time, meaning in the sea once again, and send upon you a violent wind, which is the one that blows away whatever it passes over, shattering and crushing it, from their saying: So-and-so broke the back of so-and-so, and drowns you because of your disbelief, meaning: God will drown you with this violent wind because of your disbelief in Him, meaning: because of your disbelief in Him. Then you will not find for yourself against Us a follower, meaning: Then you will not find for yourself against Us a follower who follows us because of what we did to you, nor a revenger who takes revenge on us by destroying you. It was said: Tabi’a is in place of tabi’, just as it was said: Alim is in place of Alim. The Arabs say for anyone seeking blood money or a debt or something else: Tabi’a. And from this is the saying of the poet: They came back and their gazelles came back, as if they were guaranteeing a fine for the loss of their camels. And similar to what we said about the Qasif and the Tabii’, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then He will send upon you a violent wind, meaning: a storm. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Thi Hajjaj, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Qasifa is the one that drowns. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then you will not find for yourselves against Us a follower thereof, meaning a supporter. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Muhammad said: Tha’ir, and Al-Harith said: Nasir Tha’ir. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: Then you will not find for yourselves against us a follower of it. He said: A rebel. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then you will not find any follower of it against us. That is, we do not fear that we will be followed by anything of that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then you will not find anyone to follow us in it. He said: No one will follow us in anything of that. The plural of tarat is tarat and tir, and the verb af’alta from it is atarat.
17:70: God Almighty says: And We have certainly honored the children of Adam by giving them dominion over other creation, and by subjecting all creation to them. And We carried them on land on the backs of beasts and ships, and in the sea in the ships that We subjected to them. And We provided them with good things meaning: good foods and drinks. These are permissible and delicious. And We preferred them over many of those We have created, with [definite] preference. He mentioned to us that this enabled them to work with their hands, and to take food and drink with them and raise them to their mouths, and this is not possible for other creation. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, he said, And We have preferred them in the hands with which they eat and work, and all other than humans eat with other than that. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us on the authority of Zayd bin Aslam, regarding His statement, And We have certainly honored the children of Adam, he said: The angels said, O our Lord, You gave the children of Adam the world to eat from and enjoy, but You did not give us that, so give it to us in the Hereafter! He said, By My glory, I will not make the offspring of one I created with My hands like one to whom I said, ‘Be,’ and he was.
17:71: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the Imam whom God Almighty mentioned that He calls all people with. Some of them said: He is His Prophet, and whoever follows his example in this world and takes him as an example. Who said that? Yahya bin Talha Al-Yarboui told me: Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid: On the Day We will call every people with their leader, he said: their prophet. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, on the authority of Mujahid: On the Day We will call every people with their leader, he said: their prophet. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: With their Imam he said: their Prophet. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Every people is guided by their Imam, he said: their Prophet. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, similarly. Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that he calls them with the books of their deeds that they did in this world. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, On the Day We will call every people with their leader, he said: The leader is what he did and dictated, and it was written for him. So whoever is sent fearing God, his book will be placed in his right hand, so he will read it and be happy, and he will not be wronged a thread. It is like His statement, And indeed, they are at a clear leader. The leader is what he dictated and did. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan: On the Day when We will call every people with their leader, he said: with their deeds. Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said: In their book in which their deeds are contained. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day We will call every people with their leader, meaning: with their book. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: By their deeds. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: The day when We will call every people with their book in which I revealed to them My commands and prohibitions. Who said that? 22526 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: I heard Yahya bin Zaid regarding the statement of God Almighty, On the Day We will call every people with their leader, he said: With their book in which He revealed to them God’s commands and prohibitions and His obligations, and by which they will be held accountable. And he recited, For each of you We prescribed a law and a method, he said: The law is the religion, and the method is the Sunnah. And he recited, He has prescribed for you of religion what He enjoined upon Noah, he said: So Noah was the first of them, and you are the last of them. 22527 - Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: On the Day We will call every people with their leader with their book. The most correct of these sayings in our view is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: On the Day when we will call every people with their imam whom they followed and followed in this world, because the majority of the Arabs use the word imam to mean someone who was followed and followed, and directing the meanings of God’s words to the most popular is more appropriate unless there is evidence to the contrary that must be accepted. And His statement, So whoever is given his record in his right hand, means: So whoever is given the record of his deeds in his right hand, These will read their record, that is, so that they may know everything in it, and they will not be wronged a thread, God Almighty says: And God will not wrong them in the recompense of their deeds a thread, and it is the twisted thread in the slit of the pit. The explanation of the thread has already passed, so there is no need to repeat it in this place. 22528 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they will not be wronged a thread, he said: What is in the crack of the seed.
17:72: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning indicated by his saying this. Some of them said: This indicates the blessings that God Almighty enumerated in his saying: “And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.” Then he said: And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and even further astray. Who said that? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Abd al-A'la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who said: He was asked about this verse: And whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray. He said: He said: "And We have certainly honored the children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference." He said: Whoever is blind to being grateful for these blessings in this world will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Whoever is blind in this world to the power of God therein and His proofs will be blind in the Hereafter. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And whoever is blind in this world, meaning: whoever is blind to God’s power in this world, will be blind in the Hereafter. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, In this is a blind man, he said: the world. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter, meaning: whoever is blind in this world to what he sees in it of God’s blessings, creation, and wonders, will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray in what he does not know of the matter of the Hereafter and blind. Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And whoever is blind in this world in what God showed him of His signs of the creation of the heavens and the earth and the mountains and the stars is blind in the Hereafter the unseen which he did not see and further astray from the path. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and he was asked about the statement of God the Most High: And whoever is blind in this [world] will be blind in the Hereafter and even more astray from the way. So he recited: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers. “And in yourselves, then will you not see?” And he recited: And among His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly, you are human beings dispersing. And he recited until he reached: “And to Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. All are devoutly obedient to Him.” He said: All are obedient to Him, except the son of Adam. He said: So whoever is blind in these signs that he knows are from Us, and bears witness to them while he sees Our power and blessings, he will be blind in the Hereafter, which he did not see, and even more astray from the way. The first and most correct of the sayings in this regard, in my opinion, is the saying of those who said: The meaning of this is: And whoever is blind in this world to the proofs of God, that He is the One Who is alone in creating and managing it, and disposing of what is in it, then he is blind in the matter of the Hereafter, which he has not seen or witnessed, and in what is to come in it, and more astray in his path. He says: And more astray in his path than in the matter of this world, which he has witnessed and witnessed. And we said: This is the most correct of its interpretations, because God, the Most High, did not specify in His statement, And whoever is blind in this world, the blindness of the disbeliever in Him to some of His proofs against him in it without others, so that it is directed to his blindness to His blessings in what He bestowed upon him of honoring the children of Adam, and carrying them on land and sea, and what He enumerated in the verse in which He mentioned His blessings upon them, but He made the report general about his blindness in this world, so they are as God, the Most High, was obscured. And the reciters differed in the reading of His statement, So he is blind in the Hereafter, so all the reciters broke, I mean the first letter of His statement, And whoever is blind in this. As for his saying, He is blind in the Hereafter, most of the Kufi reciters also inclined his saying, He is blind in the Hereafter. As for some of the Basran reciters, they opened it and interpreted it to mean: He is more blind in the Hereafter. He cited as evidence for the correctness of his reading his saying, and more astray in the way. This reading is the more correct of the two readings in that regard, based on the evidence we mentioned from its reciter as well. The reason for the one who disliked reading it as such was that he thought that it was intended to mean blindness of the eyes, which no one can be described as being more blind than another, since blindness of sight does not vary, so that one of them is more blind than the other, except by introducing something more severe or more obvious. This is not the case in that. Rather, we said: Is that from the blindness of the heart in which there is a difference? Rather, what was meant by it was the blindness of the hearts of the disbelievers, from the proofs of God that their eyes have seen, so that is why it was permissible and good. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? 22535 A - Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujayid, So he is blind in the Hereafter. He said: Blind to his argument in the Hereafter.
17:73: The people of interpretation differed regarding the temptation that the polytheists almost tempted the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with, from what God revealed to him to something else. Some of them said: That was the familiarity with the gods because the polytheists called him to that, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was tempted by it. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub al-Qummi told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to touch the Black Stone, but the Quraysh prevented him and said: We will not let him touch our gods. So he thought to himself and said: What does it matter if I touch them after he calls me to touch the stone, and God knows that I am reluctant to do so? But God refused, so God revealed: And they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, so that you might invent something else about Us. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little. It was mentioned to us that the Quraysh were alone with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, one night until morning, talking to him, exaggerating, blackening and approaching him. Among their words was that they said: You are doing something that no one else among the people has done, and you are our master and the son of our master. They continued talking to him until he was about to attack them, then God prevented him and protected him from that, so He said, And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: So that you may fabricate against us something other than it. He said: They surrounded him one night and said: You are our master and the son of our master. They wanted him to do some of what they wanted, so they thought he would commit some of what they wanted, then God protected him. So that is what His statement: You almost inclined to them a little is what they wanted, so they thought he would commit some of what they wanted. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: They said to him: Go to our gods and touch them, so that is what he said, a little. Others said: That was only because the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to delay the people’s conversion to Islam for a period of time that they asked him to delay. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, “And they almost tempted you away from that which We revealed to you, so that you might invent something else about Us. And then they would have taken you as a friend.” That is because the Thaqif people said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: O Messenger of God, give us a year until our gods are guided. Then when we take away the one who is guided to our gods, we will take him, then we will submit and break the gods. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, thought about giving them a year and giving them a year, but God said, And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little. The correct thing to say about this is that God, the Most High, mentioned that He informed His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the polytheists almost tempted him to do something other than what God revealed to him, and that is a slander against God. It is possible that this was what was mentioned about them that they invited him to touch their gods and be intimate with them, and it is possible that this was what was mentioned about Ibn Abbas regarding the matter of Thaqeef and their questioning of him from what we mentioned, and it is possible that it was something else, and there is no clarification in the Book or in a report that cuts off the excuse as to which of them it was, and the difference of opinion about it exists according to what we mentioned, so there is nothing in it that is more correct than believing in its apparent meaning, until a report comes that must be submitted to with an explanation of what was meant by that from it. And His saying, And if they had done so, they would have taken you as a friend. God Almighty says: And if you had done what they called you to do of temptation away from that which We revealed to you, they would have taken you as a friend for themselves, and you would have been for them and they would have been your friends.
17:74: The statement in the interpretation of the words of God Almighty: And had We not strengthened you, O Muhammad, by protecting you from what these polytheists called you to of temptation, You would have almost inclined towards them a little. He says: You would have almost inclined towards them and felt a little reassured, and that is what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, intended to do, which was to do some of what they had asked him to do, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, as mentioned when this verse was revealed, what: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And had We not strengthened you, you would have almost inclined toward them a little, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not leave me to myself for the blink of an eye.
17:75: God Almighty says: If you had inclined towards these polytheists, O Muhammad, a little in what they asked of you, then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death. And similar to what we have said about that, the people of interpretation said. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Then We would have made you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death, meaning: double the punishment of this world and the hereafter. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, the weakness of life, he said: its torment, and the weakness of death, he said: the torment of the Hereafter. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then We will surely make you taste double the punishment of life and double the punishment of death: meaning the torment of this world and the hereafter. Muhammad told us, he said: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The weakness of life and the weakness of death. He said: The torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say about His statement, The double of life and the double of death, meaning the torment of this world and the torment of the Hereafter. Some of the Arab scholars from Basra used to say about His statement, Then We would surely make you taste double of life, it is abbreviated, like saying, The double of the torment of life and the double of death, so they are two torments, the torment of death is doubled by the torment of life. And His statement, Then you will not find for yourself against Us a helper, means: Then you will not find for yourself, O Muhammad, if We make you taste, because of your reliance on these polytheists, if you had relied on them, the torment of life and the torment of death against Us, a helper who would help you against Us, prevent you from your torment, and save you from the punishment that befell you from Us.
17:76: The Almighty says: These people are to provoke you from the land: He says: To make you disappear from the land you are in so that they can expel you from it. And then they will not remain behind you except a little. He says: And if they expel you from it, they will not remain behind you except a little, until I destroy them with a sudden punishment. The people of interpretation differed about those who almost provoked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to expel him from the land and the land from which they wanted to expel him. Some of them said: Those who almost provoked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from that were the Jews, and the land from which they wanted to expel him was Medina. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir bin Sulayman told us, on the authority of his father, who said: A Hadrami claimed that it had reached him that some Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: The land of the prophets is the land of Ash-Sham, and this is not the land of the prophets. So God revealed: And they almost tempted you to leave the land to expel you from it. Others said: Rather, the people who did that were Quraysh, and the land was Mecca. Those who said that mentioned: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, “And indeed they almost drove you from the land to expel you from it. And then they would not have remained behind you except a little.” The people of Mecca intended to expel the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca, and if they had done that they would not have settled there. But God restrained them from expelling him until He commanded him, and despite that they hardly remained after the departure of the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca until God sent killing upon them on the day of Badr. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: To provoke you from the land. He said: They did that after that, so God destroyed them on the day of Badr, and they did not live long after that until God destroyed them on the day of Badr. And that was God’s way with the messengers when their people did something like that to them. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Your disagreement except for a little, he said: If the Quraysh had expelled Muhammad, they would have been punished for that. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Mujahid narrated: The same. The two opinions that I consider most correct in this regard are those of Qatadah and Mujahid, because His statement, And they almost drove you away from the land, is in the context of God Almighty’s report about the Quraysh and His mention of them, and the Jews were not mentioned before that. So His statement, And they almost, is directed to it being report about them, so it is more appropriate for it to be report about someone who was mentioned than anyone else. As for the little that God Almighty excluded in His statement, And then they will not remain behind you except for a little, it is, according to what has been said, what happened between the departure of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from Mecca until God killed those of their polytheists at Badr. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And then they will not remain behind you except a little, meaning by a little the day they were captured at Badr, so that was the little that they remained after that. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And then they will not remain behind you except a little, the little time they remained after the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, left their midst to Badr, and he seized them with punishment on the day of Badr. And what he meant by his statement, your opposition is after you, as the poet said: After the spray, he spread a mat between them. He means by his saying: its opposite: after it. It has been narrated from some of them that he used to read it: behind you. The meaning of that, and the meaning of the disagreement in this place, is the same.
17:77: God the Most High says: If they had expelled you, they would not have remained behind you except a little, and We would have destroyed them with a punishment from Us. This is Our way with those whom We sent before you of Our messengers. For this is how We used to do with nations when they expelled their messengers from among them. The word sunnah was used in the accusative case for exit because the meaning of this is: We would have punished them after a little while, as is Our way with the nations of those whom We sent before you of Our messengers. You will not find in Our way any change from what it has done. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, The way of those We sent before you of Our messengers, and you will not find in Our way any change, meaning the way of the nations and messengers before you was like this when they denied their messengers and expelled them, they did not argue that God had sent down His punishment upon them.
17:78: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, Establish prayer, O Muhammad, at the decline of the sun. The people of interpretation differed regarding the time that God meant by the decline of the sun. Some of them said: It is the time of its setting, and the prayer that he was commanded to perform at that time is the sunset prayer. Those who said that mentioned: Wasil bin Abdul A’la Al-Asadi told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, meaning Al-Shaibani, on the authority of Abdul Rahman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of his father, that he was with Abdullah bin Masoud, on a roof when the sun set. The sun, so he recited, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, until he finished the verse, then he said: By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, this is when the sun declines and the fasting person breaks his fast, and it is the time for prayer. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saad, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Abd al-Ghafir, that Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah wrote to him that Abdullah ibn Masoud used to pray the Maghrib prayer when the sun set, and break his fast at that time if he was fasting, and swear an oath on it, as he swears on any of the prayers, by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the time for this prayer, and he would recite its interpretation from the Book of God: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. Muhammad bin Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: This is the decline of the sun, and this is the darkness of the night, and he pointed to the east and the west. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: Ibn Abbas said: The setting of the sun means its setting, he says: It set in a vast expanse. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of al-Aswad, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: When the sun set, it went out, meaning it left a wide space. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Its setting is its sunset. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqatada: It was mentioned to us that Ibn Masoud used to pray it when it was obligatory, and he would break his fast at that time if he was full. Then he would swear by it an oath that he did not swear by any of the prayers, by God, besides whom there is no god, that this hour is the time for this prayer. Then he would recite and pray it, and its confirmation is from the Book of God: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, he said: My father used to say: Its decline is when the sun sets until the darkness of the night falls. He said: It is the sunset when the night falls, and the sun declines to set. Saeed bin Al-Rabi’ narrated to me, he said: Sufyan bin Uyaynah narrated to us, Amr bin Dinar heard Abu Ubaidah bin Abdullah bin Masoud say: Abdullah bin Masoud used to pray the Maghrib prayer when the sun’s edge set, and he swore that it was the time about which God said: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said when the sun set: This is, by God, there is no god but Him, the time for this prayer. He said: Its decline is its setting. Others said: The decline of the sun is its inclination to the meridian, and the prayer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded to be performed at its decline is the noon prayer. Those who said that were mentioned: Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Amara ibn Umair, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: Its declination is its inclination, meaning the sun. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said, regarding His statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun, he said: Its decline means its disappearance. Musa bin Abdul Rahman told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Abdul Hamid bin Jaafar, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, regarding his statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun, he said: Its decline is its inclination. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Sayyar bin Salamah, on the authority of Abu Barzah Al-Aslami, regarding his statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun, he said: When it has passed its zenith. Ibn Hamid told us again, he said: Abu Tamila told us, he said: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us, he said: Sayyar ibn Salamah Al-Riyahi told us, he said: I came to Abu Barzah and my father asked him about the prayer times of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun had declined, then he recited: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. Al-Husayn bin Ali Al-Sada’i told me, he said: My father told us, he said: Thana Mubarak, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: God Almighty said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. He said: The noon prayer is its decline, when it has passed the sky and has a shadow on the earth. Yaqoub told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun, he said: Its decline means its disappearance. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, similarly. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Ibn Yaman told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ja’far, on the authority of Abu Ja’far, regarding Establish prayer at the decline of the sun, he said: at the zenith of the sun. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: The sun’s decline: its deviation after noon, meaning the shadow. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The decline of the sun, he said: When it deviates from the middle of the sky. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Establish prayer at the decline of the sun means when the sun has passed its zenith for the noon prayer. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, at the decline of the sun, he said: when it declines. Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Mujahid said: The sun’s decline is when it sets. The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion of the one who said: Establish prayer at the sun’s decline means the noon prayer. This is because decline in the speech of the Arabs means inclination. It is said from this: So-and-so leaned towards such-and-such: if he leaned towards it. And from this is the report narrated from Al-Hasan that a man said to him: Does the man give you his wife? He meant by that: Does he incline her to delay her right? And from this is the saying of the rajaz poet: This is the place where my feet will stand, Rabah, until I rub them in the open space. It is narrated: Barah with the opening of the Baa. Whoever narrates it as Barah with the breaking of the Baa, then it means: that the observer places his hand on his eyebrow from its rays, to see what he encounters from its changes. This is the interpretation of the people of the Gharib, Abu Ubaidah, Al-Asma’i, Abu Amr Al-Shaibani and others. I have mentioned the story narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Masoud, that he said when the sun set: I rubbed Barah, meaning: Barah a place, and I do not know this interpretation, I mean his saying: Barah a place from the speech of those who are in Al-Asad, or from the speech of Abdullah, if it is from the speech of Abdullah, then there is no doubt that he was more knowledgeable about that than the people of the Gharib whose statement I mentioned, and that what is correct in that is his statement, not theirs, and if it is not from the speech of Abdullah, then the people of Arabic were more knowledgeable about that than him. And when the people of the Gharib said in that, there is evidence from the statement of Al-Ajjaj, which is his saying: The sun is about to set, I push it with my palm so it can move So he informed that he pushes its rays to look at its setting with his palm. And whoever narrated that with the opening of the Baa, then he made it a name for the sun and broke the Haa to extract it according to the estimation of Qutam, Hidham and Raqash. So if the meaning of the Duluk in the speech of the Arabs is the inclination, then there is no doubt that when the sun declines from the middle of the sky, then it has inclined to set, and that is the time of the Dhuhr prayer, and thus the report was reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, even if there is some doubt in the chain of transmission of some of it. Abu Kuraib told us: Khalid bin Mukhallad told us: Muhammad bin Jaafar told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us: Abu Bakr bin Khamro bin Hazm Al-Ansari told us, on the authority of Abu Masoud Uqba bin Amr, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to me at the decline of the sun when it had passed its zenith, and he led me in the noon prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Abu Tamila told us: Al-Husayn ibn Waqid told us: Sayyar ibn Salamah al-Riyahi told us: Abu Barzah said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray the noon prayer when the sun had declined, then he recited: Establish prayer at the decline of the sun. Ibn Hamid told us: Al-Hakam bin Bashir told us: Amr bin Qais told us, on the authority of Sayyar bin Abi Laila, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Jabir bin Abdullah, who said: I invited the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and whoever of his companions wanted to eat with me, then they went out when the sun declined. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out and said: Go out, O Abu Bakr, the sun has set. Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Razi told me: Sahl ibn Bakkar told us: Abu Awana told us, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Qays, on the authority of Nabih al-Anzi, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, similar to the hadith of Ibn Humayd. So if what we have said is correct, based on what we have cited as evidence, then it is clear that the meaning of His statement, may He be glorified and exalted, Establish prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night, is that the noon and afternoon prayers, within their limits, are among the prayers that God has made obligatory upon you in them, because they are the two prayers that God made obligatory upon His Prophet from the time of the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. The darkness of the night is its approach and its nearness with its darkness, as the poet said: This night has returned when it has become dark. And similar to what we have said about that, the people of interpretation said, with their differences, about the prayer that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was commanded to be established in his presence. Some of them said: The prayer that was commanded to be established in his presence is the sunset prayer. Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Establish prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. He said: The darkness of al-Layl 92:the beginning of the night. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, he said: I heard Ikrimah asked about this verse: Establish prayer from the decline of the sun until the darkness of the night. He said: The beginning of the night. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: The darkness of the night is the setting of the sun. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: The darkness of the night means the sunset prayer. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, Until the darkness of the night means the beginning of the night for the Maghrib prayer. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: A group of my nation will remain upon the fitrah as long as they pray the Maghrib prayer before the stars appear. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, until the darkness of the night, meaning the darkness of the night. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: My father used to say: The darkness of the night means the darkness of the night. Others said: It is the afternoon prayer. Mention of those who said that: Abu Kuraib narrated: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, on the authority of Ash'ath, on the authority of Ja'far, on the authority of Abu Ja'far: Until the darkness of the night he said: The afternoon prayer. The more correct of the two opinions is the opinion of the one who said: The prayer that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded to be performed at the darkness of the night is the sunset prayer and nothing else, because the darkness of the night is what we described of the approach of the night and its darkness, and that does not occur except after sunset. As for the afternoon prayer, it is one of the things that are performed between the beginning of the decline of the sun and the darkness of the night, not at the darkness of the night. As for his statement, And the recitation of the Qur'an at dawn, its meaning is, And establish the Qur'an of dawn, meaning what you recite in the dawn prayer of the Qur'an, and the Qur'an is connected to the prayer in his statement, Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun. Some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The accusative of his statement and the Qur’an of dawn is for enticement, as if he said: And upon you is the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed. He says: What you recite in the dawn prayer of the Qur’an is witnessed, witnessed, as he mentioned, by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. And Ba Arzi said about that, the people of interpretation said, and the traces came from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Mention of those who said that: Ubaid bin Asbat bin Muhammad Al-Qurashi told me: My father told me, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding this verse: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” He said: It is witnessed by the angels of the night and the angels of the day. Muhammad ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: Adam narrated to us, saying: Laith ibn Sa`d narrated to us, and Muhammad ibn Sahl ibn `Askar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, saying: Laith ibn Sa`d narrated to us, on the authority of Ziyadah ibn Muhammad, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, on the authority of Fadala ibn `Ubayd, on the authority of Abu al-Darda`, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God opens the remembrance in three hours remaining of al-Layl 92:in the first hour of them He looks in the book which no one looks at but Him, erasing what He wills and confirming. Then He descends in the second hour to the Garden of Eden, which is His home that no eye has seen, nor has it crossed the mind of man, and it is His dwelling place, and none of the children of Adam dwell with Him except three: the prophets, the truthful ones, and the martyrs. Then He says: Blessed is he who has entered you. Then He descends in the third hour to the lowest heaven with His spirit and His angels, and it shakes itself, and He says: Arise with My help. Then He looks down upon His servants and says: Whoever seeks My forgiveness, I will forgive him. Whoever asks Me, I will give him. Whoever calls upon Me, I will answer him! Until dawn breaks, when he says, “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” Moses said in his hadith: God, the angels of the night, and the angels of the day witnessed it. Ibn Askar said in his hadith: God, the angels of the night, and the angels of the day witnessed it. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Uqbah ibn Abd al-Ghafir, who said: Abu Ubaidah ibn Abdullah said: Abdullah used to say that at the time of the dawn prayer the two guards of God’s angels would gather and recite this verse: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” The recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is the morning prayer. We used to say that at that time the two guards of God’s angels gather: the guards of the night and the guards of the day. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And the Qur’an of dawn means the dawn prayer. As for his statement: It was witnessed, he is saying: The angels of the night and the angels of the day witness that prayer. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr Ibn Murrah, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, on the authority of `Abdullah, that he said regarding this verse, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is ever witnessed.” He said: The angels of the day descend and the angels of the night ascend. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Dhirar bin Abdullah bin Abi Al-Hudhayl, on the authority of Abu Ubaidah, regarding his statement, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” He said: The guards of the night and the guards of the day from the angels witness it in the dawn prayer. Abu Al-Sa’ib told us: Abu Mu’awiyah told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding His statement, “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” He said: They used to say that the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer and they all bear witness to it, then these ascend and those stand. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed.” He meant the dawn prayer. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And the Qur’an of dawn, he said: the dawn prayer. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is the morning prayer. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed he said: The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the Qur’an of dawn, meaning the morning prayer. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, Ibn Zayd said: And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn he said: the dawn prayer. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed he said: witnessed by the angels in what they mention. He said: Ali ibn Abi Talib and Ubayy ibn Ka’b used to say: The middle prayer that God has urged us to do is the dawn prayer. He said: That is because the noon prayer and the afternoon prayer are the prayers of the day, and the sunset and night prayers are the prayers of the night, and it is between them, and it is a prayer of sleep, and we do not know of a prayer that is neglected like it. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Abu Al-Ward Ibn Thamamah, on the authority of Abu Muhammad Al-Hadrami, he said: Ka`b told us in this mosque, he said: By the One in Whose Hand is Ka`b’s soul, this verse, “And the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn. Indeed, the recitation of the Qur’an at dawn is witnessed,” is for the dawn prayer. Indeed, it is witnessed. Al-Hasan bin Ali bin Abbas told me, he said: Bishr bin Shuaib told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: Saeed bin Al-Musayyab and Abu Salamah bin Abdul-Rahman told me, that Abu Hurairah said: I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the dawn prayer. Then Abu Hurairah said: Recite if you wish: “And the Qur’an of dawn. Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, “And the Qur’an of dawn.
