Indeed, the Qur’an of dawn is witnessed.” He said: The dawn prayer is one in which the angels of the night gather? The angels of the day.
17:79: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And during part of the night, stay awake after sleep, O Muhammad, with the Qur’an, as a voluntary act of worship purely for you and not for your nation. And staying awake at night means being awake and staying awake after sleep at night. As for the awake itself, it is sleep, as the poet said: Did you not knock on our door while our companions were asleep? So the best of gifts became more generous. Al-Hutay'ah said: Did you not knock on the door of the Indians and my companions in Hawran, Hawran, the soldiers are asleep? And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: My father and Shuaib ibn al-Layth told us, on the authority of al-Layth, on the authority of Mujahid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abu Hilal, on the authority of al-A’raj, who said: Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf told me, on the authority of a man from the Ansar, that he was with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on a journey, and he said: Let me see how the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prays. He said: So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, slept, then he woke up, raised his head to the sky, and recited four verses from the end of Surat Al Imran 3:Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth. My mother shook her head with all four hands, then he went to the water-skin, took a siwak and used it to clean himself, then he performed ablution, then he prayed, then he slept, then he woke up and did as he did the first time, and they claim that it was the night prayer that God commanded him to do. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Ja`far and Abd al-Rahman told us: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Alqamah and al-Aswad, that they said: Night prayer after sleep. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Amer told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad, who said: Tahajjud is after sleep. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Yahya bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Shu’bah, who said: Abu Ishaq told us, on the authority of Muhammad bin Abd Al-Rahman bin Yazid, on the authority of Alqamah and Al-Aswad, similarly. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, he said: Tahajjud is after sleep. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Yazid told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: Tahajjud is what comes after the last evening prayer. It was narrated on the authority of Abdullah bin Saleh, on the authority of Al-Layth, on the authority of Jaafar bin Rabi’ah, on the authority of Al-A’raj, on the authority of Katheer bin Al-Abbas, on the authority of Al-Hajjaj bin Amr, who said: The night prayer is only after sleep. As for his saying, A voluntary act for you, he is saying: A voluntary act for you in addition to the obligatory acts that I have imposed upon you. There is a difference of opinion as to the meaning for which the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was singled out for this, even though the prayer of every worshipper after his prostration, if he had performed his obligatory prayers before his prostration, is a voluntary prayer, since they were not obligatory upon him. Some of them said: The meaning of his being singled out for this is that it was obligatory upon him, and for others it is voluntary. And it was said to him: Make it a voluntary prayer for you, meaning it is a surplus for you from the obligatory prayers that I have imposed upon you over what I have imposed upon others. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you, means by the additional prayer that it is specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who was commanded to pray at night and it was prescribed for him. Others said: Rather, it was said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because his doing that did not atone for any of his sins, because God Almighty had forgiven him what came before of his sin and what came after, so it was an additional prayer for him as an additional prayer. As for the rest, it is an atonement for him, but it is not an additional prayer for him. Those who said that mentioned: Al-Qasim narrated: Al-Husayn narrated: Hajjaj narrated: Ibn Jurayj narrated: Abdullah ibn Katheer narrated: Mujahid said: The voluntary prayer is for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically because his past and future sins have been forgiven. So whatever action he does other than the obligatory one is voluntary because it is not done to expiate sins, so it is voluntary and additional. People do other than the obligatory one for their sins to expiate them, so people do not have voluntary prayers. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas, because God Almighty had singled out the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for what was imposed upon him of standing at night, to the exclusion of the rest of his nation. As for what was mentioned about Mujahid in this regard, it is a statement that has no meaning, because what was mentioned about the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was most of the time he sought forgiveness for his sins after the revelation of the words of God, the Almighty, That God may forgive you what is past of your sin and what is to come. This is because this surah was revealed to him after he returned from Al-Hudaybiyyah, and When the help of God and the conquest come was revealed to him in the year he died. And it was said to him in it, “So glorify the praises of your Lord and ask His forgiveness. Indeed, He is ever Accepting of repentance.” So he, may God bless him and grant him peace, would count for himself in one sitting seeking forgiveness a hundred times, and it is known that God did not command him to seek forgiveness except when he was forgiven by his seeking forgiveness. So the reason for the corruption of what Mujahid said is clear. Ibn Wakee’ told us: My father told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Shammar, on the authority of Atiyah, on the authority of Shahr, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The voluntary prayer was only for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A voluntary act for you. He said: A voluntary act and a virtue for you. And his saying, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, and Perhaps from God is obligatory, and the reason for its being explained by the saying of the people of knowledge: Perhaps from God is obligatory, is because the believers know that God does not fail to do with His servants what He has made them hope for in terms of reward for their deeds and compensation for their obedience to Him. It is not from His attribute that deceit is present, and there is no doubt that He has made the one who said that to him hope for his benefit, if he has undertaken it and adhered to it. If the one to whom it was said adheres to it and undertakes it, and then it does not benefit him, and there is no reason that prevents him from benefiting him, along with the hope that he has given to his companion for his undertaking it and adherence to it, then he is jealous of his companion for what he did of failing to do with him in what he had made him hope for with his saying that he said to him, it was like that, and it is not permissible for the Most High to be from His attribute of deceiving His servants, it is correct and necessary that everything that He has made them hope for in terms of their obedience to Him, or in terms of an action, or a command or prohibition that He has commanded them to do, or prohibited them from doing, then He will fulfill it for them. And it is from Him like a promise that He does not fail to fulfill. They said: Perhaps, and perhaps it is obligatory from God. The interpretation of the statement: Establish the obligatory prayer, O Muhammad, at these times in which I have commanded you to establish it, and during the night, perform the obligatory prayer that I have imposed upon you, perhaps your Lord will raise you on the Day of Resurrection to a position in which you will stand, praised, praising Him, and being envied. Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that praised position. Most of the people of knowledge said: That is the position in which he, may God bless him and grant him peace, will stand on the Day of Resurrection to intercede for the people so that their Lord may relieve them of the great severity of that day that they are in. Those who said that mentioned: Muhammad ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah ibn Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The people will be gathered together on one plain, and the caller will hear them, and their sight will penetrate them, barefoot and naked as they were created, standing, not a soul being concealed except by His permission. He will be called: O Muhammad, and he will say: At your service and at your pleasure, and good is in your hands, and evil is not from you, and the guided one is the one you have guided, your servant is in your hands, and with you and to you, there is no refuge or escape from you except to you, blessed and exalted are you, glory be to you, Lord of this house, this is the praised station that God Almighty mentioned. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah ibn Zafar, on the authority of Hudhayfah, who said: The people will gather for one game. Do not hide your soul, for the first thing that Muhammad the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will call upon, and Muhammad the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will stand and say: At your service, and then he mentioned something similar. Sulayman bin Amr bin Khalid Al-Raqi told us: Issa bin Yunus told us, on the authority of Rashdin bin Kurayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. He said: The praised station is the station of intercession. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Kuhail, he said: Abu al-Zura’ told us, on the authority of Abdullah, in a story he mentioned. He said: Then the bridge will be ordered and will be struck on the bridge of Hell, and people will pass according to their deeds. Some of them will pass like lightning, like the wind, like the birds, and like the fastest of beasts, and so on until a man will pass running, then walking, until the last of them will come, stumbling on his stomach, and he will say: O Lord, why did You delay me? He will say: I did not delay You, rather it was your deeds that delayed You. He said: Then God will permit intercession, and the first intercessor on the Day of Resurrection will be Gabriel, peace be upon him, the Holy Spirit, then Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, then Moses, or Jesus. Abu al-Zura’ said: I do not know which of them he said. He said: Then your Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, will stand as a fourth, and no one will intercede after him in what he intercedes for, and it is the praised station that God mentioned: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station. Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God Almighty: “And during part of the night, pray with it as an additional prayer for you. Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praised station.” He said: The praised station is the station of intercession on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, A praised station, he said: The intercession of Muhammad on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Abu Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Asim Al-Ahwal, on the authority of Abu Uthman, on the authority of Salman, he said: It is intercession, God will intercede for him for his nation, so he is the praised station. Bishr narrated to us, Qan: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Saeed narrated to us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station, and it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given the choice between being a prophet-servant or a king-prophet, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, motioned to him: Be humble, so the Prophet of God chose to be a slave-prophet, so the Prophet of God was given two things: he is the first from whom the earth will split open, and the first to intercede. And the people of knowledge used to see that it is the praiseworthy station about which God, the Blessed and Exalted, said, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a praiseworthy station, intercession on the Day of Resurrection. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: A praiseworthy station. He said: It is intercession. God will intercede for him on behalf of his nation. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar and al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah bin Zafar, who said: I heard Hudhayfah say about His statement, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, that God will gather the people in one place where the caller will hear them, and their sight will penetrate them, barefoot and naked, as they were created silent, no soul speaking except with His permission. He said: Then Muhammad will be called, and he will say: At your service and at your pleasure, and good is in your hands, and evil is not from you, and the Mahdi is the one whom you have guided, and your servant is before you, and for you and to you, there is no refuge or escape from you except to you, blessed and exalted are you, glory be to you, Lord of the House. He said: So that is the station of praise that God mentioned, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise. Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Silah ibn Zafar, who said: Hudhayfah said: God will gather the people on one plain, where their sight penetrates and they hear the caller, barefoot and naked as they were created the first time. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, will stand and say: At your service and at your pleasure. Then he mentioned something similar, except that he said: It is the praised station. Others said: Rather, that is the praised station that God promised His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that He would send him to, and it is that He will seat him with Him on His Throne. Who said that? Abbad bin Yaqub Al-Asadi told us: Ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, he said: He will seat him with Him on His Throne. The more correct of the two statements on this is the one that is authentically reported from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. That is what: Abu Kuraib narrated to us, he said: Waki` narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud bin Yazid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise. He was asked about it, and he said: It is intercession. Ali bin Harb told us: Makki bin Ibrahim told us: Dawud bin Yazid al-Awdi told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, “On the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, ‘Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise,’ he said: It is the station in which I intercede for my nation.” Abu Utbah al-Himsi Ahmad ibn al-Faraj told us: Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us, on the authority of al-Zubaidi, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my nation will be on a hill, and my Lord will clothe me in a green garment, then I will be given permission, and I will say whatever God wills me to say, and that will be the praised station.” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam told me: Shu`ayb ibn al-Layth told us: al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Abi Ja`far, that he said: I heard Hamza ibn Abdullah ibn Umar say: I heard Abdullah ibn Umar say: The Messenger of God said: “The sun draws near until the sweat reaches the middle of the ear. While they are like that, they will seek help from Adam, peace be upon him, and he will say: ‘I am not the one who can do that.’ Then from Moses, peace be upon him, and he will say the same. Then from Muhammad, who will intercede among the creation and walk until he takes hold of a ring in Paradise. On that day, God will raise him to a praiseworthy station.” Abu Zaid Umar ibn Shabah told me: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Saeed ibn Zaid told us, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hakam: Uthman told me, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of al-Aswad and Alqamah, on the authority of Ibn Masoud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will stand in the Praised Station. A man said: O Messenger of God, what is that Praised Station? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “That will be when you are brought barefoot, naked and uncircumcised, and the first to be clothed will be Abraham, peace be upon him. He will be brought two white robes and put them on, then he will sit facing the Throne. Then my garment will be brought to him and he will put it on, and I will stand on his right in a station that no one but me will stand in, and the first and the last will envy me for it. Then a river will be opened from al-Kawthar to the Cistern.” Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Husayn, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will spread out the earth like a leather cover until there will be nothing for a human being except the space for his feet. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Then I will be the first to be called, and Gabriel, the Most Merciful, will be on my right. By God, I had never seen him before. Then I will say: ‘O Lord, this one informed me that You sent him to me.’ God Almighty will say: ‘He has spoken the truth. Then I will intercede.’ He said: ‘Then he will be the station of praise.’” Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhbari, on the authority of Ali bin al-Husayn, he said: The Prophet said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, and he mentioned something similar, and he added to it: Then I will intercede and say: O Lord, Your servants worshipped You at the ends of the earth, and it is the praised station. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Aamer told us: Ibrahim bin Tahman told us, on the authority of Adam, on the authority of Ali, who said: I heard Ibn Umar say: The people will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and each prophet will come with his nation. Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, will come at the end of the nations, he and his nation. He and his nation will ascend to a mound above the people, and he will say: O so-and-so, intercede, O so-and-so, intercede. And they will continue to return it to one another until it returns to him, and that is the praised station that God promised him. Muhammad ibn Awf told us: Haywah and Rabi’ told us: Muhammad ibn Harb told us, on the authority of al-Zubaidi, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka’b ibn Malik, on the authority of Ka’b ibn Malik, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “People will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection, and I and my nation will be on a hill, and my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, will clothe me in a green garment, then I will be given permission to say whatever God wills me to say, and that will be the praised station.” Although this is the correct interpretation of His statement, Perhaps your Lord will raise you to a station of praise, based on what we have mentioned of the narration from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, his companions, and the followers, what Mujahid said about God seating Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on His throne is a statement whose authenticity is not proven, neither from a report nor from a theoretical standpoint. This is because there is no report from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, nor from any of his companions, nor from the followers that this is impossible. As for a theoretical standpoint, all those who claim to be Muslims differed about the meaning of this in three ways: A group of them said: God Almighty is separate from His creation. Before He created things, He was, then He created things and did not touch them, and He is as He has always been. However, since the things that He created, since their terror was not touched, it is necessary that there be something separate from them, since there is no doer of things, nor is He touching bodies or separate from them. They said: If that is the case, and God Almighty is the Doer of things, and it is not permissible in their saying that He is described as being in contact with things, then it is necessary, according to their claim, that He is separate from them. According to the doctrine of these people, it is the same whether He seated Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on His throne or on the earth, since it was from their saying that His separation from His throne and His separation from His earth have one meaning in that He is separate from both of them, not in contact with either of them. Another group said: God, may He be exalted, was before He created things, nothing touched Him, and nothing was separate from Him. Then He created things and established them with His power, and just as He was before things created Him, nothing touched Him, and nothing was separate from Him. So according to the statement of these people, it is the same whether He seated Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, on His throne or on His earth, since it was the same according to their statement that His throne and His earth were neither touched nor separate from the one, just as He was neither touched nor separate from the other. Another group said: God, the Mighty and Sublime, before He created things, nothing touched Him, and nothing was separate from Him. Then He created things and created them, so He created for Himself a throne on which He sat and became in contact with Him, just as before He created things, nothing provided Him with sustenance, and nothing deprived Him of that. Then He created things, so He provided for this and deprived that, and gave this and withheld that. They said: So likewise, before He created things, nothing touched Him or was separate from Him. He created things, so He touched the throne by sitting on it, not the rest of His creation. So He touched whatever He willed of His creation, and was separate from whatever He willed of it. According to the doctrine of these people, it is the same whether He seated Muhammad on His throne or seated him on a pulpit of light, since it was from their saying that the Lord’s sitting on His throne is not a sitting that occupies the entire throne, nor is the seating of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, a reason for him to have the attribute of Lordship, nor does it remove him from the attribute of servitude to his Lord, just as the separation of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, from what was separate from Him from things does not require it. The attribute of Lordship, nor does it remove him from the attribute of servitude to his Lord because he is described as being separate from Him, just as God Almighty is described, according to the one who said this statement, as being separate from it, he is separate from Him. They said: If the meaning of separate and separate does not require Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, to leave the attribute of servitude and enter into the meaning of Lordship, then likewise it does not require him to sit on the Throne of the Most Merciful. It has become clear, then, by what we have said, that it is not impossible in the statement of one of those who claim to be Muslims what Mujahid said, that God Almighty will seat Muhammad on His Throne. If someone says: We do not deny that God seated Muhammad on His throne, but we deny that He seated him... Abbas bin Abdul-Azim told me: Yahya bin Katheer told us, on the authority of Al-Jariry, on the authority of Saif Al-Sadusi, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salam, who said: Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, will be on the throne of the Lord on the Day of Resurrection, in front of the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He. He only denies that He will seat him with Him. It was said: Do you accept that He will seat him on it and not with Him? If he accepts that, then he has come to the conclusion that He is either with Him, or that He will seat him, and God is separate from the throne, or not touching it, nor separate from it. In any of that, he said, it was an entry into some of what he was denying. If he said that it is not permissible, then it was an exit from the statement of all the groups whose statement we have mentioned, and that is a departure from the statement of all those who claim to be Muslims, since there is no statement in that except the three statements we have mentioned, and it is not impossible in one of them what Mujahid said about that.
17:80: God Almighty says to His Prophet: And say, O Muhammad, O Lord, let me enter with truth. The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the entrance of truth that God commanded His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to desire that He let him enter it, and about the exit of truth that He commanded him to desire that He let him exit it. Some of them said: He meant by the entrance of truth: the entrance of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to Medina, when he migrated to it, and the exit of truth: his exit from Mecca, when he left it migrating to Medina. Those who said that mentioned: Ibn Wakee’ and Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Qabus bin Abi Dhanyan, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: “The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, then he was commanded to emigrate, so God, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed His name: ‘And say, “My Lord, let me enter with a truthful entrance and let me exit with a truthful exit, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.”’” Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Buzay` told us: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awfi, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God, Let me enter with a truthful entrance and let me exit with a truthful exit, he said: When the infidels of Mecca conspired against the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to kill him, or expel him, or tie him up, and God wanted to fight the people of Mecca, He ordered him to go out to Medina, and he is the one about whom God said, Let me enter with a truthful entrance. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: An entrance of truth he said: Medina. An exit of truth he said: Mecca. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter with a truthful entrance and let me exit with a truthful exit.’ God brought him out from Mecca to the migration to Medina. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit,’ he said: Medina when he migrated to it, and the exit of truth: Mecca when he exited from it a truthful exit. He said that when he left as a migrant. Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: And say, ‘My Lord, let me die a truthful death, and bring me out after death from my grave on the Day of Resurrection a truthful exit.’ Mention of those who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And say, ‘My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance.’... the verse. He said: By entering he means death, and by exiting he means life after death. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: Enter me into your matter with which you sent me as prophethood with a truthful entrance, and exit me from it with a truthful exit. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Enter me with an entrance of truth, he said: in what you sent me with of your matter, and bring me out with an exit of truth, he said likewise also. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, with a similar wording. Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: He brought me into Paradise with a truthful entrance, and He brought me out with a truthful exit, from Mecca to Medina. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, he said: Al-Hasan said: He brought me into Paradise with a truthful entrance and a truthful exit from Mecca to Medina. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He brought me into Islam with truth. Who said that? Sahl bin Musa Al-Razi told us: Ibn Numayr told us, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, My Lord, let me enter with a truthful entrance, he said: Let me enter Islam with a truthful entrance, and let me exit from it with a truthful exit. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: He brought me into Mecca in safety, and brought me out of it in safety. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid bin Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit, meaning Mecca. He entered it in safety and exited it in safety. The most correct of these sayings in interpreting this is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: And He brought me into the city with a true entrance, and He brought me out of Mecca with a true exit. We said that this is more appropriate for the interpretation of the verse, because it follows His statement, “And indeed they almost incited you from the land to expel you from it. And then they would not remain behind you except for a little.” We have previously demonstrated that He meant by that the people of Mecca. So since this was following God’s report of what the polytheists wanted to provoke the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to expel him from Mecca, it was clear, since God had expelled him from it, that His statement, And say, My Lord, let me enter a truthful entrance and let me exit a truthful exit, was a command from Him to him to desire that He expel him from the city in which the polytheists are by expelling him from it a truthful exit, and that He let him enter the city to which God had transferred him a truthful entrance. And His statement, And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority. The people of interpretation differed in their interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Grant me a supporting king who will support me against whoever opposes me, and a strength by which I will establish Your religion, and by which I will repel from him whoever intends to harm him. Who said that? Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzaie told us: Bishr bin al-Mufaddal told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of al-Hasan, regarding the words of God Almighty, And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority, He promises him that He will take away the kingdom of Persia and the glory of Persia and give it to him, and the glory of the Romans and the kingdom of the Romans and give it to him. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority, that the Prophet of God knew that he would not be able to do this without an authority, so he asked for an authority to support the Book of God Almighty, the limits of God, the obligations of God, and the establishment of the religion of God. And the authority is a mercy from God that He has placed among His servants. Were it not for that, some of them would raid others, and the strong among them would devour the weak. And others said: Rather, what he meant by that was a clear argument. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us - and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, a supporting authority, he said: A clear argument. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of those who said: This is a command from God Almighty to His Prophet to desire from Him that He grant him authority to support him against those who rebelled against him and plotted against him, and tried to prevent him from fulfilling God’s obligations regarding himself and His servants. I said that this is more correct, because it came after God informed him of what the polytheists intended to do, which was to expel him from Mecca. God Almighty informed him that if they did that, they would be punished soon. Then He commanded him to seek Him to expel him from among them, a truthful expulsion that their enemies would attempt, and to bring him into another land, a truthful entrance that their enemies and its people would attempt to bring him into it, and to give him a supporting authority over the people of the town from which its people had expelled him. He meant everyone who was similar to them. If he was given that, then he was given, without a doubt, a clear argument. As for his saying Nasir, Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we said about it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, in his statement, And grant me from Yourself a supporting authority, he said: He will support me. And God said to Moses, We will strengthen you with your brother, and We will grant you both authority, so they will not reach you with Our signs. This is presented and postponed. Rather, it is authority with Our signs, so they will not reach you.
17:81: God Almighty says: And say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who almost provoked you to leave the land to expel you from it, The truth has come and falsehood has perished. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the truth that God ordered His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to inform the polytheists that it had come, and the falsehood that He ordered him to inform them that it had perished. Some of them said: The truth is the Qur’an in this place, and falsehood is Satan. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And say, ‘The truth has come,’ he said: The truth is the Qur’an, “And falsehood has perished. Falsehood is bound to perish.” Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And say, ‘The truth has come,’ he said: the Qur’an. And falsehood has perished,’ he said: falsehood has perished, which is Satan. Others said: Rather, the truth is sufficient to fight the polytheists and falsehood is polytheism. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, And say, ‘The truth has come,’ he said: The fighting has drawn near, and falsehood has perished, he said: Polytheism and what they are in. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, entered Mecca, and around the House were three hundred and sixty idols. He began to stab them and say: “The truth has come and falsehood has perished. Falsehood is bound to perish.” The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty commanded His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, to inform the polytheists that the truth has come, and that is everything in which there is pleasure and obedience to God, and that falsehood has perished. He says: And everything in which there is no pleasure or obedience to God has gone, which is disobedience to Him and obedience to Satan. This is because the truth is everything that contradicts the obedience of Satan, and falsehood is everything that agrees with his obedience. God Almighty did not specify the report about some of his obedience, nor the disappearance of some of his disobedience, rather He knew the report about the coming of all of the truth, and the disappearance of all of falsehood. Thus came the Qur’an and revelation, and upon this the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, fought the people of polytheism with God, I mean upon establishing all of the truth, and invalidating all of falsehood. As for the Almighty’s saying, And falsehood perished, its meaning is: falsehood was lost, from their saying: his soul perished, meaning it went out and I destroyed it, and from their saying: the arrow was destroyed, meaning it went beyond the target and continued on its direction. It is said from this: falsehood perished, it perishes, and God destroyed it, meaning He made it go away. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Indeed, falsehood is bound to perish. He said: It will go away.
17:82: And the Almighty said: And We send down to you, O Muhammad, from the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers. The Almighty says: And We send down to you, O Muhammad, from the Qur'an that which is a healing by which one can be cured of ignorance and misguidance, and by which one can see from blindness for the believers and a mercy for them, not for the disbelievers in it, because the believers act according to what is in it of the obligations of God, and they make lawful what He makes lawful and forbid what He forbids, so He thereby admits them into Paradise and saves them from His punishment, so it is a mercy and a blessing from God for them, which He bestowed upon them. And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss. He says: And this that We send down to you from the Qur'an does not increase the disbelievers in it in loss, meaning: destruction, because whenever a command from God about something is sent down in it or a prohibition about something is forbidden, they disbelieve in it, so they do not obey His command, and they do not desist from what He forbade them from, so that increases their loss to what they were in before that of loss, and filth to their filth before. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And We send down of the Qur’an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers, if the believer hears it, he benefits from it, memorizes it, and remembers it. And it does not increase the wrongdoers thereby except in loss, that is, he does not benefit from it, nor memorize it, nor remember it, because God made this Qur’an a healing and a mercy for the believers.
17:83: The Blessed and Exalted says: And when We bestowed favor upon man, and saved him from the distress of what he was in at sea, and he was on the verge of destruction by the wind blowing upon him to the land, and other than that of Our favors, he turned away from mentioning Us, and he had been seeking help from Us, more than anyone else, in the state of distress in which he was. And he distanced himself means: And he distanced himself from Us, meaning himself, as if he had not called upon Us in a distress that had befallen him before that. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And he distanced himself from us, he said: He distanced himself from us. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The reading is to make the hamza in na'a before the alif, which is the eloquent language, and we read it with it. Some of the people of Madinah used to read it as wa na'a making the hamza after the alif, and this is even though it is a permissible language that came from the Arabs by bringing forward in similar words the hamza in a place where it is delayed, and delaying it in a place where it is advanced, as the poet said: Flags reduce the vision of the dreamer, so he raves about what he saw in the dream As he said, Abar is Abar, so they brought forward the hamza, so that is not the good language, but the other one is the eloquent one. And the Almighty’s saying, And when evil touches him, he is despairing. He says: And when evil and hardship touch him, he is hopeless of relief and comfort. And similar to what we said about the hopeless, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And when evil touches him, he is despairing, meaning: hopeless. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And when evil touches him, he is despairing. He said: When evil touches him, he despairs and loses hope.
17:84: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to the al-Nas 114:Each of you acts according to his own nature: according to his own direction and method. Your Lord knows best who among you is best guided to the path. He says: Your Lord knows best who among you is best guided to the path of truth than anyone else. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Everyone acts according to his own nature, meaning: according to his own side. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement: On his likeness he said: On his side. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, “Say: Each one acts according to his nature,” he said according to his nature, according to his individuality. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: “Say: Each one acts according to his own nature.” He said: According to his own way and according to what he intends. Others said: The problem is religion. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding his statement: Everyone acts according to his own nature, he said: According to his religion, the nature is the religion.
17:85: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: The disbelievers among the People of the Book ask you about the spirit, what is it? Say to them: The spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you and all the people have not been given of knowledge except a little. He mentioned that those who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the spirit, and this verse was revealed about their question to him about it, were a group of Jews. The novel mentioned that: Abu Hisham narrated: Waki` narrated: Al-A`mash narrated: Ibrahim narrated: Alqamah narrated: Abdullah said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a field in Madinah, and he had a palm branch with him that he was leaning on. He passed by some Jews. Some of them said: Ask him about the soul. Some of them said: Do not ask him. So he stood leaning on his palm branch, and I stood behind him, and I thought that revelation was being sent to him. Then he said: “And they ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” Some of them said to one another: Did we not tell you not to ask him? Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi narrated: My father narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: While I was walking with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a lava field in Medina, we passed by Jews. Some of them said: Ask him about the soul. They said: What has made you hear what you dislike? So they went to him and asked him. He went and I knew that revelation was being sent to him, so I stood where I was. Then he recited: “And they ask you about the soul. Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord. And you have been given of knowledge only a little.” They said: Did we not forbid you from asking him? Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: The People of the Book asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the spirit. God Almighty revealed: “And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about the spirit. Say, ‘The spirit is from the command of my Lord. And you have not been given of knowledge except a little.’” They said: Do you claim that we have been given of knowledge except a little, while we have been given the Torah, which is wisdom? And whoever has been given wisdom has certainly been given much good. He said: Then the verse was revealed: And if all the trees on the earth were pens, and the sea were ink, with seven more seas to replenish it, the words of God would not be exhausted. He said: What you have been given of knowledge, God saved you with it from the Fire, is abundant and good, but in the knowledge of God it is little. Ismail bin Abi Al-Mutawakkil told me: Al-Ashja’i Abu Asim Al-Himsi told us: Ishaq bin Isa Abu Ya’qub told us: Al-Qasim bin Ma’n told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a field in Medina, when a Jew came to him and said: O Abu Al-Qasim, what is the spirit? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was silent, and God Almighty revealed: “And they ask you about the spirit. Say, ‘The spirit is from the command of my Lord.’” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And they ask you about the spirit, the Jews met the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they deceived him and asked him and said: If he is a prophet who has knowledge, then he will know that, so they asked him about the spirit, and about the people of the cave, and about Dhul-Qarnayn, so God revealed all of that in His book, “And they ask you about the spirit. Say: The spirit is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little,” meaning the Jews. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And they ask you about the soul, he said: The Jews ask about it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid: And they ask you about the soul. He said: The Jews ask it. Muhammad bin Saad told us, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they ask you about the soul. That is because the Jews said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Tell us what the soul is, and how is the soul in the body tormented? The soul is from God Almighty and nothing had been revealed to him about it, so he did not tell them anything. Then Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him and said to him: “Say: The soul is from the command of my Lord, and you have not been given of knowledge except a little.” So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, informed them of that. They said to him: Who brought you this? The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: Gabriel brought it to me from God. They said: By God, none told you this except an enemy of ours. Then God, may His name be blessed, revealed: “Say: Whoever is an enemy to Gabriel - for he has brought the Qur’an down upon your heart.” Ibn Humayd told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: I was walking with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one day, and we passed by some Jews. They said: O Abu al-Qasim, what is the spirit? He remained silent. Then I saw that revelation was being sent to him. He said: So I moved away from him to a courtyard, and this verse was revealed to him: And they ask you about the spirit. The Jews said: This is how we find it with us. The interpreters differed about the spirit mentioned in this place. What is it? Some of them said: It is Gabriel, peace be upon him. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: And they ask you about the spirit. He said: It is Gabriel. Qatada said: And Ibn Abbas used to conceal it. Others said: It is an angel. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And they ask you about the spirit, he said: The spirit is an angel. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Abu Marwan Yazid bin Samra, the master of Caesarea, told us, on the authority of someone who told him, on the authority of Ali bin Abi Talib, that he said regarding His statement, And they ask you about the spirit, he said: It is an angel from the angels who has seventy thousand faces, each face has seventy thousand tongues, each tongue has seventy thousand languages. He glorifies God Almighty in all of those languages. God creates from every glorification an angel who flies with the angels until the Day of Resurrection. We have explained the meaning of the spirit in other places in our book, so there is no need to repeat it. As for his saying, From the command of my Lord, he means: It is from the matter that God Almighty knows but you do not know it, and He knows what it is. As for his statement, And you have been given of knowledge only a little, the people of interpretation differed about the meaning of his statement, And you have been given of knowledge only a little. Some of them said: He meant by that: those who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the soul and all people other than them, but when he included the non-addressee with the one being addressed, the speech came out as addressing, because the Arabs do this when the one being reported about, absent, and the one being addressed come together in the speech, they made the speech address the group. Who said that? Ibn Humayd told me: Salamah told us: Muhammad ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of some of his companions, on the authority of Ata ibn Yasar, who said: And of knowledge you have been given only a little was revealed in Mecca. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, the Jewish rabbis came to him and said: O Muhammad, have we not heard that you say: And of knowledge you have been given only a little? Do you mean us or your people? He said: No, I mean you. They said: You recite: We have been given the Torah, and in it is clarification of everything. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: It is little in the knowledge of God, and He has given you that which, if you acted upon, you would benefit. Then God revealed: And if all the trees on the earth were pens (Al-Luqman 31:10) to His saying: Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding the Almighty’s saying: And of knowledge you have been given only a little, he said: O Muhammad, and all people. Others said: Rather, he meant by that: those who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about the soul in particular, and not others. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And you have been given only a little knowledge, meaning: the Jews. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: The speech was addressed to the one to whom it was addressed, and what is meant by it is all of creation, because the knowledge of everyone except God, even if it is abundant, is little compared to God’s knowledge. Rather, the meaning of the speech is: And you, O people, have not been given of knowledge except a little of the much that God knows.
17:86: God Almighty says: And if We willed, We could surely take away what We have given you of the knowledge which We have revealed to you of this Qur’an. We could take it away, and you would not know it. Then you would not find for yourself, as to what We will do to you, a guardian, meaning: someone who would stand up for you and prevent Us from doing that to you, nor a supporter who would aid you and stand between Us and what We want with you. He said: Abdullah bin Masoud interpreted the meaning of God Almighty taking it away as His removing it from the hearts of its readers. The novel mentioned that: Abu Kuraib narrated: Abu Bakr bin Ayyash narrated to us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Rafi’, on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Muqal, who said: I said to Abdullah: And he mentioned that it flows over the Qur’an, how can that be when we have established it in our hearts and our copies of the Qur’an? He said: It flows over it at night, and nothing of it remains in a copy of the Qur’an or in the heart of a man. Then Abdullah recited: And if We will, We can surely take away that which We have revealed to you. Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Ishaq ibn Yahya told us, on the authority of Al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, he said: A red wind will blow from the direction of Ash-Sham, and not a single verse will remain in a man’s copy of the Qur’an or his heart. A man said: O Abu Abd Al-Rahman, I have collected the Qur’an. He said: Nothing of it will remain in your heart. Then Ibn Mas’ud recited: And if We will, We can surely take away that which We have revealed to you.
17:87: The Almighty says: And if We willed, We could surely take away, O Muhammad, that which We have revealed to you, but He does not will that, out of mercy from your Lord and His favor to you. Indeed, His favor upon you has been great, in His choosing you for His message, sending down to you His book, and all of His countless favors upon you.
17:88: God Almighty says: Say, O Muhammad, to those who said to you: We can produce the like of this Qur’an: If mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of it, they could never produce the like of it. Even if some of them were to each other helpers and supporters. It was mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, because of a group of Jews who argued with him about the Qur’an and asked him to bring them a verse other than it that would testify to his prophethood, because they were capable of bringing something like this Qur’an. The novel mentioned that: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit narrated to us, saying: Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Mahmoud ibn Sayhan, Umar ibn Ada, Bahri ibn Amr, Aziz ibn Abi Aziz, and Salam ibn Mishkam came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they said: Tell us, O Muhammad, what you have brought us is the truth from God Almighty, for we do not see it as being harmonious as the Torah is harmonious. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: By God, you know that it is from God and you will find it written down among you. If mankind and the jinn were to gather together to produce something like it, they would not produce it. Then he said, and they were all: Phinehas, Abdullah ibn Suriya, Kinanah ibn Abi al-Haqiq, Ashya’, Ka’b ibn Asad, Samual ibn Zayd, and Jabal ibn Amr: O Muhammad, does neither man nor jinn teach you this? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: By God, you know that it is from God. You find it written with them in the Torah and the Gospel. They said: O Muhammad, God does for His Messenger when He sends him what He wills, and He determines for him what He wants. So send down to us a book that we can read and recognize, or else we will bring you something like what you bring. So God Almighty revealed about them and what they said: “Say: If mankind and the jinn gathered in order to produce the like of this Qur’an, they could not produce the like of it, even if they were to each other assistants.” Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his saying, If mankind and the jinn gathered together, to… His saying, And if some of them were to support others, he said: Helpers. He said: He says: If the jinn came out and humans helped them, and they supported each other, they would not have produced anything like this Qur’an. And the Almighty’s saying, They will not produce the like of it, is in the nominative case, and it is an answer to his saying if, because when the Arabs answer if without, they raise what comes after it, because if is like an oath, and the answer to an oath without is in the nominative case. And sometimes it is in the accusative case because the one with which it is answered has a lam added to it, as Al-A’sha said: If you are killed after a battle, do not turn away from the blood of the people.
17:89: God Almighty says: And We have already made clear to the people in this Qur’an every example, as an argument for them with all of that, and as a reminder to them, and as a warning to the truth so that they may follow it and act upon it. But most of the people refused except to be disbelievers. He says: So most of the people refused except to deny the truth, and to reject God’s arguments and evidence.
17:90: God Almighty says: And the polytheists among your people said to you, O Muhammad, we will not believe you until you boast to us of a spring from this land of ours that gushes forth water for us. His saying a spring is derived from the saying of the speaker: the water springs: if it appears and gushes forth, it springs forth and gushes forth, and it is what springs forth. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth: meaning, until you cause springs to gush forth for us from the earth: meaning in this country of ours. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, he said: Springs. Muhammad told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, a spring he said: springs. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. The reciters differed in their reading of his statement tafjahuf burst forth. It was narrated on the authority of Ibrahim al-Nakha’i that he read hatta tafjahuf lana lightly, and his statement fathajaf al-nahr tafajaf’ir thawahiran with emphasis. This is how the reciters of the Kufians read it, so it is as if they went with their lightening of the first to the meaning: until water bursts forth for us from the earth all at once. And with their emphasis of the second to the meaning that it bursts forth in various places, time after time, if that is the bursting of rivers and not one river. The lightening in the first and emphasis in the second, according to what I mentioned from the recitation of the Kufians, is more pleasing to me because of what I mentioned of the separation of their meanings, even though the correctness of the first is not proven.
17:91: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of your people say to you, O Muhammad: We will not believe you until you bring forth for us a spring from our land that gushes with water or bubbling, or you have an orchard, which is Paradise, of palm trees and grapes, and the rivers will burst forth through it, gushing forth through this land of ours that we are in, through it, meaning: through the palm trees and vineyards, and by His saying through it, gushing forth He means between them at their roots, gushing forth because of their buildings.
17:92: The reciters differed in reading his statement kasfan, so most of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a silent seen, meaning: or the sky falls on us as you claimed, a seen, because kasfan in the speech of the Arabs is the plural of kasfa, which is the plural of a large number for the genus, just as sidra is pluralized with sidra, and tamer with tamer. It was narrated from the Arabs by hearing: Give me a piece of this garment, meaning a piece of it. It is said from it: He brought us a bathreed kasfa, meaning pieces of bread. It may be possible, if it is read like this, kasfan with a silent seen, that it is intended to refer to the source of kasf. As for kasf with a fatha on the seen, it is a plural of three to ten. It is said: one seffa, three sefs, and likewise to ten. Most of the reciters of the people of Medina and some of the Kufians read it as kasfan with a fatha on the seen meaning: the plural of one seffa from three to ten, meaning definitely: between three to ten. The more correct of the two readings in this regard, in my opinion, is the reading of the one who reads it with a silent seen, because those who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that did not intend in their question to him that it be with a known limit of certainty, rather they asked that the sky fall on them definitely, and this is also the interpretation that came from the people of interpretation. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement an eclipse he said: the entire sky. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah bin Katheer said, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, As you claimed, a fragment upon us, he said: Once, and what is in al-Rum 30:And makes it a fragment, he said: Definitely. Ibn Jurayj said: A fragment is based on the statement of God, If We will, We can cause the earth to swallow them up or cause fragments from the sky to fall upon them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or the sky will fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed. He said: That is, in pieces. Ali told us, he said: Abdullah bin Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying an eclipse means: cutting off. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told us: Muhammad bin Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Kasfan means: cutting off. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Or the sky will fall upon us in fragments, as you have claimed, meaning in pieces. God Almighty says about what the polytheists said to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Or do you bring God, O Muhammad, and the angels before you? The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of the tribe in this place. Some of them said: Its meaning is: until God and the angels come to each tribe of us, tribe by tribe, and they see them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, and the angels as tribes, he said: each tribe is separate from us. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, Or you bring God and the angels as a tribe, he said: Tribes on their own, each tribe. Others said: The meaning of this is: Or you bring God and the angels clearly so that we may meet them face to face, and see them clearly. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or you bring God and the angels face to face so that we may see them with our own eyes. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj: Or you bring God and the angels face to face so that we may see them. Some Arabists have interpreted it as meaning guarantor, from their saying: He is the tribe of so-and-so due to what so-and-so owes him and is his guarantor. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of Qatada, that it means seeing, from their saying: I met so-and-so face-to-face, and so-and-so is the tribe of so-and-so, meaning opposite him, as the poet said: We will reconcile with you until you are treated like a madman's scream that was made easy by his predecessor. It means I met her. Some of the scholars of the Arabic language from Basra used to say: If they described with the estimation of Fa’il from their saying I met and the like, they made the word of the description of the dual and the collective of the feminine and masculine into one word, like their saying: This is my tribe, and they are a tribe, and they are my tribe.
17:93: God Almighty says, informing us about the polytheists whose case we mentioned in these verses: Or will you, O Muhammad, have a house of gold? Which is the decoration. As Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Or you have a house of gold. He said: A house of gold. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement of adornment he said: of gold. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Or you have a house of gold. Gold here means gold. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Or you should have a house of gold. He said: Of gold. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Al-Thawri told us, on the authority of a man, on the authority of al-Hakam, who said: Mujahid said: We knew what Az-Zukhruf was until we saw it in the recitation of Ibn Masoud: Or you will have a house of gold. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: We did not know al-Zukhruf until we heard a verse of gold in the recitation of `Abdullah ibn Mas`ud. And his saying: or ascend into the sky means: or ascend by stairs to the sky. It was said in the sky, and he ascends to it, not in it, because the people said: or ascend by a ladder to the sky, so the word fi was inserted into the speech to indicate the meaning of the speech. It is said: I ascended by the ladder, so I ascend, ascending, ascending, as the poet said: You are the one who made me climb the stairs, tired, gray-haired and lame. And his saying, And we will not believe in your ascension, means: We will not believe you because of your ascension to heaven until you bring down to us a book, published so that we can read it, in which we are commanded to follow you and believe in you. Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, A book that we read, he said: From the Lord of the Worlds to so-and-so, with every man a scroll that he reads in the morning at his head. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, something similar, except that he said: A book that we read from the Lord of the Worlds. He also said: It will be placed at his head in the morning and he will read it. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Until you bring down to us a book that we can read: meaning a specific book in which we are commanded to follow you. And His saying, “Say: Glory be to my Lord,” the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists among your people, who say these words to you, sanctifying God from what they describe Him with, and magnifying Him from being brought to Him and His angels, or having a way to do anything that you ask of Him. Was I anything but a human messenger? He says: Am I anything but a servant of His servants from the children of Adam? So how am I able to do what you have asked of me of these matters, for only my Creator and your Creator is able to do them, and I am only a messenger conveying to you what I was sent with to you, and what you have asked me to do is in the hand of God, to whom I and you are servants, and no one else is able to do that. This speech that God informed us that He spoke to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, as mentioned, was from a group of Quraysh who gathered to debate and argue with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they spoke to him with what God informed us about them in these verses. Mentioning the names of those who debated the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the reason for which they debated him. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bakir narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: An old man from the people of Egypt, forty-some years old, narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that Utbah and Shaibah, the sons of Rabi’ah, Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, a man from Banu Abd al-Dar, Abu al-Bukhtari, the brother of Banu Asad, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib, Zama’ah ibn al-Aswad, al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, Umayyah ibn Khalaf, al-As ibn Wa’il, and Nabih and Munabbih, the sons of al-Hajjaj al-Sahmis, gathered, or whoever gathered from them, after sunset at the back of the Ka’bah. Some of them said to each other: Send to Muhammad, speak to him and argue with him until you find an excuse for him. So they sent to him: The nobles of your people have gathered to speak to you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them quickly, thinking that he had changed his mind about his affair, and he was keen on them, loving their guidance and being upset by their hardship. Until he sat with them, and they said: O Muhammad, we have been sent to you to excuse you, and by God we do not know a man from the Arabs who brought upon his people what you brought upon your people. You have cursed the fathers, and denounced the religion, and belittled dreams, and cursed the gods, and divided the community, and there is no ugly matter that I did not do between us and you. If you only came with this hadith seeking money, we will collect for you from our money until you are the richest of us. If you only seek honor among us, we will make you our leader. If you want kingship, we will make you our king. If this who brings you what he brings is a vision that you see has overcome you. They used to call the follower of the jinn: the visionary, so perhaps that is what happened, we will spend our money seeking medicine for you until we cure you of it, or excuse you. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I do not have what you say. I did not come to you with what I came to you seeking your money, nor honor among you, nor kingship over you, but God sent me to you as a messenger, and revealed to me a book, and commanded me to be a bearer of good tidings to you. And as a warner, so I conveyed to you the message of my Lord, and advised you. If you accept from me what I have brought to you, then it is your portion in this world and the Hereafter, and if you reject it from me, I will be patient for the sake of God until God judges between me and you, or as the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said. They said: O Muhammad, if you do not accept what we have offered you, then you know that there is no one among the people in a narrower land, or less wealthy, or more difficult to live than us, so ask your Lord who sent you with what He sent you with, so let him hasten these mountains that have become narrow for us, and expand our land for us, and let rivers gush forth for us in it like the rivers of Syria and Iraq, and let him send to us those of our fathers who have passed away, and let among those he sends to us be Qusayy ibn Kilab, for he was a truthful old man, so we will ask them about what you say, is it true or false? If you do what we ask you, and they believe you, then we will believe you, and we will know by that your status with God, and that He sent you as a messenger of truth as you say. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: This is not what I was sent for. I have come to you from God with what He sent me with. I have conveyed to you what I intended to convey to you. If you accept it, then it is your portion in this world and the next. If you reject it, I will be patient with God’s command until God judges between me and you. They said: If you do not do this for us, then take it for yourself. Ask your Lord to send an angel who will confirm what you say and will respond to us on your behalf. Ask Him, and let Him make for you gardens, treasures, and palaces of gold and silver, and make you independent of what we see you seeking. You stand in the markets and seek a living as we seek it, so that we may know the excellence of your position with your Lord if you are a Messenger as you claim. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to them: I will not do this. I am not the one who asks his Lord for this. I was not sent to you with this, but God sent me as a bearer of good tidings and a warner. If you accept what I have come to you with, then it is your portion in this world and the next. If you reject it, I will be patient with God’s command until God judges between me and you. They said: Then let the sky fall on us.
