Eclipse, as you claimed that if your Lord wills He will do, for we will not believe in you unless you do, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: That is up to God, if He wills He will do that to you, so they said: O Muhammad, how did your Lord know that we would sit with you, and ask you about what we asked you about, and request from you what we request, and then he would come forward to you, and teach you what you have returned to us with, and inform you what he will do with us in that since we do not accept from you what you have brought us, for it has reached us that only a man in Yamamah called Ar-Rahman is teaching you this, and by God we will never believe in Ar-Rahman, excuse us to you O Muhammad, by God we will not leave you and what you have conveyed from us until we destroy you or you destroy us. One of them said: We worship the angels, they are the daughters of God. Another of them said: We will not believe you until you bring us God and the angels before us. When they said that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rose from them, and with him rose Abdullah bin Abi Umayyah bin Al-Mughira bin Abdullah bin Amr bin Makhzum, who was his cousin, the son of Atika bint Abdul Muttalib. He said to him: O Muhammad, your people offered you what they offered you, but you did not accept it from them. Then they asked you for themselves matters, so that they might know your status with God, but you did not do that. Then they asked you to hasten the punishment with which you threaten them. By God, I will never believe you until you take a ladder to the heavens and ascend it while I watch, until you come to it and bring with you a published copy with you, with four angels who will testify that you are as you say. By God, if you did that, I would think that I would not believe you. Then he turned away from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, turned away to his family, sad and sorry for what he had missed out on from his people when they had invited him, and for what he had seen of their estrangement from him. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, left them, Abu Jahl said: O people of Quraysh, Muhammad has refused to do anything but what you see of slandering our religion, cursing our fathers, belittling our dreams, and insulting our gods. I swear by God that I will sit for him tomorrow with a stone as big as I can carry, and when he prostrates in his prayer, I will crush his head with it. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us: Ibn Ishaq told us: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, the freed slave of Zayd ibn Thabit, told us, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah, the freed slave of Ibn Abbas, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, in a similar manner, except that he said: And Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith, sons of Banu Abd Al-Dar, and Abu Al-Bukhtari ibn Hisham. Yaqub bin Ibrahim told me: Hisham told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Saeed, who said: I said to him regarding the words of God Almighty: We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth. He said: I said to him: It was revealed about Abdullah bin Abi Umayya. He said: They have claimed that.
17:94: God Almighty says: And what prevented, O Muhammad, the polytheists of your people from believing in God and in what you brought them of the truth when guidance came to them means: when the explanation came to them from God about the truth of what you are calling them to and the correctness of what you brought them, except their saying out of ignorance Did God send a human being as a messenger? The first is in the accusative case because the word prevented falls on it, and the second is in the nominative case because the verb belongs to it.
17:95: God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to those who refused to believe in you and to believe in what you brought them from Me, in denunciation of God sending a messenger from among human beings: If there were, O people, angels on the earth walking in peace, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger, because the angels are only seen by their likes from the angels, and those whom God has chosen from the children of Adam to see them, as for others, they are not able to see them, so how can He send to them messengers from the angels, and they are not able to see them while they are in the forms in which God created them, and only the messenger is sent to the humans from among them, as if there were angels on the earth walking in peace, then We sent to them a messenger whom We sent from among them an angel like them.
17:96: God Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you: Has God sent a human being as a messenger? "God is sufficient as a witness between me and you." For He is the best sufficiency and judge. "Indeed, He is ever, with His servants, Acquainted." He says: God is aware of His servants and knows their affairs and actions, who is right and wrong among them, who is guided and who is astray. "All-Seeing" of their management, policy, and disposition as He wills, and how He wills and loves. Nothing of their affairs is hidden from Him, and He will reward all of them for what they have presented when they come to Him.
17:97: God the Almighty says: And whoever God guides, O Muhammad, to believe in Him, and to believe in you and to believe in what you have brought from your Lord, then let him succeed in that, for he is the guided, rightly guided one who is on the right path, not the one whom someone else guides, for guidance is in His hand. And whoever He sends astray: He says, and whoever God sends astray from the truth, and lets him down from his right path, and does not guide him to believe in God and believe in His Messenger, then you will not find for them, O Muhammad, any guardians to support them other than God, if God wills to punish them and rescue them, And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces He says: And We will gather them at the place of Resurrection after they have been dispersed in the graves when the Hour comes on their faces, blind and dumb which is the plural of mute. By mute he means: dumb. As Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us, he said: Abd Al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and mute, he said: muteness, and deaf, which is the plural of deaf. If someone says: How did God describe these people as being gathered blind, dumb and deaf, when He said: And the criminals will see the Fire and think that they will fall into it. So He informed us that they will see, and He said: “When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its wrath and its roaring. And when they are thrown therein into a narrow place, chained together, they will cry out there for destruction.” He informed that they hear and speak. It was said: It is possible that what God described them with of blindness, dumbness and deafness will be their description when they are gathered to the place of resurrection, then He will give them hearing, sight and speech in other conditions other than the state of gathering. And it is possible that this will be, as was narrated from Ibn Abbas in the hadith that: Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf, then he said, And the criminals will see the Fire and think, and he said, They will hear its roaring and groaning, and he said, Leave there destruction. As for his statement, blind, they will not see anything that will please them. His saying, dumb, means they do not speak with an argument. His saying, deaf, means they do not hear anything that pleases them. And His saying, Their abode is Hell, means that He, the Most High, says: Their destination is Hell, and in it are their dwellings, and they are its fuel. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Their abode is Hell, means that they are its fuel. And his saying, Every time it subsides, We increase their blazing fire, means by his saying subsides: it becomes soft and calm, as Adi bin Zaid Al-Abbadi said in describing Misnah: Its middle is like a firefly or a lamppost, sometimes fading and sometimes shining What he means by his saying: The lamp fades is that it softens and weakens sometimes, and strengthens and shines at other times. From this is the saying of Al-Qatami: It fades for an hour and blows for an hour In a similar manner to what we said about this, the people of interpretation said, with their differences in the expression of its interpretation. Who said that? Ali bin Dawud told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: Whenever it subsides, he said: It becomes still. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Every time it subsides, We increase their blazing fire. He said: Every time you burn them, you ignite them with firewood. Then when you burn them and nothing of them remains, they become glowing embers. That is their extinction. Then when they are replaced with a new creation, they return to them. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Mujahid. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, similarly. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Whenever it subsides, he said: Its subsidence is that it ignites them as firewood, and when it burns them and nothing remains of them, it becomes glowing embers, and when they are replaced with a new creation, it returns to them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Every time it subsides, We increase their blazing fire, meaning: Every time their skins are burned, they are replaced with other skins, so that they may taste the torment. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding Every time it subsides, We increase their blazing fire, he said: Every time something of it softens. It was narrated on the authority of Marwan, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, Whenever it subsides, he said: it becomes still. And his statement, We will increase their blazing fire, he said: We will increase these infidels’ blazing fire, and that is the ignition of the fire upon them and its burning in them and its raging after it subsides, in their bodies.
17:98: God Almighty says: This is what We have described of what We will do to these polytheists on the Day of Resurrection, what I mentioned that We will do to them of gathering them on their faces blind, dumb and deaf and burning them in the Fire, as We have explained of their state therein, their reward for their disbelief in this world in Our signs, meaning in His proofs and arguments, and they are His messengers who called them to worship Him, and their singling Him out as divinity without idols and statues, and their saying when they are commanded to believe in the Promise and in the reward and punishment of God in the Hereafter, When we are bones worn out and dust “will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation?” They say: We will be resurrected after that as a new creation, as We began it the first time in this world, as a denunciation of that, and astonishment and amazement that this should happen.
17:99: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him: Have these polytheists who say, When we are bones and dust, will we indeed be resurrected as a new creation? not looked with the eyes of their hearts, so that they would know that God, who created the heavens and the earth, and originated them from nothing, and established them with His power, is able with that power to create their likes and their likes from creation after their annihilation and before that, and that whoever is able to do that, it is not impossible for Him to bring them back as a new creation, after they become bones and dust. And His statement, And He has appointed for them a term about which there is no doubt, God the Almighty says: And God has appointed for these polytheists a term for their destruction, and a time for their punishment about which there is no doubt. He says: There is no doubt that He will grant them that term. But the wrongdoers refused except to be ungrateful, meaning: So the disbelievers refused except to deny the truth of His threat with which He threatened them and to deny it.
17:100: God the Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists: If you, O people, possessed the treasures of my Lord’s possessions of wealth. And by mercy in this place, He means wealth. Then you would withhold it for fear of spending. He says: Then you would be stingy with it, and not give it generously to others, for fear of spending and poverty. 2732 2 - As Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: Then you would withhold it for fear of spending. He said: poverty. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Fear of spending means fear of poverty. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. And his saying, And man is ever stingy, means: And man is ever miserly and withholding. As Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And man is ever stingy, he said: miserly. Al-Qasim told us: Al-Husayn told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said, regarding His statement, And man is ever stingy, he said: miserly. 2737 2 - Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And man is ever stingy, he said: miserly, withholding. And there are four dialects for qatur in the speech of the Arabs. It is said: qatar so-and-so is stingy and niggardly, and qatar yaqtur, and aqtar yaqtur, as Abu Dawud said: I do not consider poverty as nothingness, but the loss of someone I have afflicted with death.
17:101: God Almighty says: And We gave Moses, son of Imran, nine clear signs, which made it clear to whoever saw them that they were proofs for Moses, bearing witness to his truthfulness and the reality of his prophethood. The people of interpretation differed about them and what they are. Some of them said about that: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And We gave Moses nine clear signs. He said: The nine clear signs: his hand, his staff, his tongue, the sea, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood, are detailed signs. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We gave Moses nine clear signs, the throwing down of the staff twice before Pharaoh, the pulling out of his hand, the knot that was on his tongue, and five signs in al-A’raf 7:the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. Others said something similar to this statement, except that they made two signs out of them: one of them was obliteration, and the other was the stone. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Buraidah ibn Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz asked me about his statement, And We gave Moses nine clear signs, so I said to him: They are the flood, the locusts, and the lice. And the frogs, and the blood, and the sea, and his staff, and the obliteration, and the stone. He said: What is the obliteration? I said: Moses prayed and Aaron believed. He said: Your prayer has been answered. Omar said: How can jurisprudence be anything but like this? Omar bin Abdul Aziz called for a map that belonged to Abdul Aziz bin Marwan that was found in Egypt. In it were the walnut, the egg, and the lentil, which is not unknown. They were transformed into stones that were from Pharaoh’s money that were found in Egypt. Others said something similar, except that they made two of them: one of them was the years, and the other was the decrease in fruits. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein bin Waqid told us, on the authority of Yazid al-Nahwi, on the authority of Ikrimah and Matar al-Warraq, regarding his statement, nine signs, they said: the two toucan, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the stick, the hand, the years, and a decrease in fruits. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughirah, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding his statement, Nine clear signs, he said: The flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, and the blood. And the years, and the decrease in fruits, and his staff, and his hand. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ata’ bin Abi Rabah was asked about the statement, And We gave Moses nine clear signs, what are they? He said: The flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the staff of Moses, and his hand. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said something similar to what Ata’ said, and he added: We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a loss of fruits. He said: They are the nines, and they say: The nines are the years, and the loss of the foreignness of Moses’ tongue. Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated: Abd al-Razzaq narrated: Muammar narrated: Qatada narrated: Ibn Abbas narrated: Concerning His statement, Nine clear signs, they are consecutive, And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a loss of fruits, he said: Years were for the people of the desert, and a loss of fruits for the people of the towns. So these are two signs, and the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, these are five, and the hand of Moses when he brought it out white to the onlookers without any disease: leprosy, and his staff when he threw it down, and behold, it was a clear serpent. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And We gave Moses nine clear signs, he said: Moses’ hand, his staff, the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs, the blood, the years, and a decrease in the fruits. Others said something similar, except that they made the years and the decrease in fruits one sign, and they made the ninth: The staff swallows up what they fabricate. Who said that? Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us: Al-Hasan told you, regarding His statement, Nine clear signs, “And We seized the people of Pharaoh with years of famine and a loss of fruits,” he said: This is one sign, and the flood, and the locusts, and the lice, and the frogs, and the blood, and the hand of Moses, and his staff when he threw it down and behold it was a clear serpent, and when he threw it down and behold it devoured what they were fabricating. Others said about that what Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told me: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told me: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah: I heard `Abdullah ibn Salamah narrating on the authority of Safwan ibn `Assal: A Jew said to his companion: Let us go to the Prophet so that we may ask him about this verse: And We gave Moses nine clear signs. He said: Do not say to him, Prophet, for if he hears you, he will have four eyes. So they asked, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do not associate anything with God, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not kill a soul which God has forbidden except by right, do not practice magic, do not consume usury, do not walk with an innocent person to a man of authority to kill him, and do not accuse a chaste woman, or he said: Do not flee from the battle. Shu`bah was the doubter, and you Jews are specifically required not to transgress on the Sabbath. So they kissed his hand and foot and said: We bear witness that you are a Prophet. He said: What prevents you from becoming Muslims? They said: David prayed that there would always be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that the Jews will kill us. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Sahl bin Yusuf, Abu Dawud, and Abd Al-Rahman bin Mahdi told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Amr, who said: I heard Abdullah bin Salamah narrating on the authority of Safwan bin Assal Al-Muradi, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar, except that Ibn Mahdi said: Do not walk to someone in authority. Ibn Mahdi said: I think he said: To someone innocent. Abu Kurayb narrated: Abdullah bin Idris and Abu Usamah narrated something similar, on the authority of Shu`bah bin Al-Hajjaj, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salamah, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal, who said: A Jew said to his companion: Let us go to this Prophet. His companion said: Do not say Prophet, for if he heard you he would have four eyes. He said: So they came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him about nine clear signs. He said: They are: Do not associate anything with God, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not take the life which God has forbidden except by right, do not walk with an innocent person to a person in authority to kill him, do not practice magic, do not consume usury, do not accuse a chaste woman, do not turn back on the day of battle, and you, the Jews in particular, are required not to transgress on the Sabbath. He said: So they kissed his hands and feet and said: We bear witness that you are a Prophet. He said: What prevents you from following me? They said: David prayed that there would always be a prophet among his descendants, and we fear that if we follow you, the Jews will kill us. Mujahid bin Musa told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Shu’bah bin Al-Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Salamah, on the authority of Safwan bin Assal, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. As for his saying, So ask the Children of Israel when Moses came to them, most of the reciters of Islam read it as a command, meaning: So ask, O Muhammad, the Children of Israel when Moses came to them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hasan Al-Basri in his interpretation of it: Al-Harith told me: Al-Qasim told us: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Hasan: So ask the Children of Israel. He said: Your question to them: your consideration of the Qur’an. It was narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it as ask meaning: Moses asked the Pharaoh of the Children of Israel to send them with him as a statement. Who said that? Ahmad bin Yusuf told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Harun, on the authority of Hanzala Al-Sadusi, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he recited: He asked the Children of Israel when he came to them, meaning that Moses asked Pharaoh of the Children of Israel to send them with him. The reading that I do not permit anyone to read with anything other than it is the reading that the readers of the countries follow, due to the consensus of the proof of the readers on its correctness, and their desire for what contradicts it. And his saying, And Pharaoh said to him, ‘Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you are bewitched.’ He says: So Pharaoh said to Moses: “Indeed, I think, O Moses, that you practice the science of magic. These wonders that you do are from your magic.” It may be possible that what is meant by it is that I think, O Moses, you are a magician, so the object was placed in the place of the subject, as it was said: Indeed, you are ominous and auspicious for us, but it is actually ominous and auspicious. Some of them interpreted a concealed veil to mean: a covering veil, and the Arabs often use the word maf’ul as the subject.
17:102: The reciters differed in their reading of the statement "I have known. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it as I have known" with a fat-ha on the ta', as a way of addressing Moses to Pharaoh. It was narrated from Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, in this regard, that he read "I have known" with a damma on the ta', as a way of informing Moses about himself. Whoever recites it according to this reading, then his interpretation of the statement "Indeed, I think, O Moses, you are bewitched" should be according to his school of thought. Indeed, I think that you have been bewitched, so you see that you are speaking correctly but not correctly. This is one way of interpretation. However, the reading that the reciters of the regions follow is different from it, and it is not permissible for us to contradict the evidence in what it has come with from the reading that is agreed upon. And then, God, the Most High, mentioned that Pharaoh and his people denied the nine signs that Moses brought them, even though they knew that they were from God, by His saying: “And put your hand into your bosom; it will come out white without disease, [as] nine signs to Pharaoh and his people. Indeed, they were a people of wickedness. But when Our clear signs came to them, they said, “This is obvious magic.” And they denied them, though their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance.” al-Naml 27:So God, the Most High, mentioned that they said: It is magic, even though they knew and were convinced thereof that it was from God. Likewise, His saying: Indeed, you have known is only information from Moses to Pharaoh that he knew that they were signs from God. It was mentioned from Ibn Abbas that he provided evidence for that with the same argument that we mentioned. He said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Abu Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jiyyir, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he used to recite Indeed you know O Pharaoh in the accusative case, None sent down these except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, then he recited, And they denied it, while their souls were convinced thereof, out of injustice and arrogance. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: Moses said to Pharaoh: You have certainly known, O Pharaoh, that these nine clear signs that I showed you were not sent down as proof for me of the truth of what I am calling you to, and as a witness for me of my truthfulness and the correctness of my statement. Indeed, I am a Messenger of God. None has sent me to you except the Lord of the heavens and the earth, because no one other than Him has the power to do that, nor anything like it. Insights: He means by insights: the signs, that they are insights for whoever sees them, and guidance for whoever is guided by them, by which whoever sees them knows that whoever brings them has been destroyed, and that they are from God and not from anyone else, since they are miracles that no one other than the Lord of the heavens and the earth has the power to do, nor anything of them, and it is the plural of insight. And his saying, And indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, means: Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are cursed and prevented from good. The Arabs say: What prevented you from this matter? That is, what prevented you from it, and what turned you away from it? And God made him doomed, so he is yathbiruhu and yathbiruhu, two languages, and a man who is yathbiru is: imprisoned from good deeds, doomed, and from this is the saying of the poet: If I follow Satan in his ways of error, and whoever deviates from his inclination will be doomed. And in a similar manner to what we said in interpreting that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Abdullah bin Abdullah Al-Kalabi told us: Abu Khalid Al-Ahmar told us: Omar bin Abdullah told us, on the authority of Al-Munhal bin Amr, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, he said: cursed. Abu Kuraib narrated: Marwan bin Muawiyah narrated: Umar bin Abdullah Al-Thaqafi narrated: Al-Munhal narrated: Saeed bin Jubair narrated: Ibn Abbas narrated: The same. 22756 - Ali narrated: Abdullah narrated: Muawiyah narrated: Ali narrated: Ibn Abbas narrated: His statement, Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, you are doomed, means: cursed. Others said: Rather, its meaning is: Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, you are defeated. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, meaning: defeated. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, Indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, meaning defeated. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: I think you, Pharaoh, are doomed. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: Mathburan: meaning perished. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed: meaning, destroyed. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, something similar. Others said: I think you are a changer and a modifier. Who said that? Abu Kuraib told us: Abdullah bin Musa told us, on the authority of Isa bin Musa, on the authority of Atiyah: I think, O Pharaoh, that you will be doomed. He said: Changed. Others said: It means: crazy, without a mind. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And indeed, I think, O Pharaoh, that you are doomed, he said: If a person does not have a mind, what benefit will it bring him? Meaning: If he does not have a mind that benefits him in his religion and livelihood, the Arabs call him doomed. He said: I think you do not have a mind, O Pharaoh. He said: While he was afraid of him and my tongue could not speak, I would say this to Pharaoh, but when God expanded his chest, he dared to say to him more than what God had commanded him. We have already explained what is most correct in this regard.
17:103: God Almighty says: Then Pharaoh wanted to provoke Moses and the Children of Israel from the land, So We drowned him in the sea, and those with him of his army all together, and We saved Moses and the Children of Israel, and We said to them after the destruction of Pharaoh Dwell in the land the land of Ash-Sham. So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together He says: So when the Hour comes, which is the promise of the Hereafter, We will bring you all together. He says: We will gather you from your graves to the place of resurrection all together: that is, mixed together, some of you have wrapped around others, you do not know each other, and none of you will side with his tribe or his clan, from your saying: I wrapped the armies: if you strike some of them with others, so everyone is mixed together, and likewise everything that is mixed with something has wrapped around it. The interpreters differed in their interpretation of this, and some of them said something similar to what we said.
17:104: Who said that: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Qan: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibn Abi Razin, We have brought you in droves. He said: From every people. Others said: Rather, it means: We have brought you all. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, We have brought you all together, he said: All together. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, We have brought you all together, all of them. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told me, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, So when the promise of the Hereafter comes, We will bring you all together, meaning all together, the first of you and the last of you. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, We have brought you all together, he said: All together. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, We have brought you all together, meaning all together. He made the word al-lafif singular, and it is a report on the whole, because it has the meaning of a source, like the saying of the speaker: I wrapped him up in a wrapping and a wrapping.
17:105: God the Almighty says: And with the truth We have sent down this Qur'an, meaning: We sent it down enjoining justice, fairness, good morals, and praiseworthy and commendable matters, and forbidding injustice, ugly matters, bad morals, and reprehensible actions. And with the truth it has come down, meaning: And with that it was sent down from God to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. And His statement: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And We have not sent you, O Muhammad, to those of Our servants to whom We sent you, except as a bringer of good tidings of Paradise for whoever obeys Us, and adheres to Our commands and prohibitions, and as a warner for whoever disobeys Us and opposes Our commands and prohibitions.
17:106: Or a Qur’an which We have divided into parts for you to read. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters in the countries read it as farqanahu with a light ra’ from farqanahu, meaning: We perfected it, separated it, and explained it. It was reported on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he used to read it with emphasis on the letter ra and say farqanahu meaning: We revealed it bit by bit, verse by verse, and story by story. The first reading is more correct in our view, because it is the reading upon which the evidence is unanimously agreed upon, and it is not permissible to contradict it in matters of religion and the Qur’an. If this is the more correct reading, then the interpretation of the statement is: “And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, and We have detailed it as a Qur’an, and We have made it clear and perfected it, that you may recite it to the people at intervals.” And in a similar manner to what we said about this interpretation, a group of people of interpretation said. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts, meaning: We have detailed it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Abu Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Abu bin Ka`b, that he read, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts, in a lightened form: meaning, We have explained it. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn Abbas said: And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts. He said: We have explained it in detail. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Badal Ibn Al-Muhabbir told us: Ibad told us, meaning Ibn Rashid, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he recited, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts, making it lighter: God distinguished between truth and falsehood. As for those who read the other reading, they interpreted what I mentioned of the interpretation. It was mentioned that what I narrated of the interpretation from the reader of that is the same. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu Al-`Aliyah, he said: Ibn Abbas used to recite it, and a Qur’an that was divided and heavy, saying: It was revealed verse by verse. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Yazid bin Harun told us, he said: Dawud told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: He said: The Qur’an was revealed all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree, then it was revealed after that over twenty years. He said: And they do not bring you an example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation. And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts in order that you may recite it to the people at intervals, and We have revealed it gradually. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts so that you may recite it to the people, it was not revealed in its entirety, and there were about twenty years between its beginning and its end. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts, he said: Divided into parts means He did not reveal it all. And he recited, And those who disbelieved said, ‘Why was the Qur’an not revealed to him all at once?’ until he reached and the best explanation, to refute what they bring. Some of the Arabists from Kufa used to say: The accusative of his statement and a Qur’an means: and a mercy, and he interpreted that as and We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner and a mercy, and he said: That is permissible, because the Qur’an is a mercy, and its accusative in the manner we have mentioned is more appropriate, and that is like what God Almighty said: And the moon - We have determined for it phases and his statement: that you may recite it to the people at intervals means: that you may recite it to the people at a slow pace, so that you recite it slowly and clearly, and do not rush in reciting it, lest it be understood from you. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, who said: I said to Mujahid: A man recited Surat al-Baqarah and Al Imran, and another recited Surat al-Baqarah, and their bowing and prostration are the same. Which of them is better? He said: The one who recited Surat al-Baqarah and recited And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts in order that you may recite it to the people at intervals. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, So that you may recite it to the people at intervals, meaning: with confirmation. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement with a pause he said with a measured recitation. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, his statement, So that you may recite it to the people at intervals, he said: In a measured manner. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, That you may recite it to the people at intervals, he said: The interpretation of what God said, And recite the Qur’an with measured recitation: is its interpretation. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Ath-Thawri told us, on the authority of Ubayd, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: So that you may recite it to the people slowly means to read it slowly. And in the word slow down there are different forms of the Arabic word: makth, “mukth,” mukth, and makithani with a shortened mikthana, and the reading is with a damma on the mim. And His statement, And We sent it down gradually, God Almighty says: We divided its revelation, and We sent it down little by little. Yaqub told me, he said: Ibn Ulayyah told us, he said: Abu Raja’ told us, he said: Al-Hasan recited: “And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts that you may recite it to the people over a period of time. And We have sent it down gradually.” He said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, would send down this Qur’an part by part because He knew that it would happen and would occur among the people. He told us that there were eighteen years between its beginning and its end. He said: So one day I asked him in anger, and I said: O Abu Sa’id, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts. Abu Raja’ made it heavy, so Al-Hasan said: It is not We divided it, but We divided it, so Al-Hasan recited it lightly. I said: Who tells you this, O Abu Saeed, the companions of Muhammad? He said: Who tells me? He said: It was revealed to him in Mecca eight years before he migrated to Medina, and in Medina for ten years. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And a Qur’an which We have divided into parts in order that you may recite it to the people at intervals, and We have revealed it gradually. It was not revealed in one night or two nights, nor a month or two months, nor a year or two years, but there were twenty years between its beginning and its end, and whatever God willed of that. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, he said: He used to say: The Qur’an was revealed to the Prophet of God over eight years, and ten after he emigrated. Qatada used to say: Ten in Mecca, and ten in Medina.
17:107: God the Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you, We will not believe in you, until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth: Believe in this Qur'an, which if mankind and the jinn gathered together to produce the like of it, they could not produce it, even if they were to back each other up. But do not believe in it, for your belief in it will not increase the treasures of God's mercy, nor will your abandonment of belief in it decrease that. And if you disbelieve in it, then those who were given knowledge of God and His verses before its revelation from among the believers of the People of the Two Books, when this Qur'an is recited to them, they fall on their chins in prostration to the ground in reverence and honor for it, and in knowledge from them that it is from God. The people of interpretation differed as to what is meant by His statement, fall on their chins. Some of them said: What is meant by it is the faces. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, They fall upon their chins in prostration, meaning: upon their faces. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, They fall down on their chins in prostration. He said: On their faces. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Others said: Rather, he meant beards. Who said that? Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Al-Hasan said regarding they fall to the chins he said: the beards.
17:108: And His saying, Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled. God Almighty says: And those who were given knowledge before the revelation of this Qur'an say, when they fell upon their chins in prostration upon hearing the Qur'an recited to them, sanctifying the connection between what the polytheists add to it, that the promise of our Lord of reward and punishment has been fulfilled, truly and certainly, believing in the Qur'an and confirming it. And chins in the speech of the Arabs: the plural of chin, which is the meeting of the two jaws. If that is the case, then what Al-Hasan said about that is more similar to the apparent meaning of the revelation. In a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said, with their differences, about those meant by his saying, those who were given knowledge, and in it is recited to them. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, he said: Mujahid said: Those who were given knowledge before him... to His saying in humility. He said: They are people from the People of the Book when they heard what God revealed to Muhammad “and they say, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord has been fulfilled.’” Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, “Say: Believe in it or do not believe. Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it” before the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, “when what has been revealed to them from God is recited to them, they fall upon their faces in prostration * and say, ‘Glory be to our Lord. Indeed, the promise of our Lord will be fulfilled.’” Others said: What he meant by his saying those who were given knowledge before him is the Qur’an that was revealed to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. Who said that? Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, regarding his statement, When their book is recited to them, their book. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, When it is recited to them, what God revealed to them from God. We said: What is meant by his saying when it is recited to them is the Qur’an, because in the context of mentioning the Qur’an, no other books are mentioned, so the speech is directed to it. Therefore, the ha’ in his saying before it was made from the mention of the Qur’an, because the speech mentioning it came before it, and that is his saying and a Qur’an which We have divided and what follows it in the context of reporting about it. Therefore, what we said must be correct if there is no evidence that contradicts what we said about it that must be accepted.
17:109: God Almighty says: And those who were given knowledge from among the believers of the People of the Two Books before the revelation of the Criterion, when the Qur’an is recited to them, fall down on their chins weeping, and the admonitions and lessons in the Qur’an increase their humility, meaning submission to God’s command and obedience to Him, and their submission to Him. Ahmad bin Mani’ told us: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us: Misa’ar told us, on the authority of Abdul-A’la Al-Taimi, that whoever is given knowledge that does not make him cry is likely not to have been given knowledge that benefits him, because God described the scholars, saying: Indeed, those who were given knowledge before it - when it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces... the two verses. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Misa’ar bin Kadam, on the authority of Abd Al-A’la Al-Taimi, something similar, except that he said: When it is recited to them, they fall upon their faces, then he said: And they fall upon their faces weeping... the verse. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: And they fall upon their faces weeping, and it increases them in humility. He said: This is an answer and explanation of the verse in Kaf Ha Ya Ain Sad: When the verses of the Most Gracious are recited to them, they fall down in prostration and weeping.
17:110: God the Almighty says to His Prophet: Say, O Muhammad, to the polytheists of your people who deny the supplication of the Most Gracious: Call upon God O people, or call upon the Most Gracious, whichever you call upon, He has the best names. By whatever name of His, the Most Majestic, you call upon your Lord, you are calling upon only One, and He has the best names. This was only said to him, may God bless him and grant him peace, because the polytheists, as mentioned, heard the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, calling upon his Lord: O our Lord, God, and O our Lord, the Most Gracious, so they thought that he was calling upon two gods, so He revealed this verse to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, as an argument for His Prophet against them. Mention of the narration with what we mentioned: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Muhammad ibn Katheer told me, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Waqid, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was prostrating and supplicating: O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful. The polytheists said: This one claims that he is supplicating alone, but he is supplicating in pairs. So God Almighty revealed: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, to Him belong the best names.”... the verse. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Isa told me, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Makhul, that the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was praying at night in Mecca one night, saying in his al-Sajdah 32:O Most Gracious, O Most Merciful. A polytheist heard him, and when morning came he said to his companions: “Look at what Ibn Abi Kabsha said. He is calling tonight upon the Most Gracious who is in Yamamah.” And there was a man in Yamamah called the Most Gracious, so the verse was revealed: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, He has the best names.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his saying: “Say: Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, to Him belong the best names.” Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement Whatever you call upon is one of His names. Musa bin Sahl told me, he said: Muhammad bin Bakkar Al-Basri told us, he said: Hammad bin Isa told us, on the authority of Ubaid bin Al-Tufayl Al-Juhani, he said: Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of Abdul Aziz bin Umar bin Abdul Aziz, on the authority of Makhul, on the authority of Arak bin Malik, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: God has ninety-nine names, all of which are in the Qur’an. Whoever counts them will enter Paradise. Abu Ja`far said that the inclusion of what in his statement, Whichever you call upon, has two aspects: One of them is that it is a connection, as was said: In a little while they will become regretful. The other is that it is in the meaning of if, and it was repeated because their wording differed, as was said: I have never seen a night like the night. His statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. The people of interpretation differed regarding prayer. Some of them said: What is meant by that is: Do not recite your supplication aloud, nor in a low voice, but rather in a way between that. And they said: What is meant by prayer in this context is supplication. Who said that? Yahya bin Isa Al-Damaghani told me: Ibn Al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwa, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, she said: In supplication. Bashar told us: Hisham bin Urwa told us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: It was revealed regarding supplication. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Hisham ibn Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, the same. Al-Hasan bin Arafa told us: Ibad bin Al-Awam told us, on the authority of Ash’ath bin Suwar, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: They used to recite their supplication aloud, but when this verse was revealed, they were commanded not to recite aloud, nor in a low voice. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Malik al-Bakri, on the authority of Abu al-Juza’, on the authority of Aisha, who said: It was revealed regarding supplication. Matarbin Muhammad Al-Dhabi told me, he said: Abdullah bin Dawud told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Ziyadah bin Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Supplication. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Hijri, on the authority of Abu Ayyadh, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: It was revealed regarding supplication. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sharik told us, on the authority of Ziyadah ibn Fayyad, on the authority of Abu Ayyad, the same. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us on the authority of someone who mentioned it on the authority of Ata’, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. He said: It was revealed regarding supplication. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the verse: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. He said: In supplication. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, he said: It was revealed regarding supplication. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice in supplication and asking. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: It was revealed regarding supplication and asking. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Yahya told us, he said: Sufyan told us, he said: Qais bin Muslim told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: In supplication. Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Ayyash al-Amiri, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: Whenever the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, greeted the Prophet, they would say: O God, grant us camels and children. He said: Then this verse was revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: In supplication. Ibn Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And do not recite your prayer aloud... the verse, he said: In supplication and asking. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hussein told us, he said: Isa told me, on the authority of Al-Awza’i, on the authority of Makhul: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: Is that in supplication? Others said: He meant prayer by that. The proponents of this statement differed regarding the meaning intended by the prohibition of reciting it aloud. Some of them said: What is meant by reciting it aloud is recitation. Who said that? Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: This verse was revealed while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was hidden: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: When he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an, and when the polytheists heard that, they would curse the Qur’an, the one who revealed it, and the one who brought it. He said: So God said to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: And do not recite your prayer aloud, lest the polytheists hear it, and do not recite it in a low voice from your companions, so do not let them hear the Qur’an until they learn from you. Abu Kuraib told us, he said: Uthman bin Saeed told us, he said: Bishr bin Ammar told us, on the authority of Abu Rawq, On the authority of Ad-Dahhak, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an aloud in prayer with the Muslims, this would be difficult for the polytheists if they heard him, so they would harm the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, by cursing and criticizing him. This was in Mecca, so God revealed: O Muhammad, Do not recite your prayer aloud, meaning: Do not recite the Qur’an aloud loudly so that the polytheists hear it and harm you, and do not recite the Qur’an in a low voice, meaning: Do not lower your voice so that your ears cannot hear. And seek a way between that, meaning: Seek a way between recitation aloud and loud, and between recitation in a low voice and low voice, neither loudly nor in a low voice so that your ears cannot hear. That was the measure. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, migrated to Medina, all of this was dropped, and now he can do whichever of those things he wants. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak saying: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice... the verse. This was when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Mecca, when he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice in recitation so that the polytheists could hear him, and they would harm him. So God commanded him not to raise his voice so that his enemy could hear, nor to recite so low that the Muslims behind him could not hear. So God commanded him to seek a way in between. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise his voice when reciting the Qur’an, and when the polytheists heard his voice, they would curse the Qur’an and whoever brought it. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would whisper the Qur’an so that his companions could not hear him. Then God revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. Muhammad bin Ali bin Al-Hasan bin Shaqiq told us: I heard my father say: Abu Hamza told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far bin Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his voice and the polytheists heard him, they would curse the Qur’an and the one who brought it. But when he lowered his voice, his companions would not hear him. God said: And seek a way between the two. Abu Kuraib narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Dawud ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited the Qur’an aloud while he was praying, they would disperse and refuse to listen to him. So when a man wanted to listen to some of what the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was reciting while he was praying, he would eavesdrop on them out of fear of them. If he saw that they knew that he was listening, he would go away for fear of harming them, and he would not listen. If the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, lowered his voice, those who were listening would not hear anything of his recitation. So God revealed to him: And do not recite your prayer aloud lest they disperse from you. And do not recite it in a low voice so that those who wanted to hear it would hear it, who would eavesdrop on it without them, perhaps he would be alerted to some of what he heard and benefit from it. And seek a way between that. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to recite the Qur’an aloud in the Sacred Mosque. The Quraysh said: Do not recite aloud, lest you offend our gods and insult your Lord! So God revealed: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice… Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, he said: Bishr told us, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, he said: It was revealed to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while he was hiding in Mecca. When he prayed with his companions, he would raise his voice with the Qur’an. When the polytheists heard him, they would curse the Qur’an, the One who revealed it, and the One who brought it. So God said to His Prophet, And do not recite your prayer aloud, meaning your recitation, lest the polytheists hear and curse the Qur’an. And do not recite it in a low voice from your companions, so that they do not hear him. And seek a way between that. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Iyas, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: In recitation. Ibn Bashar told us: Muhammad ibn Ja`far told us: Sa`id told us, on the authority of Abu Bishr, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding this verse: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice. He said: When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, raised his voice, his companions were amazed by it, and when the polytheists heard that, they would curse him, so this verse was revealed. Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Salamah, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I was told that when Abu Bakr prayed and recited, he would lower his voice, and that Umar would raise his voice. It was said to Abu Bakr: Why do you do this? He said: I am conversing with my Lord, and He knows my need. It was said: Well done. It was said to Umar: Why do you do this? He said: I drive away Satan and wake up the sleepy. It was said: Well done. So when the verse, And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between the two, was revealed, it was said to Abu Bakr: Raise your voice a little, and it was said to Umar: Lower your voice a little. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Hassan bin Ibrahim told us, on the authority of Ibrahim al-Sayegh, on the authority of Ata’, regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Some people say that it is in prayer, and others say that it is in supplication. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. And when the Prophet of God was in Mecca, when the polytheists heard his voice, they would accuse him of every evil, so God commanded him to lower his voice, and to make his prayer between himself and his Lord, and it was said: What your ear hears is not fear. Al-Hasan bin Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Muammar told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would raise his voice in prayer, and he would be accused of impurity, so he said: Do not raise your voice so that you cause harm, and do not recite it in a low voice, but seek a way between the two. Others said: What is meant by that is: Do not recite the testimony of faith in your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. Who said that? Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs bin Ghayath told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, who said: This verse was revealed regarding the testimony of faith: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. Abu Al-Sa’ib told me: Hafs told us, on the authority of Ash’ath, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, similarly. And he added to it: The Bedouin would recite aloud, saying: All compliments are for God, and all prayers are for God, raising his voice, so And do not recite your prayer aloud was revealed. Others said: Rather, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to pray in Mecca out loud, so he ordered it to be concealed. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and Al-Hasan Al-Basri, who said: He said regarding the Children of Israel: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, prayed, he would recite his prayer aloud, and this bothered the polytheists in Mecca, until he and his companions concealed their prayers. For this reason he said: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that. And he said in al-A’raf 7:And remember your Lord within yourself in humility and fear, without being loud in speech, in the mornings and the evenings, and do not be among the heedless. Others said: The meaning of this is: Do not recite your prayer aloud, as you would improve it by performing it in public, and do not recite it in a low voice, as you would improve it in private. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he used to say: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice: meaning, do not show off in public, nor hide it in secret, but seek a way between that. Al-Hasan told us, he said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, he said: Muammar told us, he said: Al-Hasan used to say regarding His statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Do not do it well in public, and do it badly in private. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Do not show off in public, and do not recite it in secret. Ali bin Al-Hassan Al-Azraqi told me: Al-Ashja’i told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Al-Hassan: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice. He said: Do good in public, but do bad in private. Ali told me, he said: Abdullah told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice, he said: Do not pray to show off to people and do not abandon it out of fear. Others said about that what: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said about His statement: And do not recite your prayer aloud, nor in a low voice, but seek a way between that, he said: The way between that is what Gabriel prescribed for the Muslims in the prayer. He said: The People of the Book used to recite in a low voice, then one of them would recite the letter aloud, and he would shout it out, and they would shout it out behind him, so he forbade shouting as these people shout, and speaking in a low voice as the people fear, then there was the way between that which Gabriel prescribed for the prayer. The first and most correct of the sayings on this matter is what we mentioned on the authority of Ibn Abbas in the report narrated by Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, because that is the most correct of the chains of transmission that have been narrated on the authority of a companion in which there is a statement. And the most similar of the sayings to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is that His statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice comes after His statement, “Say, ‘Call upon God or call upon the Most Gracious. Whichever [name] you call upon, to Him belong the best names.’” And after rebuking the disbelievers for their disbelief in the Qur’an, and that is because of their distance from it and from faith. So if that is the case, then what is more appropriate and similar to His statement, And do not recite your prayer aloud or in a low voice is that it is due to the reason for what is in its context of speech, unless it comes with a meaning that requires it to be diverted from it, or there is evidence for its diversion from it that indicates diversion from what is in its context. If that is the case, then the interpretation of the statement is: Say, Call upon God, or call upon the Most Gracious, whichever you call upon, He has the best names. And do not, O Muhammad, recite aloud in your prayer, or in your supplication to your Lord in it, or in your asking of Him, or in your remembrance in it, lest the polytheists harm you with your loud recitation. And do not recite in a low voice, lest your companions hear it. And seek a way between that. Rather, seek a way between loudness and low recitation, so that you may hear your companions, and the polytheists may not hear it and harm you. And if the statements of the people of interpretation had not gone with what I mentioned from them of interpretation, and we do not permit disagreement with them in what came from them, then a possible interpretation would have been to say: And do not recite aloud your prayer which We have commanded you to recite in a low tone, which is the daytime prayer because it is mute and is not recited aloud, and do not recite in a low tone your prayer which We have commanded you to recite aloud, which is the night prayer because it is recited aloud, and seek a way between that by reciting aloud what We have commanded you to recite aloud, and in a low tone what We have commanded you to recite in a low tone, do not recite all of it aloud, nor in a low tone for all of it, so that would have been a possible interpretation not far from correctness, but we do not see it as correct due to the consensus of the proof from the people of interpretation to the contrary. If someone says: What is this recitation that is between the loud and the low tone? It was said: Matar bin Muhammad told me, he said: Qutaybah and Wahb bin Jarir told us, they said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Al-Ash’ath bin Salim, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, he said: Abdullah said: He did not fear the one who made his ears hear. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of al-Ash’ath, on the authority of al-Aswad ibn Hilal, on the authority of Abdullah, the same.
17:111: The Most High mentioned to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And say, O Muhammad, ‘Praise be to God, who has not taken a son,’ so he would be a servant, not a lord, because the Lord of lords should not have a son. And He has no partner in the kingdom, so he would be helpless and in need of the help of others, weak. He who is in need of a helper for what he has tried, and is not alone in the kingdom and authority, And He has no protector from humiliation, meaning: He has no ally who has allied with him from the humiliation that is in him, because he who is in need of the help of others is humiliated and disgraced, and he who is humiliated and disgraced and submits to a helper is not a god who is obeyed. And glorify Him with all glorification, meaning: And magnify your Lord, O Muhammad, with what We have commanded you to magnify Him with in word and deed, and obey Him in what He has commanded you and forbidden you. And in the same way as we said in his saying: And he had no protector from humiliation, said the commentators. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, all on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And he had no protector from humiliation, he said: He did not oppose anyone, nor did he seek anyone’s support. Al-Qasim told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Hajjaj told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to teach his family this verse: “Praise be to God, who has not taken a son and has no partner in dominion and has no protector out of weakness. And glorify Him with all glorification,” the young among his family and the old. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Hakam told us, he said: Abu al-Junayd told us, on the authority of Ja`far, on the authority of Sa`id, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The entire Torah is in fifteen verses from the Children of Israel, then he recited: Do not make with God another god. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Abu Sakhr told me, on the authority of Al-Qurazi, that he used to say regarding this verse: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son... the verse. He said: The Jews and Christians said: God has taken a son. The Arabs said: At your service, at your service, you have no partner except a partner who is yours. The Sabians and the Magians said: Were it not for the allies of God, God would have been humiliated. So God revealed: “And say: Praise be to God, who has not taken a son and has no partner in dominion and has no protector out of humiliation. And glorify Him, O Muhammad, as they say.”
